News.title: Desperate search for missing boy after he got into difficulty swimming at popular beach as emergency crews rush to scene
News.content:
SEA SEARCH Desperate search for missing boy after he got into difficulty swimming at popular beach as emergency crews rush to scene

A DESPERATE search is underway for a boy, 13, who has gone missing after getting into difficulty in the sea.

Emergency crews have rushed to a beach off the coast of Hornsea, East Yorkshire, this evening to try and find the boy.

It was reported that the boy vanished in the sea, sparking a large scale search for him.

Cops have deployed special search teams and high-tech drones to scour the water.





Authorities have shared an urgent plea to the public to stay clear of the area, let rescue teams work, and avoid online speculation.

Enquiries are ongoing to piece together exactly what happened.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation is asked to contact police right away.

Chief Superintendent Phil Booker, of Humberside Police, said: “After receiving the report, officers were immediately deployed alongside other emergency services and upon attending, it was discovered that a 13-year-old boy had reportedly got into difficulty whilst swimming in the water.



“Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors (POLSA), along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him.

“We would urge people to please avoid the area where possible to allow emergency services to work efficiently and safely, and refrain from speculating on the circumstances of the incident.

“Our enquiries continue to ascertain the full circumstances around the report, and we would ask anyone with any information that may assist us.”

Cops have urged people to speak to the officers in Hornsea if you have any information.



Or contact them via their non-emergency number 101 quoting log 415 of 4 August.

More to follow… For the latest news on this story keep checking back at The Sun Online

News.title: Fuming cops vow to drag Burnham to court if he fails to halt PC Harper’s killers’ release as they say ‘we will not stop’
News.content:
PM Andy Burnham faces being taken to court by furious cops for failing to halt the early release of two of hero PC Andrew Harper’s killers.

A Police Federation chief revealed they are poised to take legal action unless Mr Burnham reverses the decision.



Thames Valley chair Aileen O’Connor called the ruling “an insult to Andrew’s family, friends and colleagues” and said “Andy Burnham may be on his holidays but we won’t rest on this.”

PC Harper’s family are understood to be backing the move.



A petition to stop his killers being let out passed 100,000 verified signatures.

The Government has given the green light for thousands of killers, thugs and paedophiles to leave jail.



It means two of PC Harper’s killers — Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole — will be eligible for release within months.

Mr Burnham had raised hopes he could block the move but decided prisons are too full to exclude manslaughter from the scheme.

Ms O’Connor, of Thames Valley Police Federation, said the decision was a betrayal of PC Harper’s legacy.

He died trying to stop then-teen quad bike thieves Bowers, Cole and Henry Long in Berkshire on August 15, 2019.



Writing in The Sun, she challenges the PM and Justice Secretary Alex Norris to stand before PC Harper’s widow Lissie and his family “and explain why those responsible for killing a police officer should be eligible for early release”.

She adds: “Try telling the officers who attended the scene where Andrew died and witnessed the horrific consequences of that crime.”

She also told LBC News: “I will throw everything I can at this through a proper legal challenge from KCs, barristers, you name it. I will do what



“I have to do to protect Andrew Harper’s legacy and further victims who don’t have a platform to come on national radio or TV to put across their point.

“There are silent victims here in the families of individuals who have been killed who will also be outraged at this.”

A petition launched by Ms O’Connor passed 100,000 verified signatures on Tuesday evening.

It demands Mr Burnham and Mr Norris “explain why those responsible” for the killing should be eligible for release.

After 100,000 signatures, petitions are considered for debate in Parliament.



Ms O’Connor added online: “This decision pours salt into wounds that have never healed.

“It is an insult to Andrew’s family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family.”

Mr Norris made a personal call to PC Harper’s mum Debbie Adlam explaining that the decision was made due to prison overcrowding.



But Ms Adlam said her family were “bitterly disappointed”.

She added: “I don’t feel like we should be in this position. It’s not somewhere we would expect to be.

“We really feel we should have more support than this and, you know, Andrew deserves better than this and so do we.

“I think from our perspective we need to know that people are going to be keeping in touch and letting us know what’s going on.”

The Sentencing Act was passed in January.



It means offenders on standard fixed sentences and due to be released after half their term will now leave after a third.

But violent offenders who would have been freed at two thirds of a sentence will now be out after half.

Mr Norris told Sky News: “Were we not to make these changes, then we would run out of prison places in October or November.”



“I know that’s difficult. I know that’s created harm, and it’s not Lissie Harper’s fault, and I’m sorry that she’s been put into this situation as a result.”

The Prison Governors’ Association said the late changes to policy had put “huge pressure” on staff which could make mistakes “more likely”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ministers are also under pressure to send back more than 10,000 foreign criminals.

Tory Shadow Justice Secretary Nick Timothy urged the repeal of human rights laws that prevent them being returned.

News.title: Andy Burnham should follow my plan to solve Britain’s prison crisis – build, rent, remove
News.content:
LAST week I held a press conference with a group of women who had suffered horrific sexual violence and had received a letter saying that the Government was going to release their rapists and abusers early.

It was a powerful moment and one that really brought home the horror of Labour’s early release scheme.



So, while I welcome Andy Burnham’s U-turn, it’s disgraceful it took the victims and the Conservative Party raising the issue to force the new Prime Minister’s hand.

But it’s still not enough.



Killers, including two of the men involved in the death of PC Andrew Harper, are still eligible for release.

It doesn’t have to be like this.

In 14 years of Conservative government, we never let rapists, paedophiles and killers out early.

In fact, we made sure any early release was after two-thirds of a sentence.

Labour have lowered that to just one third!

Britain’s prisons are overcrowded.



But the Government needs to look at our plan to build, rent, remove.

Build more prisons, rent jail spaces abroad and remove foreign criminals back to their home countries.

The Conservative Party is the party of common sense.

That means keeping the most dangerous and disgusting criminals behind bars and the law-abiding public safe.

News.title: Devastated dad breaks silence as disturbing online searches of mom-grandma duo who poisoned 4 kids to death are revealed
News.content:
THE heartbroken father of four children fatally poisoned by their mom and grandmother has described the murders as a ‘horrendous, spiteful act’ as chilling new details have been revealed.

Police revealed on Tuesday that Sarah Myers, 44, and her mother, Amy Steadman, 64, carefully plotted the killings in the hours before taking their own lives.



After a press conference, the children’s father, Brady Harmon, told The U.S. Sun that he cannot comprehend the “sick” and “sadistic” actions investigators say led to the deaths of his children.

The young victims – 10-year-old twins Gavin and Gracelynn, 11-year-old Hudson, and 13-year-old Harper – were found dead alongside Steadman and Myers in the grandmother’s apartment in Mechanicville, New York, on June 23.





Police claimed the mom and grandmother gave the children a cocktail of drugs in an attempt to poison them before one of them stabbed Gavin with a knife.

They allegedly killed the kids in an attempt to stop Harmon from spending the summer with them.

Investigators found a heartbreaking message from Gracelynn who was in pain and asked for help from the killer duo – who ignored her desperate plea as she battled through severe stomach pain.

They carried out the murders before taking their own lives on June 10 and the six decomposing bodies were found days later after a neighbor called for a welfare check.



Harmon exclusively told The U.S. Sun, “I cannot understand what would go through those sick, sadistic, twisted minds to carry out this horrendous, spiteful act on harming my children because I have access to them for 60 days.

“You stab Gavin. Gracelynn is trying to communicate and say, ‘I need help,’ and you guys give them nothing.

“Just more pain. More fear. That’s a father’s worst fear.”

He previously said he had spent years fighting to rebuild a relationship with his children and was days away from finally bringing them to Utah for a court-approved 60-day summer visit.

According to investigators, text messages between Myers and Steadman showed they planned to poison the children between 10:30 am and noon, hours before Myers was due to have a scheduled call with Harmon.



But when the children did not succumb to the deadly plan as quickly as expected, one of the women sent a chilling message, “It’s not working, we need another option.”

Police said internet searches recovered from Steadman’s phone included medication reactions and the effects of insulin on non-diabetics.

Later chilling searches included, “Where’s the most fatal place to be stabbed” and “Find the carotid artery in the neck.”



One of the most haunting pieces of evidence released by police was a text allegedly sent by Gracelynn after becoming ill, reading: “Why would you do that? You both won’t let me puke.”

Later that evening, Steadman sent a further haunting message to Myers claiming, “Gracie is aware.”

Investigators believe Gavin survived the poisoning attempt and was then stabbed to death with a knife, with police saying he suffered defensive wounds.

Authorities also recovered a handwritten note in which Steadman claimed the killings were intended to “protect” the children from Harmon ahead of his court-ordered parenting time.

Myers also made allegations of abuse against Harmon, which he has denied.



Police said they found no evidence supporting the allegations made against him and he has never been charged.

The couple had been involved in a custody dispute but had reached an agreement that allowed Harmon to spend the summer with the children.

He previously told The U.S. Sun that his last FaceTime call with the kids was on June 7, when he said they appeared happy.

Harmon said that when he tried to contact Myers again days later, she told him the children were sick and they would speak the following day — but he never heard from them again.

Weeks after losing his four children, Harmon said the pain remains overwhelming.



“Even over a month later, it’s still not easier,” he said.

“And I don’t think it ever will be.”

Referencing the abuse allegations, he claimed there was no evidence and branded Myers a “narcissist.”

He added, “I didn’t do anything.”

Harmon, who has an older daughter from a previous relationship and has since remarried, also pointed to previous concerns raised about Myers’ care of the children.



Records reviewed by CBS affiliate WRGB CBS 6 Albany showed child welfare officials investigated Myers multiple times between 2020 and 2024, with some cases resulting in findings of inadequate guardianship and educational neglect.

There is no indication that CPS found grounds to remove the children from Myers’ care.

CPS are yet to comment on the case, Mechanicville Police Chief William Rabbit said on Tuesday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The police investigation remains ongoing as authorities continue reviewing evidence and await toxicology reports.

Following their deaths, Harmon spread their ashes on top of a mountain in Utah during a private funeral with his family.

News.title: Tragedy as gardener who died in large fire in picturesque town is pictured as his son pays touching tribute
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BLAZE HEARTBREAK Tragedy as gardener who died in large fire in picturesque town is pictured as his son pays touching tribute

A GARDENER has tragically died after a major fire broke out while he was working in the backyard of a home.

Francis Owens, who was in his 70s and from the picturesque town of Chipping Campden in the Cotswolds, has been described as a “much loved” father in a touching tribute from his son.



Emergency services rushed to Berrington Road and Castle Gardens at around 5.40pm on Monday.

Fields behind the road had caught fire and grew into a “large” blaze.



Gloucestershire Fire and Rescue Service used 13 fire engines to tackle the inferno.

Sadly, Gloucestershire Police have confirmed that Francis died at the scene.

There has been no reports of any “third party involvement in the death”.

Nathaniel Hooton, the deputy chief fire officer, said crews from Hereford and Worcester Fire and Rescue Service and Warwickshire Fire and Rescue Service had supported their efforts the extinguish the fire.

He said they “worked extremely hard to bring the fire under control”.

Francis’ son, Patrick Owens, shared his heartbreak in a touching tribute to his father on Facebook.



He said: “You were The Renaissance Man of Chipping Campden, and The Cotswolds & The Luddite of Our Generation.”

“You were and are still very much loved, especially Mum, your beautiful wife Mandy Owens .

“It’s been a tough night but we are just now sitting down and listening to Chipping Campden’s morning Chorus, of all The Beautiful Bird Song which Mum and you loved so very much at this time of morning.

“Love you, Dad. I promise I will look after Mum, I promise – until you both meet again.”

Francis, known locally as Jesse, had attended the local grammar school when he was younger.



On his website, the gardener said he gave up a “yuppy” career to work with his hands.

Jesse said he mixed “a passion for hard physical labour with a healthy questioning of modern big-tech and validating a slowing world being fun, good and necessary”.

News.title: Disgraced paedo Huw Edwards blasted after entering poetry contest under false name & calling himself a ‘wayward son’
News.content:
PAEDOPHILE Huw Edwards has been blasted for entering a poetry contest under a false name and calling himself a “wayward son”.

The ex-BBC presenter competed in Wales’s largest cultural festival using the pseudonym Y Gelyn, meaning The Enemy.



Edwards, convicted in 2024 over 41 child abuse images and videos of boys as young as seven, penned a tribute to his late dad and talked about “our dark condition”.

He would have scooped a £750 prize for winning the National Eisteddfod’s Crown contest — but his effort fell short.



Actress Sera Cracroft, who has spoken of being a child abuse victim, said: “I’m very disappointed he’s done that so soon after being convicted of creating paedophilia online.

“It’s far too soon for him to try and redeem himself”.



She said it would have been “catastrophic” if Edwards, 64, had won.

A victim of Edwards, who was sent inappropriate messages by him at the BBC, added: “Has this man no shame? After everything he has done he should just disappear.”

Reform UK MP Sarah Pochin said by taking part, even anonymously, Edwards had shown a total lack of self-awareness and gross insensitivity.

She added: “Rather than trying to resurrect his career, his time would better spent reflecting on his dreadful crimes.”



Edwards’ effort is said to have opened with the words: “A wayward son, in the torment of his hell.”

In 2024 when he got a six-month suspended jail term and was put on the sex offenders’ register for seven years, it was said his relationship with his dad caused him mental pain.

The National Eisteddfod said all entries are anonymous, adding: “Nobody, including the judges, know beforehand who has competed.”

News.title: Brexit, the BBC, moaning Sussexes and ‘black hole of badness’ Starmer – Rod Liddle’s most cutting takedowns
News.content:
PUCKISHLY profound… A master of the written word… An inimitable journalistic force who was the true voice of common sense.

These were just a few of the tributes to legendary Sun columnist Rod Liddle following the announcement on Monday of his death at the age of 66 after a short illness in hospital.



The fearless, working-class writer, who grew up in the North East, joined us 15 years ago and was known as a defender of the downtrodden.

Whether it was woke culture or political leaders, razor-sharp Rod rightly skewered the lot.

Now, in memory and tribute, we share some of his most hilarious observations.



ON KEIR STARMER

WHAT do you think our Prime Minister, Sir Keir Starmer, got for Christmas? Yes, I hear you. “A personality”. I can see him unwrapping it . . .

“Well, it’s very nice, thank you, but what do I do with it?”.

THE question, then, is whether Sir Keir is a singularity, a black hole of perceived badness, surpassing everything bad that went before it.

EVERYONE seems to be agreed that Sir Keir Starmer is the most useless Prime Minister since the title was invented. I wouldn’t disagree with that.



ON BORIS JOHNSON

HE seemed “refreshing” for a politician, a kind of village idiot waving around a pig’s bladder on a stick but somehow conversant in Latin.

ON KYLIE

GIVE it up, Kylie, you dingo. You seem to be a nice woman. You were on Vicar Of Dibley once – so why not retire now with good grace? We should be so lucky.

ON LILY ALLEN

ANOTHER gobbet of self-referential, breast-beating respec’ me bro sputum against a backdrop of the usual over-produced R&B pop schlock’



ON ENGLISHNESS

THE best thing about being English is not being French. Or Belgian. Can you imagine that? Waking up every morning to the realisation that you’re Belgian? You’d go out of your mind.

ON THE NORTH-SOUTH DIVIDE

TO the London media elite, the North of England is a dark, mythical realm populated entirely by coal miners, pigeon fanciers and people who eat tripe.

LONDON columnists write about the North with the same wide-eyed, patronising fascination that 19th-century Victorian explorers used when describing uncontacted tribes in the Amazon.

ON LOVE ISLAND

IT offers us a glimpse into a terrifying, brain-dead dystopia where conversation consists entirely of three-word sentences and heavy sighs.



ON TONY BLAIR’S ‘PHILANTHROPIST OF THE YEAR’ AWARD

NOT only has he destabilised the Middle East, he’s also pocketed vast amounts from Asian dictators who he advises on how to clean up their image. I assume “philanthropist” is a politer way of saying, “See you next Tuesday.”

ON BREXIT

IF you listen to the Remain campaign, the moment we leave the European Union, locusts will cover the land, the rivers will turn to blood and, worst of all, the supply of prosecco will dry up entirely.

TO hear the BBC talk about the European Union, you would think it was a cross between Mother Teresa and the local parish council, rather than a corrupt, unelected, empire-building monstrosity that can’t even get its own accounts audited.

ON VIRTUE-SIGNALLING

IT’S the luxury good of the modern middle classes. It costs them absolutely nothing to display, imposes heavy costs on everyone else and makes them feel immensely good about themselves while changing nothing whatsoever.

CORPORATE virtue-signalling is simply capitalism wearing a rainbow badge. It allows massive multinationals to underpay their staff and dodge their taxes while pretending to be morally superior because they changed their social media avatar for a month.



ON NIGEL FARAGE

FOR the Tories, Nigel Farage is not just a rival politician; he is an inescapable recurring nightmare. Just when they think they have buried him, he pops back up like a pantomime villain with a cigarette in one hand and half their voter base in the other.

WHILE every other politician was being coached by PR consultants on how to look relatable, Nigel just stood there holding a beer, grinning like a man who had just won twenty quid on a scratchcard.

ON LIZ TRUSS

LIZ TRUSS and Kwasi Kwarteng went into the economy like two toddlers who had escaped from nursery with a pair of rusty hedge trimmers, wildly slashing away at anything that looked remotely like economic stability.

ON PUBLIC TRANSPORT

YOU pay the price of a small holiday in Tuscany for a ticket, only to spend three hours standing next to a broken toilet in a vestibule while an automated voice apologises for a delay caused by “leaves on the track” in May.”



ON X FACTOR

AS anyone who’s ever watched The X Factor knows, really bad singers are terrifically entertaining.

ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES

I LOOK forward to the sight of [King] Charles, on horseback, leading a battalion against Xi Jinping’s People’s Army to try to take the site of China’s latest coal-fired power station.

ON CHINA

I WAS thrilled to learn that our government intends to enjoy an “open” relationship with China — one of my favourite countries, as I am sure it is yours.

ON THE WEATHER

WE used to call 25 degrees in July “summer”. Now the Met Office issues a red “extreme heat” warning, tells everyone to stay indoors with a damp flannel over their faces and treats a warm afternoon in Sussex as if it were a tactical nuclear strike.



ON JUST STOP OIL & ECO PROTESTERS

IT requires absolutely zero sacrifice . . . It is purely a therapeutic lifestyle choice designed to allow affluent urbanites to feel morally superior to people who actually have to drive to work.

IF it were up to me I would advance towards them in a steamroller. Glued your arse to the road, have you? Well you won’t be needing it much longer.

ON JEFF BEZOS

THE Washington Post adopted the grand slogan “Democracy Dies in Darkness” right around the time it was purchased by Jeff Bezos, a man who built an empire where warehouse workers are monitored by algorithms so they don’t spend too long in the toilet.

ON ELON MUSK

THERE is something magnificently absurd about these multi- billionaires who have conquered every financial frontier on Earth and now feel compelled to build giant rocket ships shaped suspiciously like phallic symbols just to escape the rest of us for eleven minutes.

ON BURKAS

THEY believe it is in accordance with their religion, and they do so happily and proudly. There are lots of things that people wear which make me cringe. Fat toffs wearing pink corduroy trousers. Chavs wearing onesies. Kids dressed like gangsters in gold chains. But I don’t think we should BAN them.



ON SELF-DEPRECATION

UNTIL now, the worst case of buyer’s remorse I have ever seen was my mum and dad. Not when they had me.

ON COVID

ONE of the exciting events you may have missed this week was the appearance of the First Minister for Wales before the Covid inquiry . . . If only you’d have known, you’d have got some friends round, opened a few beers and settled down to watch Mark Drakeford talking 50 shades of s**t.

ON ­MILLWALL FC

THERE was something about the atmosphere. Perhaps it was the bloke who tried to brick the ref that did it for me, I can’t remember. Or the fella who chased Derek Dougan around the pitch.

ON GRETA THUNBERG

“YOU have stolen my dreams and my childhood with your empty words” is perhaps the whitest thing anyone has ever said at the UN. What is the correct answer? Is it (a) Go to your room? Or is it (b) Forgive me, to make it up to you, Daddy and I are going to set the entire course of human civilisation on a new track?



ON BOB GELDOF’S LIVE AID 30

ANYONE listening to the BBC this week could be forgiven for thinking that the musician Bob Geldof had just emerged from Africa, like a latter-day Dr Livingstone, the first Westerner with news of a deadly new virus. He and his makeshift band of celebrities have adopted Ebola, their song blazing from the radio while Geldof himself has been in every studio exhorting people, with his usual stream of expletives, to . . .

ON GARY LINEKER

IN a parallel universe, where the beautiful game is unknown, Gary Lineker is a popular Leicester costermonger, a job to which his charm, conversational skills and intellectual hinterland are well suited.

ON JONATHAN ROSS

JONATHAN ROSS is paid millions of pounds a year by the BBC to act like an arrogant, spoiled schoolboy who believes he is utterly immune to the standard rules of decency.

ON TAYLOR SWIFT

FORGIVE me. I did not see the monster she would become. The morphing, over nine years, into a hideous colossus, a purveyor of ever more derivative and anodyne Kardashian pop.



ON ROY KEANE’S INJURY LAY-OFF

ALMOST half of the season will have elapsed before he can return to punch, kick and maul people. And I assume he will be so incapacitated in the meantime that we will be spared his pungent views, too. This is a national tragedy.

ON THE SUSSEXES

IN a very modern twist on the old “Never explain, never complain” mantra of the Windsors, “Always complain, always explain why everyone except you is such a horrid bully” became the Sussex strap line.”

THE Groom of the Stool was the most intimate of an English monarch’s courtiers, responsible for assisting in excretion . . . But I do remember thinking, “Oh – so that’s what a Groom of the Stool looks like,” on first seeing a photograph of Omid Scobie.

ON AMY NUTTALL

‘She has now issued her cheating husband Andrew Buchan a seven-point plan designed to rescue their marriage. Interesting. Nowhere does it say, ‘Don’t shag anyone else’. That’s an omission’



ON THE BBC

THE BBC’s idea of diversity is hiring people of every ethnic background, gender identity and sexual orientation under the sun – provided they all went to Oxbridge, read English Lit, live in North London and hold precisely the same political views.

THE BBC licence fee is the only tax in the country where you are threatened with a criminal record and a prison sentence if you refuse to pay for a product you don’t even want, produced by people who actively despise you.

IF the BBC were forced to go on to a voluntary subscription model tomorrow, half its audience would cancel before lunchtime and the rest would only keep it so they could watch the snooker.

ON SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS

THE name under which these women collectively labour is “influencer”, a term which, like “content creator”, is close to meaningless and both could be usefully replaced by “s**tgibbon” or “unemployable”.



AN influencer is simply someone with a smartphone, a staggering level of self-absorption and the breathtaking audacity to ask a restaurant owner for a free three-course meal in exchange for posting a picture of a dessert to three thousand bot accounts in Rostov.

ON ANDREW MOUNTBATTEN-WINDSOR

“IN the annals of public relations disasters, Prince Andrew’s television appearance sits somewhere above the captain of the Titanic announcing that the iceberg was actually very small and mostly made of ice cream.”

“HE sits in Royal Lodge, surrounded by his teddy bears, wondering why no one is inviting him to cut ribbons at a bypass opening in Slough.”

ON EMMA WATSON



INSTEAD of telling them all the rules of Quidditch or how to turn someone into a frog, she bored them [The UN] all rigid with whining, leftie, PC crap.

ON DIANE ABBOTT

I LIKE Diane Abbott about as much as I like getting out of bed in the middle of the night, standing on a piece of Lego and smashing my head into the door.

She’s not exactly my cup of tea, y’know?

And she has said some wonderfully stupid things in her time. But . . . she speaks her mind. She clearly cares.

News.title: Hornsea missing boy live: Huge rescue operation as teen vanishes off Yorkshire coast
News.content:
HM Coastguard is involved in the massive search operation off the Yorkshire coast

A huge rescue operation is under way after a 13-year-old boy went missing while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast - this is a breaking story

A huge search is under way after a 13-year-old boy went missing after going swimming off the East Yorkshire coast.

Emergency services were called to Hornsea at about 6pm after reports that the boy had got into difficulty in the water.

Emergency crews, including Hornsea Inshore Rescue, HM Coastguard and Humberside Police, are involved in the search. The RNLI said its Bridlington all-weather lifeboat has been launched.

Chief Superintendent Phil Booker said: "Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors, along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him."

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

That includes compulsory water safety lessons in schools, a nationwide public awareness campaign, better lifesaving equipment at high-risk waterways, the introduction of Sam's Law, and a dedicated Minister for Water Safety. Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.content:
UK weather maps show Brits to bake in new heatwave as 14 counties set for 35C+ temperatures - see full list

The latest WXCharts maps show temperatures will gradually climb across southern and eastern England, with many areas forecast to reach at least 30C in the coming days

View 3 Images Weather maps are red - because it is getting hotter (Image: WXCHARTS)

These striking weather maps show the UK is soon set to swelter in temperatures of up to 36C.

‌



Forecasters say temperatures will slowly climb and, by Wednesday August 12, much of the country will be sweltering in the heat again. The warmest counties will be those in the south and east of England, including Cambridgeshire and Norfolk.

‌



The latest WXCharts maps are, in most, a bright red, which indicates temperatures will be hot. Meteorologists at Metdesk, which issued the maps, say the mercury could peak at 36C on or around Wednesday August 12.

‌



But, during this period, temperatures are widely expected to exceed 30C, including across parts of the Midlands and northern England. Scotland and Northern Ireland are expected to remain noticeably cooler, with many areas forecast to stay in the low to mid-20s.

While it will be warmest in the east, it will still be dry and sunny across Wales — albeit cooler here too. Forecasters believe it will be 26C or 27C in and around Swansea, for instance.

View 3 Images People have fun at a beach in Folkestone, Kent (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



As the Express reports, it was warm on Monday with a 33.5C high recorded by the Met Office in Wisley, Surrey. However, rain is expected on Wednesday and Thuirsday, heaviest across Northern Ireland and parts of Scotland.

A yellow weather warning is in place for thunderstorms across Angus, Perth and Kinross, Aberdeen, Aberdeenshire, Moray and Highland. The Met Office says: " Slow-moving heavy showers and thunderstorms may cause some disruption."

List of counties set for 35C+ highs next week

According to the WXCharts, temperatures of 35C or above could soon be reached across parts of:

‌



Bedfordshire

Berkshire

Buckinghamshire

Cambridgeshire

Essex

Hampshire

Hertfordshire

Leicestershire

Kent

Northamptonshire

Oxfordshire

Surrey

Sussex

Suffolk

‌



View 3 Images Edgbaston Reservoir in Birmingham is near depleted following the hot weather (Image: Getty Images)

The heatwaves have, though, led to warnings that shoppers face higher food prices and possible shortages because of the prolonged drought.

Tom Bradshaw, president of the National Farmers’ Union, called on ministers to help support the building of reservoirs on farms as part of wider measures. He said: “Water security is food security and food security is part of our national security."

Article continues below

Parched conditions have caused havoc for farmers. Many arable farmers have been forced to bring forward their wheat harvest by several weeks - in some cases the earliest for at least 20 years - because of the extreme weather, with an impact on yields - the amount produced.

News.title: UK housebuilder falls into administration as customers hear homes left unfinished
News.content:
UK housebuilder falls into administration as customers hear homes left unfinished

Hood Property Cardrona Limited, based in Scotland, has plunged into administration and may now have to sell its land near Peebles in the Scottish Borders

View 2 Images A Scottish housebuilding company has entered administration (Image: Getty Images)

A UK housebuilder has fallen into administration, reportedly leaving homes unfinished and debts of over £4 million.

‌



Scottish company Hood Property Cardrona Limited has gone under and may now be forced to sell its land near the town of Peebles in the Scottish Borders, according to The Herald.

‌



Administrators said they had to "forcibly gain entry" to the closed site for 20 homes, where offers had already been accepted on "several" properties.

‌



However, more funding would have been needed "to finish building the properties and complete the development", administrators said in an update.

James Stephen and Kerry Bailey of BDO have been appointed joint administrators and have extended the administration period until September, reports the Express.

‌



View 2 Images The administrators said a sale 'will be completed in the next few weeks' (Image: Getty Images)

When is the solar eclipse 2026 in UK and how to watch safely - complete guide READ MORE :

UK travel company plunges into liquidation as customers issued vital update READ MORE :

They said: "Upon appointment, my staff together with our appointed security agent visited the company's development site at Cardrona next to the town of Peebles in the Scottish Borders.

"Nobody was present at the site and they therefore required to forcibly gain entry to enable an initial assessment of the site to be carried out and new security measures to be put in place."

Article continues below

A sale is "now proceeding and we anticipate it will be completed in the next few weeks", they added.

HMRC has submitted a claim for £4,684, and a further £300,000 is owed to creditors, though it has not yet been confirmed whether this will be paid. The administrators warned: "It is anticipated that a dividend will not be paid to unsecured creditors."

News.title: 'Nigel Farage created the £250,000 by-election chaos — so he should answer for every penny spent'
News.content:
'Nigel Farage created the £250,000 by-election chaos — so he should answer for every penny spent'

Nigel Farage decided to quit as MP for Clacton-on-Sea, Essex, last month and now stands in a by-election there on Thursday, a stunt said to cost the taxpayer £250,000

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Nigel Farage has dumped the country with a £250,000 by-election bill for a stunt that reeks of vanity, evasion and contempt for taxpayers. He quit his seat only to stand again after rivals accused him of dodging scrutiny over a £5million gift from a Thai-based crypto billionaire.

‌



The result is a democratic farce: a near metre-long ballot paper, a record 34 candidates, Count Binface among them, and Tendring Council forced to spend scarce money on extraordinary arrangements. Farage never stops preaching about waste, bloated government and respect for the public purse.

‌



Yet when his own career is on the line, he is happy to burn through taxpayers’ cash without blinking. Clacton deserves a serious MP, not another circus built around one man’s ego.

‌



His party’s supposed crusade against waste looks utterly fraudulent. Farage called this election. He created the chaos. He should answer for every penny spent and explain why local people must pay for his latest exercise in self-preservation.

Hit banks with windfall tax

Together, HSBC, Lloyds, Barclays and NatWest raked in more than £29 billion in six months while families are hammered by mortgage costs, energy bills and high prices.

‌



Their profits have been swollen by interest rates staying higher for longer. The banks did not cause the crisis, but benefited handsomely from it. Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey should use the autumn Budget to impose a windfall tax on excess profits.

This levy would take a share of earnings made in exceptional circumstances while leaving banks with billions. The money could cut energy bills and support the NHS, schools, social care and councils. Taxpayers rescued the banks when they were in trouble. Now, families need help, ministers must make them return the favour.

Keep your cool with your fridge

Amid the heatwaves, Britain has lost the plot over the fridge. Apples, nuts and potatoes should apparently chill out, while chocolate, tomatoes and coffee belong outside.

Article continues below

Every kitchen has now become a rather chilly game of chance. That is the cold, hard truth.

News.title: Tuscany rocked by 'strong' earthquake as people flee buildings in Pisa and Lucca
News.content:
Tuscany rocked by 'strong' earthquake as people flee buildings in Pisa and Lucca

A 'strong' 4.3-magnitude earthquake struck near Pisa on Monday morning, with its epicentre just four miles from Italy's historic Tuscan city

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A "strong" 4.3-magnitude earthquake has rocked the Italian region of Tuscany - with its epicentre just four miles from the historic city of Pisa.

‌



The quake was felt at around 10.15am local time across northern Tuscany, including the provinces of Lucca, Pisa and Massa-Carrara.

‌



The epicentre was near San Piero a Grado, around seven kilometres from Pisa, at a shallow depth of around eight kilometres, according to Italy’s National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV).

‌



The relatively shallow depth contributed to the tremor being felt widely across northern Tuscany.

Tuscany regional governor Eugenio Giani wrote on social media: "Checks are currently under way with the regional emergency system. The strong earthquake was felt throughout northern Tuscany."

View 2 Images The Leaning Tower of Pisa and the Pisa Cathedral remained open to visitors (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A second tremor followed at 1.04pm, with the Italian National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology (INGV) recording a 3.2-magnitude earthquake. The epicentre was around five kilometres from Pisa, at a depth of 11 kilometres.

Bernard Dika, undersecretary to the presidency of the Tuscany region, wrote on social media after the first quake: "Hundreds of calls have been made to the regional emergency number 112 following the strong earthquake recorded in Pisa, with many people taking to the streets.

"At the moment, there are no reports of injuries. Some precautionary evacuations are under way in the area."

‌



Three families were evacuated from a building in San Giuliano Terme, near Pisa, according to local newspaper Corriere Fiorentino. The earthquake caused structural instability at the property, requiring further inspections by firefighters. The evacuation was carried out as a precaution.

No injuries or other significant damage to buildings have been reported. In Pisa, firefighters received numerous calls following the earthquake, which prompted residents to leave their homes and gather in the streets as a precaution, Italian media reported.

Court hearings at the local courthouse were suspended, and the city hall was also evacuated as a safety measure. After inspections were completed, residents and employees were allowed to return to the buildings.

Article continues below

Rail services on the Pisa-Empoli, Pisa-Livorno, Pisa-Lucca and Pisa-Viareggio lines were suspended for around four hours - until 3.30pm local time - to allow technical checks on the infrastructure, according to Corriere Fiorentino.

The Leaning Tower of Pisa and other museums and monuments in Piazza dei Miracoli were not affected by the earthquake and remain open to visitors.

News.title: Shark sighting closes St Ouen's Bay beach on Jersey for the first time
News.content:
Shark sighting closes St Ouen's Bay beach on Jersey for the first time

Beachgoers were told to leave the water after a suspected shark was spotted at St Ouen's Bay, Jersey - days after a species usually found in the Mediterranean washed up in the area

View 2 Images Lifeguards evacuated the beach at Ouen's Bay, Jersey (file photo) (Image: Getty Images/imageBROKER RF)

Lifeguards evacuated a British beach after a large shark was spotted patrolling the waters.

‌



RNLI lifeguards used loudspeakers to tell people to get out of the water at St Ouen's Bay, Jersey after multiple sightings of the creature in the water on Saturday morning. It was described as dark grey and about 10ft to 12ft (3m to 3.6m) long.

‌



One local lifeguard said it was the first time in history that Jersey has closed the beach for a shark sighting - and it's one of only a handful of times this has happened in the entire British Isles.

‌



Great white shark weighing 100 STONE spotted off Florida tourist beach showing unusual behaviour READ MORE :

View 2 Images Jersey recently recorded its first ever sand tiger shark (file photo) (Image: ullstein bild via Getty Images)

Lifeguard Tom Rolls said he could barely believe what he was hearing when the alarm was raised by a colleague further down the coast.

He told the Jersey Evening Post: "We got the call through from one of the guards at Watersplash [beach bar], and he basically said that a shark had been spotted in the lineup.

‌



"Initially, we were like, ‘that’s a joke, you’re having us on here’. But then he was persistent. He said multiple sightings had been seen by members of the public."

Red flags were flown and a PA system was used to tell people to get out of the water, before the beach reopened around an hour later. No injuries were reported.

In June, a 4.3-metre-long (14ft) smalltooth sand tiger shark washed up on Grève d'Azette beach in Jersey, about seven miles from the location of the most recent sighting.

‌



The shark was showing faint signs of life when it was first discovered stranded in a shallow tidal pool.

Responders from British Divers Marine Life Rescue (BDMLR), Jersey Coastguard, and Marine Resources attempted to revive it, but the animal died shortly after.

Sand tiger sharks are usually found in tropical and subtropical waters, such as the Mediterranean.

Article continues below

Previous beach evacuations sparked by shark sightings

In August 2021, a stretch of water off Boscombe and Bournemouth beaches in Dorset was temporarily cleared by RNLI lifeguards after daytrippers reported of a "large marine animal" in the water. Experts said the incident was likely triggered by harmless basking shark.

And in July 2012, surfers and swimmers were evacuated from Croyde Bay in Devon after a member of the public spotted a large fin in the water offshore.

RNLI lifeguards advised people to leave the water as a precaution as the fin - also believed to be from a basking shark - appeared inside a designated safe swimming zone.

News.title: When is the solar eclipse 2026 in UK and how to watch safely  - complete guide
News.content:
When is the solar eclipse 2026 in UK and how to watch safely - complete guide

The most dramatic solar eclipse visible from the UK since 1999 will take place on August 12, with Cornwall, Devon, Somerset and Bristol offering some of the best viewing spots

This is what a solar eclipse looks like from space

The most dramatic solar eclipse visible from the UK since 1999 is now just days away.

‌



On August 12, the Moon will pass directly between the Sun and the Earth, blocking some or all of the Sun's light from reaching our planet.

‌



Across much of Europe, including the UK and Ireland, skygazers will be treated to an impressive partial solar eclipse, with around 90 per cent of the Sun covered by the Moon in many locations.

‌



Meanwhile, a total solar eclipse - where the Moon completely covers the Sun - will be visible along a narrow path crossing Greenland, Iceland, Spain, northern Russia and a small area of northern Portugal. It will be the first time in more than a century that mainland Spain has experienced a total solar eclipse.

The UK and Ireland will see their deepest solar eclipse since August 11, 1999, when a total eclipse was visible from most of Cornwall and Devon.

View 3 Images The eclipse will reach its maximum at around 7.12pm in London on August 12 (Image: Josh Edelson/Getty Images)

‌



What is a solar eclipse and how often does it happen?

A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon moves directly between the Sun and the Earth.

During an eclipse, the Earth is in the Moon's shadow. Because the Moon is much smaller than the Earth, its shadow only covers a small area of the Earth's surface, meaning a solar eclipse is visible only from certain parts of the planet.

‌



There are usually between two and five solar eclipses each year. A total solar eclipse occurs somewhere on Earth roughly every 18 months.

Which parts of the world will see a total and partial solar eclipse on August 12?

A total solar eclipse will be visible from parts of Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, Spain and north-east Portugal.

A partial solar eclipse will be visible across much of Europe, parts of Africa, North America, the Atlantic Ocean, the Arctic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean.

‌



What time is the solar eclipse - and where's the best place in the UK to see it?

The exact timings will vary depending on location.

In London, Bristol and Cardiff, the eclipse will begin at around 6.17pm, reach its maximum at around 7.12pm and finish at around 8.06pm, according to Royal Museums Greenwich. Viewers in London will see roughly 90 per cent of the Sun covered by the Moon.

Timings for other locations in the UK can be seen in the table below:

‌



View 3 Images (Image: Royal Museums Greenwich)

According to the Royal Observatory Greenwich, the best places in the UK to see the most dramatic eclipse coverage will be in the south-west of the country.

Cornwall will experience around 95 per cent coverage, while Pembrokeshire in south-west Wales will see around 94 per cent, the observatory says.

‌



Those able to travel to the south-west tip of Ireland will see some of the highest coverage anywhere in the British Isles, with almost 97.5 per cent of the Sun obscured by the Moon.

Which parts of the world will not see the solar eclipse?

Although millions of people will be able to watch the eclipse, large parts of the world will miss it.

Most of South America, southern Africa, Australia, New Zealand and much of Asia will not see the event because the eclipse will occur during nighttime hours or while the Sun is below the horizon.

‌



Those unable to view it in person will still be able to watch online, with the European Space Agency hosting a live webcast from Spain's Astrophysical Observatory of Javalambre, alongside a public celebration in León. NASA will also provide coverage, as will the Italy-based Virtual Telescope Project and others.

Is it safe to look at a solar eclipse with sunglasses?

No. Ordinary sunglasses do not provide adequate protection for viewing a solar eclipse, as they do not block the levels of solar radiation that can reach and damage the retina.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has warned that the Sun may appear less bright than usual during an eclipse, making it easier to look at it directly. However, harmful levels of sunlight can still reach the retina and cause damage - often without any immediate signs or discomfort.

‌



The Royal College of Ophthalmologists reported around 70 cases of people experiencing vision problems after viewing the 1999 total solar eclipse. Around 40 per cent of those affected had observed it for less than a minute.

View 3 Images People planning to watch the solar eclipse should make sure they wear genuine eclipse glasses (Image: Colin Davey/Getty Images)

How can I watch the solar eclipse safely then?

The UKHSA recommends two safe ways to view a solar eclipse: using specialist eclipse viewers or using indirect viewing methods.

Article continues below

Those planning to use eclipse glasses or handheld solar viewers should ensure that they are genuine eclipse glasses fitted with specially designed filters that meet the international safety standard ISO 12312-2:2015(E).

Genuine eclipse glasses are available from reputable retailers, including Royal Museums Greenwich. Eclipse glasses should not be used if the lenses are scratched, torn or damaged.

Another safe method is to use a simple pinhole projector. A small hole made in a piece of card can project an image of the Sun onto a surface, allowing the eclipse to be viewed without looking directly at the Sun.

News.title: Teen dies after being 'raped by three men in car before stumbling into traffic'
News.content:
Teen dies after being 'raped by three men in car before stumbling into traffic'

Madison Brooks was a student at Louisiana State University when she was allegedly attacked - now one of the men alleged to have assaulted her is due to stand trial

View 2 Images Madison Brooks lost her life after she was allegedly gang raped (Image: Instagram)

A 19-year-old Louisiana State University cheerleader died after she was allegedly gang raped by three men in the backseat of a car.

Madison Brooks was allegedly dumped out of the vehicle before stumbling across a highway where she was fatally struck by a truck in 2023. Now the trial of Desmond Carter, 21, one of the men who allegedly assaulted Brooks, is set to begin with the hearing scheduled for August 17.

Carter has been charged with rape alongside Kaivon Washington and Casen Carver. Prosecutors allege that the men assaulted Brooks in a car after they drank together at a bar. The men deny raping Brooks, saying they had consensual sex with her.

Footage showed Brooks stumbling into moving traffic. Authorities say the teen's blood-alcohol level was .319%, almost four times the legal driving limit. She walked into the four-lane road where she was hit by the truck, the Mirror US reports.

View 2 Images Desmond Carter is now facing trial (Image: East Baton Rouge Sherriff's Office)

In court filings last year, attorneys for Carver and Carter claimed that the injuries consistent with sexual assault allegedly found on Brooks' body were not their doing. They claimed that Brooks had consensual sex with another LSU student the night before, which caused her injuries.

A motion claimed the evidence "will gut the State's theory of the case" and prove their innocence. The filing was condemned by the prosecution, including District Attorney Hillar Moore, who called it "totally inappropriate and not in accordance with the applicable rules of law." The motion was later rejected by a judge, who deemed it "irrelevant."

Carter's attorneys have filed a motion to prohibit Brooks' supporters from wearing the teen's favourite colour in the courtroom, arguing that it could intimidate the jury.

Article continues below

The Brooks family and their supporters have been wearing pink to commemorate the late student at public events and court hearings.

The defence referenced multiple cases that determined a "carnival atmosphere" in courtrooms has infringed upon a defendant's right to a fair trial. This argument has been characterized as a "gross mischaracterization of the facts at hand" by prosecutors, according to WBRZ.

News.title: Afghan boxer arrested in Greece over discovery of Scottish woman's body in suitcase
News.content:
The man suspected of killing Scottish aid worker Elisabeth Jane Ross in Greece is 26-year-old Sharif Ahmadzai, the BBC understands.

He was arrested after the body of the 38-year-old was found in a suitcase in an abandoned building in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, several days after she was reported missing.

Ahmadzai, who was born in Afghanistan and is a champion boxer, settled in Greece after travelling there as a teenager.

Both Ross and Ahmadzai had worked with refugees and Greek police are investigating whether the pair knew each other through the charity sector.

Ahmadzai was arrested on suspicion of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences, and is expected to appear in court in Athens on Wednesday.

Police said the coroner's initial report failed to determine a cause of death, but more detailed examinations concluded it was an "obvious criminal act, likely asphyxiation".

News.title: Infantino calls executive meeting as criticism mounts
News.content:
Gianni Infantino has summoned senior leaders of football's world governing body to a meeting in Morocco on Wednesday, after another day in which its president has faced fierce criticism of his plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations.

Fifa's chief of global football development Arsene Wenger, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, and Prince Ali, president of the Jordanian Football Association, all made clear their opposition to Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise.

Infantino, who has been in Morocco over the past week, called an executive meeting in Rabat as he attempts to find a solution to the controversy.

Wenger said in a statement issued through Fifa that scrapping the plan was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

Grafstrom called the last week "a sad and reproachable series of events" in an internal email to Fifa staff.

Prince Ali, meanwhile, accused Fifa of creating a situation which "amounts to blackmail" over unpaid prize money and support for Infantino's re-election.

Wenger has been in a role which encompasses data analysis of the game, Fifa's online training and youth competitions, since 2019.

The former Arsenal boss previously supported Infantino's proposal to play the men's World Cup every two years.

A week after Infantino's investment plan was first released, the Frenchman issued a statement through Fifa in which he demanded "transparency and integrity" from the body.

"The recent events at Fifa deserve some clarity from my side," Wenger's statement read.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Wenger is one of 18 Fifa officials named in a document preservation letter Uefa sent to Fifa threatening legal action.

Carlos Cordeiro - Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance - is the only Fifa official to resign over the scandal, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future".

News.title: Princess Eugenie gives birth to baby girl in Portugal
News.content:
Princess Eugenie has given birth to a baby girl at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

The baby was born on Monday at 18:20 BST, weighing 6lbs 9oz.

This is Princess Eugenie's third child with her husband, Jack Brooksbank, following the births of her sons August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, who was born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, who was born in 2023.

A statement from Buckingham Palace read: "Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news."

In a post on Instagram, the princess, 36, wrote: "Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

"We are beyond in love with our girlie."

They are yet to announce a name.

The new arrival - who will not be an HRH - will be 15th in line to the throne, moving ahead of their great-uncle the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Edward.

The couple live between Portugal and Ivy Cottage, in the grounds of Kensington Palace.

They announced Princess Eugenie's pregnancy in May. She posted a photograph of her young sons holding a baby scan with the caption: "Baby Brooksbank due 2026!"

The Palace said on social media at the time: "His Majesty The King has been informed and is delighted with the news."

News.title: Major search under way for boy, 13, missing at sea
News.content:
A major search is under way for a 13-year-old boy who reportedly got into difficulty while swimming off the East Yorkshire coast, police have said.

Emergency services were called to Hornsea at about 18:00 BST.

Crews, including Hornsea Inshore Rescue, HM Coastguard and Humberside Police, remain at the scene. The RNLI said its Bridlington all-weather lifeboat joined the search.

Ch Supt Phil Booker said: "Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors, along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him."

News.title: Bono, Eddie Vedder and Hozier among mourners at Glen Hansard's funeral
News.content:
Stars from the world of music including U2's Bono, Pearl Jam's lead singer Eddie Vedder, and Hozier, attended the funeral of Glen Hansard on Tuesday.

The 56-year-old Oscar-winning Irish singer and songwriter died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin last week.

Hansard, who shot to prominence in 1991 musical comedy film The Commitments, was long-time frontman of acclaimed rock band The Frames.

News of his sudden death shocked the music world and fans alike, with tributes being paid from the likes of Ed Sheeran and Bruce Springsteen, who said he was "heartbroken".

News.title: Athletes go 'missing' after Commonwealth Games ends
News.content:
Several athletes have disappeared after competing in the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, failing to return home with the rest of their teams.

Police Scotland said it had received reports of various athletes "unaccounted for" in the aftermath of the Games, which concluded on Sunday.

The sports website NBS Sport, external said four members of the Ugandan boxing squad had not turned up to fly home, adding that one member of the team had told the website the athletes intended to seek asylum in Scotland.

Pakistan Today also reported, external that the boxer Qudratullah had not joined the rest of his team mates in flying home to Pakistan, and that he was not found in his room when officials went to search for him.

News.title: Care company fined for running illegal children's homes in legal first
News.content:
A care company has been prosecuted and fined for running illegal children's homes in what has been called the first case of its kind.

Catalyst Care Limited is the first unregistered children's homes provider to be successfully prosecuted, according to Ofsted, which brought the legal action against it.

Its directors pleaded guilty at Croydon Magistrates' Court in relation to failing to register children's homes and have been fined a total of Â£92,400.

The Croydon company operated three homes in Kent between 2022-2025 which accommodated up to nine children. During this time the homes received over Â£1.7m million in payments from local authorities.

Ofsted said this was despite it repeatedly warning directors they were breaking the law.

All children's homes in England must register with Ofsted, and managing a home without a registration is a criminal offence.

The directors, Miriam Ekhator and Davidson Lynch-Shyllon, were disqualified from carrying on and/or managing or having a financial interest in a children's home.

They were also ordered to pay victim surcharges totalling Â£2,960, and costs of Â£17,250.

Musa Raji, on behalf of Catalyst Care Limited, said the defendants' "focus was on the children in front of them and sadly not on the paperwork", and they "made mistakes, but did not act out of malice or greed".

The prosecution said unregistered children's homes operate without oversight, meaning children who are placed there have no assurance of "safe or suitable care".

Ofsted say in such homes there are no guaranteed checks on staff or living conditions and there is no accountability when things go wrong.

But according to the regulator, the lack of available places in legitimate settings has led to a shadow market of illegal care homes.

News.title: Justice secretary apologises to families affected by early release scheme
News.content:
Justice Secretary Alex Norris has apologised to families affected by the early release scheme, saying they were "carrying the can from previous failures".

Families, including a man whose pregnant partner died after being hit by a speeding driver, criticised the prisoner early release scheme, saying it comes "at the expense of victims".

Andy Burnham announced that prisoners convicted of rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales. The prime minister said he wanted to exclude more, but prison overcrowding prevented this.

Calvin Buckley said he was "shocked and disappointed" the killer of his partner and unborn child could be released early.

The mother of PC Andrew Harper also said she was "devastated" to learn two men jailed after her son was killed will still be eligible.

The prime minister said making more prisoners exempt was not possible without the prison system collapsing and putting the public "at much greater risk".

Justice Secretary Alex Norris also warned a prison capacity crisis would be likely if fewer prisoners were allowed early release.

Norris later said he spoke to the families as "it is really important to express that this shouldn't be where it is".

He also said he was confident the prisons would have adequate room now that about 1,000 extra prisoners will not be released early.

"We have modelled it very carefully," he said.

PC Harper, 28, was killed in 2019 when he was dragged by a car down a country road as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

His family previously said they had received a letter from the Ministry of Justice confirming that two of the offenders could be included in the early release scheme.

While the driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and would not be eligible, Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter could apply for early release after serving half of their sentences.

The Sentencing Act was amended in January, with the eligibility for early release based on the length of fixed sentence, rather than the type of offence.

The act already excluded some of the most serious and dangerous offenders, such as murderers serving life sentences or those on extended sentences.

But last month the prime minister promised to "review the policy" and paused the scheme after a backlash from survivors.

Announcing the changes on Monday, he said: "I fully understand the anger, anxiety and distress that's been caused. I've heard that loud and clear."

But PC Harper's mother Debbie Adlam, told BBC Newsnight: "It feels like we're letting Andrew down again" to hear his killers might still be eligible for release.

"We've been through the justice system, we thought we'd done as best as we could.

"Now we're standing up to fight again... so I just feel really let down, for Andrew's sake as well as ours."

She added that Norris had called her to explain the situation and apologise.

Later, on BBC Breakfast, Adlam called for more support from the probation service, stressing: "I need to know at the very, very least if they are going to be released that we're kept in mind of what's happening and we are informed".

Other families have also criticised the early release scheme.

Calvin Buckley's partner Frankie Jules-Hough and unborn child died in May 2023.

"Our justice is being taken away, I understand there's a crisis, I agree that it needs to be addressed, but not at the expense of victims," he told BBC Breakfast.

News.title: Fires started 'deliberately' on mountain as crews tackle blaze
News.content:
She said the fire was particularly bad on Monday night when "the smoke was so thick I couldn't breathe" and added that the firefighters had been "amazing".

Ian Putland said even with the windows closed he could smell the fire.

"I heard about it a couple of days ago, and didn't think it would affect me... but then I came out yesterday and saw ash on the car and it indicated how close the fire was," he said.

"I was then alarmed with all the fire people about."

He added that he was "frustrated that the fires had been started deliberately".

"There's the wildlife killed, people are being put in danger and it takes emergency services away. It is a real waste of resources."

Christian Hadfield, area manager at SWFRS, said crews had been at the incident since Saturday but declared it a major incident on Monday in order to protect homes in the area.

"We are putting fire breaks in and monitoring the area," he said.

He added there were reports of "pockets of deliberate fire setting" which put the crews "under really critical conditions and stretches the service".

The fire was "unpredictable and complex work", he said, and firefighters could be there "for many days to come".

News.title: Scottish exam pass rates rise as students find out results
News.content:
Pass rates for Scottish exams have increased as students across the country received their results.

More than 148,000 learners have been finding out the results of their Nationals, Highers, Advanced Highers and Skills for Work Awards.

Qualifications Scotland - which replaced the Scottish Qualifications Authority last year after a number of controversies - said a record number of vocational and technical qualifications were awarded.

Figures show that the poverty-related attainment gap has narrowed compared with last year.

Admissions service Ucas said a record number of Scottish students aged 18 and under had been accepted into university or college. In total, 32,370 Scottish students of all ages secured places, up from 31,850 in 2025.

News.title: Breast cancer checks missing most women under 50 who are at risk, says study
News.content:
Breast cancer is a leading cause of death in women under 50 in the UK.

Most cases - 96% - are in women over 40, while 25% are in women over 75.

Men can get breast cancer too, with about 420 new cases every year in the UK.

Natasha Finch was diagnosed with an aggressive breast cancer at just 23 despite having no known risk factors.

She has since become an advocate for breast cancer awareness and wants young women to take symptoms seriously.

"I'm six years on and still here, still winning. Going to the GP was scary, but I'm so glad I went when I did â because if I hadn't, who knows?"

"I just want to advocate for girls."

This study, by a team from Cambridge University and the Institute of Cancer Research, looks at how to predict breast cancer risk in younger women.

They used a risk calculator called Boadicea that combines factors such as family history, lifestyle, reproductive history and genetic information to give a risk score.

If all women under 50 were to have this done, they estimate about a quarter (26.5%) would be categorised as at above-average risk and referred for further assessment.

This would include a third of women under 50 (34.8%) who develop breast cancer within 10 years.

By comparison, the current Nice criteria would result in 1.4% of women under 50 being referred for further assessment, which would include just 4.4% of those women who develop breast cancer.

A main reason for the disparity, the researchers say, is because three-quarters of women (73%) under 50 who develop breast cancer within a decade have no family history of breast cancer - the key criterion in the Nice guidelines.

News.title: Half-price rail travel extended to 18-year-olds
News.content:
Eighteen-year-olds will be able to buy half-price train tickets for most services when railcard rules are changed later this month, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

It's an extension of the 16-17 Saver railcard which currently expires when the holder turns 18. From 17 August, they will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase.

It means 17-year-olds will be able to buy the railcard up until the day before they turn 18, making it valid until the day before they turn 19.

Seventeen-year old Lily-Mae from Blackpool told the BBC the move would save her "a few hundred [pounds] a year".

She uses the train to travel regularly from Blackpool North to Preston and Manchester.

"I have been planning to see my boyfriend and my friends, and it's just not really happened because of the price of the trains," she said.

"Also getting to college for me is hard as I go to a college in Preston, but I live in a different town, so now I won't have to save as much money to get there."

The existing rule meant more than 70,000 students each year were an average of Â£175 worse off than those in the same academic year who hadn't yet had their 18th birthday, the DfT said.

The 16-17 Saver Railcard costs Â£35 per year and entitles the holder to 50% off most train fares.

Rail minister Lord Hendy claimed this "common sense change" is "exactly what passengers should expect from the railway".

He said the change would "lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they're pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market".

Jacqueline Starr, chief executive of industry body the Rail Delivery Group, said the change demonstrates the sector's commitment to "offering better value fares and delivering a more joined-up railway".

Kaynat Ahmad, vice president for further education at the National Union of Students, described the railcard as "essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training".

Eighteen-year-olds were already entitled to a 16-25 Railcard, but that only entitles them to a third off the cost of travel.

The government said the measure would be paid for through increased train ridership, with more passengers as a result of more people being able to access the discounted fares.

The announcement comes after the government said the cap on most single bus fares in England will be cut from Â£3 to Â£2 next year.

News.title: Man 'driven insane' by noise admits killing fish
News.content:
A man who admitted using motor oil and detergent to kill his neighbour's fish, after being "driven completely insane" by the noise of a water pump in the pond, has been sentenced.

Gerry Duffy, 76, of Hadley Road, Barnet, north London, pleaded guilty on the day of his trial at Willesden Magistrates' Court to three counts of damaging property and one count of unlawfully destroying fish in March.

The court heard Duffy climbed into Andreas Ptohides' garden to break the water pump "out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep", having warned his neighbour he would take matters into his own hands.

Duffy was given a two-year conditional discharge and ordered to pay Â£565 in compensation to his neighbour.

Duffy, who worked as a builder before his retirement, lives in a studio flat which backs on to the garden owned by his neighbour, the court heard.

Shahid Iftakhar, prosecuting, said the "neighbour dispute" between Duffy and Ptohides, potentially caused Â£565 of damage.

He said: "The defendant has previously complained to the complainant about noise coming from his garden and has said words to the effect of, 'if you didn't deal with it, I would' â there was a warning before the incident."

The prosecution added that Duffy was captured on CCTV having "climbed into the complainant's garden and damaged the water pipes and pumps".

In mitigation, Elliott Stern told the court his client had tried to deal with the dispute without resorting to killing the fish.

Mr Stern said: "The man has been driven completely insane by this noise, he's spoken to the complainant several times.

"They initially said they would stop the water pump going but then turned around and said that's not good for the fish."

An environmental officer came to the house and told Duffy he either had to "move or close his window", the court heard.

"Out of sheer frustration and lack of sleep, Mr Duffy, out of character, I would say, lost his mind and committed various damages," said Stern.
