News.title: Tributes paid to 'quietly seismic' theatre director and playwright Peter Gill
News.content:
Theatre director, playwright and actor Peter Gill, who has died aged 86, has been described as a "gentle man with a fierce intelligence" who had a "quietly seismic" influence on British theatre.

Cardiff-born Gill performed with the Royal Shakespeare Company and appeared in films including HMS Defiant and Zulu before embarking on a successful theatre directing career.

Among those to pay tribute was Welsh actor Luke Evans, who credited Gill with launching his own career.

Gill's agent Mel Kenyon said his work had a "rare emotional delicacy" that was "beautifully observed and finely tuned".

Gill is closely associated with his work at the Royal Court in London, where he is credited with introducing the plays of English writer DH Lawrence to the theatrical world.

Born in Cardiff on 7 September 1939, he was raised in a working-class community and remained "fiercely proud of his Welsh heritage throughout his life", according to an obituary written by his agency Casarotto Ramsay & Associates.

He pursued an acting career from the age of 18 before moving into theatre, most closely associated with the Royal Court, where he championed three Lawrence plays A Collier's Friday Night, The Daughter-in-Law and The Widowing of Mrs Holroyd.

"Their success revived interest in Lawrence's dramatic work and helped spark a renaissance of his plays in London theatre circles after decades of relative obscurity following his death in 1930," the agency said.

He also presented two of his early plays, The Sleeper's Den and Over Gardens Out, at the theatre, before becoming associate director in 1970.

In 1976, he became artistic director of Riverside Studios, with his production of William Shakespeare's As You Like It marking the official opening of the Hammersmith-based theatre that year.

He also adapted Anton Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard for the theatre, helping transform it from a "small fringe theatre" into a "venue regarded as the equal of the leading theatres of the West End".

In 1980, he was appointed OBE for his services to theatre, also founding the National Theatre Studio in 1984 and running it until 1990.

News.title: Boy, 14, dies after going into water at dock
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has drowned after going into the water at a dock in east London.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) and the Metropolitan Police searched the Millwall Outer Dock near East Ferry Road after being alerted at about 18:50 BST on Monday.

His body was recovered at about 22:30 and he was pronounced dead at the scene. His family have been informed, police said.

In a post on social media, Mayor of Tower Hamlets Lutfur Rahman named the teenager as Banta Sillah and said he was "a talented young footballer who played for Frontline Community FC and was instrumental in helping the team win the Tower Hamlets Cup last week".

The Met Police has not confirmed the identity of the boy.

The mayor said Banta "had immense potential and was dearly loved by his peers".

He added: "As we mourn Banta, I urge families to speak with children and young people, we should all be aware of the dangers swimming in open water.

"Swimming should only take place in officially designated areas with lifeguards present."

News.title: Campaigners denied appeal over Gatwick expansion
News.content:
In a 29-page ruling, they said: "We conclude that each of the grounds of appeal raised by each appellant is unarguable.

"Neither appeal has a real prospect of success. We also consider that there are no other compelling reasons for either appeal to be heard."

The two senior judges also said that the previous ruling was "detailed and thorough".

Gatwick is the UK's second busiest airport and one of the busiest single-runway airports in the world.

The expansion will allow the site to be used for the departures of narrow-bodied planes such as Airbus A320s and Boeing 737s.

Following the decision, Barclay said: "We are very disappointed with the Court's decision. We took this challenge as far as we could because we believed that the decision to allow Gatwick to expand was fundamentally flawed.

"It was not supported by government policy, would only serve to line the pockets of the airport and airlines, and would do so at the expense of local residents and the climate."

Cagne said: "Residents should be immensely proud of what they have achieved in holding Gatwick Airport's shareholders to account.

"This proposed new runway will come at a significant cost to both the taxpayer and the planet."

News.title: Why Use.ai Wants Work to Happen in One Workspace, Not Many
News.content:
The Independent was not involved in the creation of this sponsored content.

Most professionals no longer struggle to access artificial intelligence. They struggle to manage it. A marketing manager might research in one AI tool, draft copy in another, and store the output in a third app, losing context at every handoff. That daily shuffle, not a shortage of clever models, has become the real tax on modern work.

The Problem With Too Many Tools

Over the past two years, teams have added AI tools faster than they have added structure. Workplace software surveys show the average knowledge worker now juggles several AI subscriptions alongside existing project management and file systems. Each tool solves a narrow task well, but none of them talk to each other. Knowledge gets trapped in separate chat histories. Files sit disconnected from the conversations that produced them. The result is a workday full of copying, re-explaining, and starting over, even when the thinking has already been done once.

This fragmentation carries a real cost. Budgets stretch across overlapping subscriptions, and time meant for output goes toward moving information between systems. For teams under pressure to move fast, that friction adds up until it becomes the default way of working.

The Case for One Workspace

Use.ai was built around a different premise. The advantage in AI work no longer comes from which model you use, but from how well your tools will work together. The platform brings AI, project management, a structured knowledge base, and file management into a single environment. In that environment, a document, a task, and a conversation about that task all live in the same place. You are not switching context every few minutes. Your files and saved credentials stay searchable and usable, so your team stops rebuilding the same workflow from scratch each week.

Organisations can also structure their operations within the platform, from building teams and setting access levels to running group conversations and collaborating on shared projects. Rather than choosing a preferred model, UseAI sits above that choice, coordinating the tools a team already relies on into a single connected system.

The Story Behind Use.ai

The idea came together after its founders watched a team complete a single project across five different AI tools, researching in one, writing in another, and editing in a third, with time lost simply moving information between them. Rebuilding that same workflow within a single environment cut the work from hours to a fraction of the time, with fewer breaks and less repetition. That experience became the founding logic of UseAI , not another interface for accessing AI, but a workspace where thinking, execution, and collaboration happen in the same system.

The platform has also attracted discussion on review sites and community forums. User notes and threads provide breakdowns that weigh it against the cost of several subscriptions.

The Path Ahead for Teams

Use.ai has emerged as more teams rethink how they organize AI at work. More teams are moving from testing individual AI tools to building their daily operations around a single connected system, and UseAI is growing alongside that demand, as more organisations lean toward adoption.

An urgent police search is underway for a 13-year-old boy who got into trouble swimming off the coast of Hornsea, East Yorkshire, on Tuesday evening.

Emergency services rushed to the scene after receiving reports at around 6pm regarding concerns for the safety of the boy.

HM Coastguard, Yorkshire Ambulance Service and Humberside Fire and Rescue Services, and Humberside Police officers have been deployed to the area of the South Promenade, and are being assisted with the force’s marine unit and drone pilots.

Chief Superintendent Phil Booker said: “After receiving the report, officers were immediately deployed alongside other emergency services and upon attending, it was discovered that a 13-year-old boy had reportedly got into difficulty whilst swimming in the water.

open image in gallery Police received reports of the incident at around 6pm on Tuesday ( AFP/Getty )

“Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors (POLSA), along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him.”

Police have asked members of the public to stay away from the beach as they conduct their search.

“We would urge people to please avoid the area where possible to allow emergency services to work efficiently and safely, and refrain from speculating on the circumstances of the incident,” Mr Booker said.

“Our enquiries continue to ascertain the full circumstances around the report, and we would ask anyone with any information that may assist us, to please speak to the officers in Hornsea, or contact us via our non-emergency number 101 quoting log 415 of 4 August.”

open image in gallery A bunch of flowers left by River Thames at Millwall Outer Dock (Ben Whitley/PA) ( PA Wire )

On Monday, a 14-year-old boy died after entering the water near Millwall Outer Dock, on London’s Isle of Dogs.

Detective Superintendent Oliver Richter urged people to only swim in designated areas, and to take the time to speak with children and young people about staying safe around water.

“As the warm weather continues, I would urge everyone to remember that open water can present serious dangers,” he said.

The Royal Life Saving Society has reminded people to “stop and think” before going swimming following a rise of water-related incidents and deaths in the UK this summer.

A Nasa astronaut has said it was “not a great feeling” when he and his crew mates were ordered to prepare for a possible evacuation from the International Space Station (ISS) during an attempt to fix an air leak.

Describing it as a “very unusual day” aboard the orbiting outpost, Chris Williams said he and his colleagues immediately fell back on their training and “knew exactly what to do”.

Recounting the experience following his recent return from an eight-month mission in space, the flight engineer said the main concern had been the safety of the two Russian cosmonauts undertaking the repair.

Mr Williams was one of five members directed by Nasa’s mission control back in June to take refuge in their docked Dragon spacecraft in case they needed to escape quickly while the work was carried out.

They were also told to put on their spacesuits.

open image in gallery Cracks aboard the ageing outpost have raised concerns (Nasa) ( PA Media )

The rare safe haven procedure was in place for around two hours before the astronauts returned to the Nasa station, circling around 250 miles above the Earth.

Nasa said at the time it had given the instruction “out of an abundance of caution”, but also spoke of its ongoing concerns about cracks and leaks aboard the ageing facility, which is due to be retired in 2030.

The agency had worked with its Moscow-based counterpart Roscosmos to tackle the problem.

Mr Williams returned to Earth on July 26 after logging 241 days on his first space flight.

Recalling the incident during a news conference at the Johnson Space Centre in Houston, Texas, Mr Williams said: “That was certainly a very unusual day on station.

“It was not something that we were expecting to do.

“We knew that there was some work going on… and that there were some cracks in the pressure vessel that they were investigating.

“But we sort of were going about our normal day until we were we were called up and told to go shelter in the Dragon.”

He added: “Now, thankfully, this is something that we talked about and planned for.

“You know, it’s certainly not a great feeling because you know my two crew mates are over on the Russian segment working in this compartment, and so you don’t you don’t feel great when your crew mates are over there on the other side.

“But we planned and prepared for a five-person shelter-in-place Dragon.

“When difficult situations like that come up, you fall back on your training, and we knew exactly what to do, and we also knew that the ground teams were working on how to make sure that we could get out of this situation as safely as possible.

“We were really thinking a lot about, like OK, what do we bring with us so that you know if we’re there for a couple hours, we have snacks and that sort of thing.”

However, at the same time the team were keeping their Russian colleagues – Sergei Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev – “in our minds”.

Mr Williams went on: “It was definitely an unusual day. But you know, you kind of flip into that that mode where you fall back on your training.”

During his time in space, Mr Williams completed 3,856 orbits of the Earth and travelled a mammoth 102 million miles.

His work on the station included carrying out research for new cancer treatments.

He also completed two spacewalks to prepare for space station power system upgrades and to replace a faulty joint on a robotic arm.

Once bitter rivals in the space race during the Cold War, Russia and the US cooperate on the space station and other projects.

That relationship has been tested by tensions between the two countries, including over the Kremlin’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Despite this, Washington and Moscow have continued to work together, with US and Russian crews flying to the station on each country’s spacecraft.

The aggressive push by Republicans to question Dr. Anthony Fauci — first in a fiery hearing last week in the Senate, now with a potential contempt vote — could have an unexpected upside. Top GOP figures have books about Fauci that could get a bump in sales.

Following Fauci’s testimony, in which he repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment to remain silent, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. immediately promoted his Fauci book from 2021 on X, claiming Americans were “tired of the lies and they wanted their freedom back.”

Senator Paul, who has led the charge in accusing Fauci of covering up a potential lab leak origin story for Covid, has not taken the same overt approach, though the Republican has a Fauci book of his own, 2023’s Deception: The Great Covid Cover-up.

The Independent has contacted Kennedy, Paul and the publisher of both books for comment.

Kennedy may have enjoyed a brief spike in sales.

open image in gallery Republicans aggressively questioning Anthony Fauci could have a financial stake in the matter, ethics experts warn, given that some, like Sen. Rand Paul, have books for sell about Fauci ( Getty )

“Once again the most censored book in recent history is one of the bestselling books in America,” according to Tony Lyons, president of Kennedy’s publisher, Skyhorse, and president of MAHA Action, a pro-Kennedy political group, told the MAHA Report last week.

The book briefly shot up to number 52 on the Amazon bestseller list, Lyons claimed, though the book is now no longer in the top 100 best-selling books on the site. It remains number one in categories such as immunology, vaccinations and virology, according to Amazon.

Lyons told The New York Times that royalties from the book went to Children’s Health Defense, the anti-pollution and anti-vax non-profit that Kennedy founded.

In a 2025 filing, Kennedy disclosed more than $450,000 in consulting fees from Skyhorse.

open image in gallery Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. promoted his 2021 book about Dr. Fauci shortly after the former public health official was questioned in the Senate last week ( Getty )

Paul, meanwhile, disclosed about $90,000 in royalties from his Fauci book in 2024, which now shares a publisher with Kennedy thanks to a 2023 acquisition.

Of course, Dr. Fauci is also a published author.

His memoir, 2024’s On Call, is a top-10 seller on Amazon in such categories as viral diseases, communicable diseases, and medical professional biographies.

Republicans have criticized the official for winning a $1 million prize from the Israel-based Dan David Foundation for “defending science.” (Government ethics officials allowed Fauci to keep the prize.)

Liverpool fighter Darren Till believes Conor McGregor should “listen to his body” after suffering catastrophic leg injuries in back-to-back UFC fights - but would still jump at the chance to fight the Irishman in his bare-knuckle promotion.

McGregor made his hotly-anticipated return to the Octagon in July after five years out of the cage, but his clash with Max Holloway ended in disaster in just 69 seconds when he endured what turned out to be an ACL tear, after throwing an audacious jumping roundhouse in the first moments of the fight.

The 38-year-old injured the same right leg he broke against Dustin Poirier in 2021, sparking many to speculate whether this latest setback would be the end of his career.

McGregor, however, has insisted he will make a comeback for the final fight in his UFC contract, setting his sights on next summer despite questions surrounding his physical state.

open image in gallery Conor McGregor wants to fight Max Holloway again in 2027 ( Getty )

Till, a former UFC title challenger who has a self-confessed love for extreme violence, recognises how hard it can be for fighters to step away from the sport but feels McGregor is in a position, physically and financially, where he should think about hanging up the gloves.

“I like it but the thing with Conor [is] he’s made a lot of money,” Till told The Independent. “He probably doesn’t still need it but he probably wants it because it’s hard for him to leave the sport behind and he’s a fighter’s fighter.

“I do get it but sometimes it’s probably best to just let it go.

“If Conor’s getting injured like that in the first few seconds of a fight, he should probably be listening to his body.”

He added: “But again, the one thing with Conor, he’s got more than enough money to get seen to and to get all the best procedures, so who knows, he might come back a better man, he might not. We’ll see.”

Till, 33, is preparing for his second fight in Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC), a promotion which McGregor has part-ownership of.

After bouncing back from a first-round knockdown to knock out Aaron Chalmers, once of Geordie Shore fame, the Scouser is now staring down the barrel of tantalising match-up against Cuban specimen Yoel Romero, an Olympic silver-medallist who continues to fight at 49.

open image in gallery Darren Till (right) and Yoel Romero refused to unlock eyes in a stare-down that lasted over 200 seconds ( BKFC )

The pair will throw down on 26 September but with Till quickly becoming the face of the company, he has not shut down the possibility of a fight with the boss, McGregor, if the Irishman decides to step into his own ring.

“If it’s ever on the cards for me and Conor, I’d happily take it,” Till said, with bare-knuckle boxing potentially a smart option for McGregor to spare his legs any further punishment.

“He’s obviously got a share in the company, he can obviously pick and choose who he wants to fight. If ever that day comes and he wants to fight me, then we’ll glove up - or we won’t glove up, because it’ll just be fists.”

Famed Game of Thrones author George R. R. Martin has disclosed that he has battled bouts of sadness and depression this past year.

Martin, 77, who wrote the best-selling fantasy novel that the smash hit HBO Max series is based on, opened up about his mental health challenges to fans in a new blog post, published Monday.

“This year has been… stressful, to say the least,” Martin admitted. “So much has been happening, it’s been overwhelming. Some great things, exciting things.”

He wrote that while some of his dreams have come true, “there have been nightmares too.”

“I have lost friends. Battled sadness and depression. The worst may be yet to come,” Martin continued. “I turned seventy-seven last September, and I tell you, getting old is no fun. But there have been amazing times as well.”

open image in gallery George RR Martin said he’s been battling bouts of ‘sadness and depression’ ( Getty )

open image in gallery Martin is currently working on ‘The Winds of Winter,’ the long-awaited sixth novel in his Song of Ice and Fire series ( Getty )

He added, “I suppose that’s just life. Of course, I knew that. If you’ve read my stories, you know that.”

Highlighting the nine Emmy nominations that HBO’s Game of Thrones spin-off prequel series, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, secured last month, Martin said: “I am proud of our team.”

The critically acclaimed drama is adapted from The Hedge Knight, the first novella in Martin’s Dunk and Egg series, later collected in the 2015 anthology A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms.

Set roughly 100 years before the events in Game of Thrones, the series stars Starring Peter Claffey as a young and naive knight and follows his dangerous exploits with his diminituive squire, Egg (Dexter Sol Ansell). It earned nine Emmy nods, including Outstanding Drama Series.

Of the 2026 Emmy ceremony, taking place September 14 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, Martin said, “I hope to attend… but that depends on… well, on a lot of things.”

Sharing his hope that the show takes home a few wins, he confessed, “I was hoping we’d get a few of the acting nominations as well. But there’s always next year.”

open image in gallery Peter Claffey leads HBO's 'A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms' as Ser Duncan the Tall ( HBO )

Martin is currently in the process of writing The Winds of Winter, the long-awaited sixth title in his A Song of Ice and Fire series, which includes Game of Thrones.

He revealed in January that he was “struggling” to complete the book. “Maybe I’m overoptimistic about how quickly I can write these things,” he told The Hollywood Reporter. “I will open the last chapter I was working on and I’ll say, ‘Oh f***, this is not very good.’ And I’ll go in and I’ll rewrite it. Or I’ll decide, ‘This Tyrion chapter is not coming along, let me write a Jon Snow chapter.’”

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

Lindsay Lohan is once again a redhead — much to the delight of her fans.

In a series of Instagram photos shared Tuesday, the 40-year-old Mean Girls star is seen sporting an ear-to-ear grin with her long red locks on full display. The tousled waves compliment her natural makeup and stand out against her blue-and-white robe.

Most recently a blonde, Lohan became known for her red hair as she rose to fame in films including The Parent Trap, Freaky Friday and Confessions of a Teenage Drama Queen.

Fans gushed over Lohan’s return to her signature red locks.

“Redhead Lindsay is the best Lindsay,” one fan commented while another said, “the most iconic redhead in pop culture.”

open image in gallery Lindsay Lohan has returned to her signature red hair ( @lindsaylohan / Instagram )

“I love how you can rock every haircolor , but I feel red is the most Iconic,” another wrote as someone else agreed, “Love that hair color! You look gorgeous with any color but your natural color is amazing!”

“SHES RED AGAIN! The most famous red head IN THE WORLD!!!” someone else chimed in while another fan wrote, “Hands down the most iconic redhead!”

Lohan also shared a behind-the-scenes look at her recent ad with Reese’s, in which she’s sporting blonde hair in some scenes and red in others, playing twins in a seeming nod to her Parent Trap days.

In the film, twins Annie and Hallie (both played by Lohan) bond over loving Oreo cookies with peanut butter. So it was only right, then, that Lohan was the face of a recent ad announcing an Oreo and Reese’s Peanut Butter collaboration.

The ad features Amy Sedaris and her twin turn up at Lohan’s “Reese’s Twins Retreat” camp.

open image in gallery Lindsay Lohan has ditched her blonde locks and is once again a redhead ( Getty )

“Welcome to my wellness retreat, where I help twins work out their differences,” a blonde Lohan began before panning to the camera, “Because, well — I know a thing or two about twins.”

Lohan recently reflected on The Parent Trap, telling Parade, “It means so much. It was, you know, my first movie audition, my first film, and it holds such an important place in my heart.

“It’s just such a lovely family movie, and Nancy Meyers has such a beautiful way of doing that in her films. And people just really connect to it. It’s so funny; still today, young kids now notice me from that, which is just wild that people still love it so much. And to be a part of something like that is really special.”

When asked which twin she identified with more, Lohan said, “I think always a bit of both, because I’m super feminine, but I’m also a little tomboy. So, I think I was both. Long hair, I like long hair better, but when I was young, I wanted the Jennifer Aniston haircut, so I was Hallie in that sense. But a little bit of both.”

Darren Till and Yoel Romero had to be forced apart by security their face-off ran beyond three tense minutes as the ex-UFC pair set the tone for their dream match in Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC).

Liverpudlian Till, 33, is making his second outing for the Conor McGregor-owned bare-knuckle promotion after securing a knockout win of Aaron Chalmers, once of Geordie Shore fame, in his debut in May.

The former UFC title contender now clashes with someone he once shared the middleweight rankings with in Romero, who at 49 continues to prove his reputation as a physical specimen.

After trading barbs in their press conference in Manchester, the fighters took to the stage to close out the show with a customary face-off - and while there were no fireworks in the sense of a physical clash, it snatched attention for a completely different reason.

Romero slowly lifted his head and locked eyes with Till, with their stare not broken for a total of three minutes and 28 seconds.

open image in gallery Yoel Romero (left) takes off his glasses as the stare-down intensifies ( BKFC )

BKFC’s live stream of the press conference went off the air before the pair went their separate ways, each man refusing to be the first one to break eye contact.

As the on-stage security tried to usher Till backwards towards the stage, the Scouser continued to stare at Romero and bowed towards him before, at long last, turning his head to depart.

Many of those in attendance admitted it was the longest face-off they’d ever seen.

Romero could be seen speaking to Till during the face-off, though the Cuban remained coy over what was said.

“We didn’t really talk much, I just told him that this isn’t a game and I did not come here to play,” Romero told The Independent through an interpreter, having spent the entire press conference refusing to bow to Till’s demands for him to speak in English.

“I was looking right through him. I could’ve been there all day. I came here to Manchester to win.”

Romero was a major threat at the top of the middleweight division during his time in the UFC. He had three opportunities at the gold and beat Luke Rockhold with the interim belt on the line in 2018 - but wasn’t eligible to become champion due to missing weight

The Cuban only made his UFC debut at the age of 36, having won Olympic silver in wrestling at Sydney 2000, and has remarkably continued to remain active for Bellator, RAF and other bare-knuckle promotions as he approaches 50.

Till, meanwhile, has experienced a rejuvenation outside the UFC, where his mesmeric rise to a welterweight title shot was followed by a sharp decline where he lost five fights in six.

He went unbeaten in three fights for Misfits, most notably finishing former UFC champion Rockhold, and now intends to go on a similarly dominant run for BKFC.

The pair will throw down at the AO Arena on 26 September.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

Sports.title: Rapper Drake called me to convince me to quit Tottenham.. I thought it was Aaron Lennon winding me up says Jermain Defoe
Sports.content:
JERMAIN DEFOE says music icon Drake persuaded him to join Toronto from Tottenham – but only after thinking Aaron Lennon was playing a cruel prank.

The legendary striker, 43, hit the headlines when his spell as Woking’s boss ended after only SIX competitive showdowns last month.



But Defoe, who was blasted by the non-league minnows following his exit, had a stunning career with Spurs.

He made 363 appearances across two spells on Tottenham’s books – notching 143 goals along the way.



Defoe quit the North Londoners when MLS side Toronto came calling in 2014.

And Canadian rapper Drake was tasked with convincing the England icon to make the stunning move.

But Defoe was certain Tottenham team-mate Lennon, 39, was winding him up when he picked up the phone.

The former West Ham and Portsmouth marksman told the Mirror: “I remember being out for dinner with my cousin.

“I got a phone call, said ‘hello, who’s this’, and he said ‘It’s Drake’. Yeah, good one – I thought he was winding me up!

“I actually thought it was Aaron Lennon, I thought, ‘Wow, your Canadian accent is unbelievable’. But no, it was Drake.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“We had a conversation and I remember he spoke about Toronto, the city, what it’s like, the people, the football club, and that was it. I decided to sign and I loved it.”

Defoe went on to find the net 12 times in 21 appearances for the Canadian side, whose home was on hosting duties for this summer’s World Cup.

And it allowed him to reunite with ex-Tottenham pal Ryan Nelsen, who was in charge of Toronto, despite initially having doubts.

The lethal finisher, who bagged a brace at Soccer Aid in June, added: “I remember getting a call from Ryan Nelsen.



“I played with Ryan at Tottenham towards the back end of his career. Obviously, he got the Toronto job and we spoke about the opportunity of going there.

“At the time I said I don’t think it’s going to happen because I was at Tottenham and I was settled and didn’t really think I was going to leave.”

Defoe reignited his Premier League career by joining Sunderland after a year-long spell with Toronto.

And he returned to the Stadium of Light, following stints with Bournemouth and Rangers, before announcing his retirement in 2022.

Sports.title: Jordan FA chief accuses Gianni Infantino of ‘BLACKMAIL’ in most scathing statement yet: ‘We certainly won’t endorse him’
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO and Fifa have been accused of “blackmail” in the most scathing statement yet.

The head of world football’s governing body has come under intense criticism since his failed plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa events.



He backed down after a chaotic few days which saw football bodies around the world threaten a rebellion.

But despite the plans being thrown in the bin, Infantino continues to come under heavy fire as he desperately tries to cling on to the Fifa presidency.



However, the president of the Jordan FA launched a damning attack on the Swiss.

And it is even claimed Fifa withheld funds owed to the Jordan FA – and that the Asian national team federation would benefit from backing Infantino.



But the Jordan FA took a strong stance and insist they “refuse to give in” or “endorse” Infantino.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein, 50, wrote on X: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.

“Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time.

“We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted visas, even though they had tickets – which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

“Secondly, we are being taxed by the US govt through Fifa for our participation.

“Money that should go to players and staff.

“This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico.



“But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

“Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.

“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.



“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.

“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

SunSport has contacted Fifa for comment in response to Prince Ali’s tweet.

Interestingly, the support of national associations in Asia could be critical to Infantino’s re-election campaign in March.



However, he may not even reach that far if Fifa council members opt to oust him.

Uefa cranked up the pressure on Arsene Wenger to quit as Fifa’s head of global football development – but he has no intention of doing so.

European football chiefs, meanwhile, are ready to team up with other confederations to set up a rival World Cup to “paralyse Fifa”.

Infantino’s furious opponents are also prepared to boycott Fifa council and committee meetings, as well as refuse to ratify decisions.

The shameless lawyer has only notched 15 declarations of support from the 211 member nations since his botched project was revealed.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

And The FA joined their Welsh counterparts in withdrawing their backing ahead of next year’s presidential election.

Sports.title: England star’s sister follows in his footsteps and signs first professional contract at Premier League giants
Sports.content:
SACHA LEWIS is looking to emulate her brother Rico – after penning her first professional contract with Women’s Super League title holders Manchester City.

The Sky Blues bolstered their squad by landing Beth Mead from Arsenal last month.



And City have now rewarded Lewis, 18, with a deal after showing plenty of promise while coming through the ranks.

The defender has followed in her brother Rico’s footsteps, having seen him make waves in the Premier League before narrowly missing out on a place in England’s World Cup squad.



Lewis is now desperate to play a key role as City aim to defend their WSL crown.

After putting pen-to-paper, the England Under-19s international said: “It’s amazing. A lot of hard work was put in and it’s such a great achievement. I’m proud.

“It means so much, it means even more because I support City. Being here in the academy, not many people get this opportunity so I’m very grateful.”

Lewis joined the Sky Blues’ U14s before working her way through the system and being integrated into the senior squad.

The teenager was rewarded with a place in the matchday squad for two WSL showdowns last season.

And City chief Andree Jeglertz included Lewis among the substitutes for the League Cup semi-final loss to Chelsea in January.

Director of football Therese Sjogran said: “This is a special moment for Sacha and one she fully deserves.

“Her development is another demonstration of the incredible pathway our young players have to the first team.

“She’s been a shining example to her team-mates despite still being just 18.

“To that point, I would also like to thank our head of girls’ academy Hannah Dingley, lead coach Izzy Christiansen and everyone involved in our Next Gen set-up for their role in Sacha’s development.



“We’re all excited to see what she can achieve at City in the coming years. With her talent and attitude, she certainly has a bright future in the game.”

Lewis will be pushing to make her WSL debut in the season opener against newly-promoted Birmingham City on September 6.

Sports.title: Ex-Newcastle chief Amanda Staveley ‘in offer to buy David Sullivan’s 38.8% West Ham stake to own MAJORITY 63.9% of club’
Sports.content:
AMANDA STAVELEY reportedly offered to buy David Sullivan’s West Ham stake – and become the majority shareholder.

The former Newcastle co-owner’s firm PCP has the backing of US and Far East-based investors.



And after being the face of the Saudi takeover at St James’ Park, she is keen to spearhead a bid to take control of West Ham following their relegation to the Championship.

As reported by The Football Boardroom, Staveley approached Sullivan to buy out his 38.8 per cent stake in the Hammers for around £228million.



She also approached the Gold family over purchasing their 25.1 per cent at a price of £150m.

Together, that would total 63.9 per cent of the club for £378m.



Should PCP’s bid prove successful, they would become the majority owners of West Ham.

However, Daniel Kretinsky owns 27 per cent through 1890 Holdings and the WHU LLC holds the remaining eight per cent, led by J Albert Smith.

Staveley’s offers would value the entire 100 per cent stake of West Ham at just shy of £600m.

Sullivan could be forced to sell his portion of West Ham with the independent football regulator investigating his position following allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Sullivan, 77, denies all allegations and resigned from his position as Joint Chair of the club to fight them.

His former co-owner and business partner David Gold died in January 2023, with his family retaining his 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham.

Daughter Vanessa took control of the Gold stake and revealed in a statement just days ago that she intends to sell them to Staveley’s consortium.

Gold said: “I have now reached an agreement to sell my family’s shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.



“While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.”

However, Staveley – who was part of the Newcastle takeover in 2021 and remained a shareholder until 2024 – could have seen her hopes dashed.

That is because Kretinsky moved to try and block her buying the Gold shares.

The Czech businessman – who owns Royal Mail – was primed to take control of the club when Sullivan resigned in June.

Kretinsky is a minority owner as it stands – he is also majority owner and president of Sparta Prague.



However, he agreed to buy 16 per cent of West Ham from the Golds to take his stake to 43 per cent – with existing shareholders getting pre-emption rights offered before being opened up externally.

But with Staveley exploring the option of buying out both Gold and Sullivan, that would take her ownership to a majority.

In response, Kretinsky is selling two per cent of the club to fellow Czech Jakub Havrlant.

That means he could then buy the Golds’ 25.1 per cent and stay at the 50 per cent mark – enough to ensure Staveley cannot supercede his ownership without becoming the majority shareholder.

Should he exceed 50 per cent, that may trigger a clause forcing Kretinsky to buy Sullivan’s stake at an inflated price.



Staveley, meanwhile, has made no secret of her ambition to get back into football – and hinted at going for West Ham as well as the land around the London Stadium.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She told Bloomberg: “Whatever club we take, there will be a big property play as well. We won’t just do a football-led.”

The news came just hours after it was reported that Staveley has failed to settle a £750,000 debt with her former club Newcastle.

Sports.title: Premier League club quietly increase stadium capacity ahead of new season as part of £40million redevelopment
Sports.content:
BRIGHTON have been giving the Amex Stadium a makeover ahead of the new season – leading to the capacity being increased.

The Seagulls are preparing to host Uefa Conference League action after sealing European qualification on the final day of last term.



Brighton, who allowed Danny Welbeck to join Chelsea last week, are set to face Romanian side CFR Cluj or Norwegian outfit Tromso in the play-off round later this month.

And they will now be able to welcome 800 more fans after quietly working on a £40million redevelopment project.



A new premium hospitality space, known as the 1901 Club, has been added to the North Stand.

It has resulted in the Amex Stadium’s capacity rising to 32,500 as the Seagulls prepare for their showdown with Aston Villa on the opening weekend of the 2026/27 season.



More changes are in the pipeline after Brighton chiefs have continued looking to improve facilities.

Plans have been made to expand the safe standing area to the lower rows of the North Stand.

It comes after the plan was initially announced by the Premier League side in January.

Construction work is scheduled to start during next month’s international break, meaning it will be ready for clashes in October.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A club statement read: “The club can confirm safe standing will be extended to the lower rows of the North Stand in September 2026.

“Following a review of the voting, safe standing is moving to lower rows but only in more central blocks where this had the most support.

“This may mean that sight lines are impacted for the seats situated immediately next to safe standing areas.

“For those supporters whose seats will be converted to safe standing, a priority window will be available to move elsewhere in the stadium.”



Away fans are also set to be relocated to the south-west corner of the arena at the end of the campaign.

It is the Amex Stadium’s biggest transformation since Brighton moved in 15 years ago.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho’s three things he wants from Vinicius Jr as Arsenal transfer outcome awaits
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho’s three things he wants from Vinicius Jr as Arsenal transfer outcome awaits

Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Jr has been sent a clear message by Jose Mourinho as the Gunners await a final decision on his future

View 2 Images Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has revealed to Vinicius Jr what he expects of him (Image: (Photo by WOLFGANG JANNACH / APA / AFP via Getty Images))

Jose Mourinho has told Arsenal transfer target Vinicius Jr to enjoy himself, be positive and continue playing his style of football. The 25-year-old is back training in the Spanish capital after his break following Brazil's World Cup exit but the focus has instead been on his future amid significant interest from the Gunners.

‌



Vinicius has just one year remaining on his current contract and while there has not been a breakthrough in extension talks for some time, that could be about to change with new discussions set to take place on Wednesday.

‌



As such, Arsenal could be about to learn a definitive transfer outcome over his future with Real's stance clear that he either agrees to extend or is sold this summer.

‌



OPINION Arsenal may be using Vinicius Jr transfer talk as smokescreen for another huge deal by Fasika Zelealem

In the meantime, the forward has been putting in the hard yards alongside his Real team-mates under Mourinho's watchful eye.

In a video posted to Real's official social media channels, he lifted the lid on exactly what the new Los Blancos chief expects from him.

‌



The 26-year-old said: "He wants me to be just as I've always been - happy, positive and playing my own style of football."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power

FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under mounting pressure to step down from his role over plans to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's plan is rapidly falling apart (Image: DANIEL DUARTE/AFP via Getty Images)

Under-fire FIFA President Gianni Infantino has called his senior staff to a crisis meeting in a bid to cling to power. The desperate move comes after Arsene Wenger, FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development, broke rank and criticised Infantino's controversial plan to sell off competitions including the World Cup.

‌



Former Arsenal manager Wenger issued a statement on Monday saying that the withdrawal of Infantino's plan was 'absolutely necessary'. Meanwhile, Infantino's close allies are said to have been urging many of the 211 member associations to publicly back him after some withdrew their support for his re-election - while the president of one federation accused him of 'blackmail'.

‌



The Times report that Infantino has called staff to the Moroccan capital of Rabat for a crisis meeting. The Swiss chief is holed up in Morocco amid the swam of backlash.

‌



It's added that a group of senior staff within FIFA had a management meeting on Tuesday - without Infantino. All bar one reportedly opposed the plan to sell off FIFA's competitions.

Gianni Infantino accused of blackmail by Jordan FA chief in brutal FIFA criticism READ MORE :

Full list of Gianni Infantino's supporters and critics as FIFA president faces fight for job READ MORE :

Wenger's comments have also piled on pressure. " The recent events at FIFA deserve some clarity from my side. I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," the Frenchman said.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

‌



Even Infantino's No.2, FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, was revealed to have slammed the plan in a leaked email. " We have all been thrown into the middle of a turmoil, which is difficult to comprehend and accept, but, as Secretary General, I urge you to remain focused on what has always united us: serving football and serving our 211 member associations." Grafstrom wrote.

Should Gianni Infantino step down? Have your say in the comments section.

"A sad and reproachable series of events - which were thankfully concluded with the FFE project permanently abandoned - for as much as we feel dismayed by them, should not overshadow this reality.

"I assure you that you as members of the administration, you will be defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience. You do not need to worry.

"Individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go. The institution, its mission and its responsibility towards world football continue, and that is why we should always keep our professionalism, sense of perspective and composure."

Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley suffers major blow to West Ham plan as Daniel Kretinsky fights back

The battle for ownership at West Ham United has intensified after Daniel Kretinsky responded to Amanda Staveley’s consortium agreeing a £150m deal with the family of David Gold

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley (Image: (Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Amanda Staveley has suffered a blow in her attempt to buy into West Ham United after Daniel Kretinsky agreed to sell just over 2% of his stake in the club to Jakub Havrlant.

‌



Within the last few days, Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, and others agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the Hammers, who were relegated to the Championship last season.

‌



Staveley’s consortium agreed a £150million deal with the family of the late David Gold on Saturday. But before Staveley can buy it, existing shareholders have first refusal at the price she agreed.

‌



However, Hammers co-chair Kretinsky sold just over 2% of his stake in the club to Czech businessman Havrlant on Tuesday, dealing a blow to Staveley and her consortium. As a result of the deal, BBC Sport explain Kretinsky can now buy Gold's 25.1% stake without his own stake exceeding 50%, which would otherwise force him to make an offer for the remainder of the club.

"I am delighted Jakub Havrlant has joined the West Ham ownership group as a shareholder, subject to the pre-emption process," Kretinsky said. "He brings exceptional experience as an investor and digital innovator and I have no doubt his involvement will strengthen our club."

While speaking on an episode of Bloomberg’s Leaders with Francine Lacqua recorded before West Ham confirmed her agreement with Gold on Saturday, Staveley revealed she is planning a 'big property play' in English football.

She said: “Whatever club we take, there’ll be a big property play as well. We won’t just do a football-led.

“I just want a challenge, and that’s what excites me. That’s where you get value uplift — when you take something from seedling and allow it to grow.”

‌



View 2 Images West Ham United co-chair Daniel Kretinsky (c) looks on during the UEFA Europa Conference League in 2023 (Image: (Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images))

Royal Mail owner Kretinsky bought 27% of West Ham in 2021 and for his plan he may need the help of the club’s third-largest shareholder, the American billionaire Albert Tripp Smith, who owns 8 per cent. While The Times are reporting that there are set to be two rounds of bidding.

In the first round, shareholders have 30 days to buy their entitlement, which is up to the same proportion as their present holding. And in the second round, any remaining Gold shares can be bought by shareholders who participated in the first round.

Sports.content:
Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint

Michael Carrick left out Radek Vitek for Manchester United's most recent pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid and the goalkeeper is now on the verge of sealing a move away

View 2 Images Radek Vitek is set to leave Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are in advanced talks with Middlesbrough over the sale of Radek Vitek. The goalkeeper has been in search of regular game time after an impressive loan spell with Bristol City last season.

‌



Vitek, 22, started United's first two pre-season friendlies under Michael Carrick after returning to Old Trafford. But Carrick left him on the bench for the Red Devils' 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on Saturday in a hint at his impending departure.

‌



Now, Vitek is on the verge of completing a move to the Riverside. Multiple reports say that the Czech is close to signing for Middlesbrough on a permanent basis, adding that United will insert both a sell-on clause and a buy-back option into the deal. No fee has emerged at this stage.

‌



Having swept the end-of-season awards at Bristol City, Vitek found himself in high demand. The 22-year-old made it clear at the start of pre-season that he was 'ready' to leave.

"I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to be, hopefully, number one, so we will see," Vitek told reporters. "We will see what is going to happen.

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so. I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Vitek isn't the only United player who could be on the move in the coming days. Joshua Zirkzee has given the green light to join Juventus while Altay Bayindir is a target for Besiktas.

Sports.content:

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been hit with a damning accusation of blackmail by Jordan football association president Prince Ali Al Hussein

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino has been accused of blackmail by Jordan's FA president Prince Ali Al Hussein (Image: (Photo by KARIM JAAFAR / AFP via Getty Images))

Jordan football association president Prince Ali Al Hussein has shockingly claimed he was told during the World Cup that his nation would benefit if he endorsed Gianni Infantino. The FIFA president has endured a whirlwind few weeks with his controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors scrapped following severe backlash.

‌



Several governing body's slammed his proposal and a member of one nation's FA that was at the World Cup has gone one step further by suggesting blackmail attempts were made. Prince Ali also revealed Jordan are yet to be paid for reaching the final of a FIFA event alongside several other issues.

‌



Part of his X post read: "For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters- until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal star makes winning return to English football with League Two club

Vito Mannone, the ex-Arsenal goalkeeper, signed for Crawley Town as a player-coach this summer and he's already been thrust between the posts by boss Colin Kazim-Richards

View 3 Images Vito Mannone made his first appearance in 18 months (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

Former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone kept a clean sheet to help new club Crawley Town beat York City 2-0 on Monday and reach the Carabao Cup first round proper. Mannone, 38, signed for the League Two side as a player-coach in June after spending last season as a free agent while earning his coaching badges.

‌



The Italian got the nod for Crawley's first game of the season, travelling to York's LNER Community Stadium in a preliminary round of the Carabao Cup. Mannone and his team-mates advanced thanks to goals from Gianmarco Di Biase and Danilo Orsi.

‌



The victory booked Crawley a trip to Watford this Saturday. It was Mannone's first competitive appearance since February 2025 with former club Lille.

‌



He was on Arsenal's books for eight years, making a total of 23 first-team appearances. Mannone left the Emirates in 2013 to join Sunderland for £2million, spending the next four seasons at the Stadium of Light before moving to Reading.

He then plied his trade in France after signing for Monaco in 2020, later joining Lorient and finally Lille. Crawley convinced Mannone to make the drop from the French top flight to the fourth tier of English football by handing him a dual role, with the 38-year-old having recently been coaching at Brighton.

‌



Mannone will head up Crawley's goalkeeping department, taking training sessions and leading player development. "I am delighted and proud to take on this role and can't wait to meet everyone at the club and to start working with the staff and players," he said.

"I'll give everything to the cause and hope to pass on my experiences as a player, leading into a successful season."

Crawley's manager, former Premier League striker Colin Kazim-Richards, explained: "To be able to add to my coaching staff, to the club, someone of Vito's calibre is a credit in itself.

"His knowledge, his footballing experiences, playing at the highest level with some of the best coaches in terms of standards, what it actually takes and ideas coming from a country that creates amazing goalkeepers, has really taken us up another level.

"Vito comes with an intensity, and it's something I'm looking forward to in terms of creating a relationship and benefiting from his skills from a goalkeeper's perspective, and also as a person. As soon as we spoke, I knew he was the right man, so I can't wait to work with him."

Sports.title: Several athletes 'unaccounted for' after Commonwealth Games in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Reports in Uganda say that four members of the nation's boxing team have gone missing in Scotland; Police Scotland says it has received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for following the end of the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Sunday

Commonwealth Games: Several athletes 'unaccounted for' after Glasgow event, according to Police Scotland

Several athletes are "unaccounted for" after the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, according to Police Scotland.

The Ugandan sporting news website NBS Sport said that four members of Uganda's boxing team have reportedly gone missing in Scotland.

They said the athletes did not re-join the rest of the delegation before the team's scheduled return to Uganda on Tuesday.

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "Police Scotland has received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for.

"Inquiries are ongoing to assess the circumstances, and early engagement is taking place with the Home Office."

Speaking to the Press Association on Monday, Commonwealth Games chief executive Phil Batty said: "We've welcomed nearly 3,000 athletes to the city from 74 nations.

"We want to deliver a safe and secure games, so we work really closely with Police Scotland, the Border Force, and UK visas and immigration to make sure everyone arrives and departs in line with regulation."

PA understands that the Home Office will take action accordingly if it is made aware of any breaches of immigration law, and that it takes all necessary steps to prevent people who could abuse the immigration system from entering the UK.

The Home Office maintains a policy of not routinely commenting on individual asylum cases, with claims considered on their individual merits in accordance with the UK's international obligations.

The Ugandan ministry of education and sports has been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Sutherland leads SunRisers to tight win over Spirit
Sports.content:
SunRisers Leeds kept their faint hopes of progression from The Hundred group stage alive with a hard-fought five-wicket victory over London Spirit at Headingley.

Spirit made 136-7 after being put in to bat, but Australian duo Phoebe Litchfield (30 from 17) and Annabel Sutherland (37 not out from 21) led the SunRisers home with two balls to spare.

Spirit got off to a flying start with the bat, but SunRisers finally got their first wicket when Amy Jones hit Dani Gibson into the hands of Kate Cross at 68 for one.

London continued to accelerate but their momentum was halted when a rain shower caused a 30-minute delay and Grace Harris, who went past her half-century, also perished as they fell from 91 for one to 136 for seven at the halfway stage.

In reply, Phoebe Litchfield and Bryony Smith also enjoyed themselves at the top of the order and it looked like SunRisers would chase the score down at a canter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Katie George stops SunRisers Leeds from getting a boundary with a huge leap and throw back into play.

However, three wickets in six balls to dismiss Litchfield, Smith and Lauren Winfield-Hill pulled the Spirit back into the contest with the hosts still requiring 78 from 59.

SunRisers closed in on victory, but Gibson and Deepti Sharma fell to create some late drama.

However, a flurry of shots from Jess Jonassen and Sutherland took the hosts close to the finish line before the latter's six gave them the win.

Meerkat Match Hero Sutherland said: "It's nice to get the win. Jess came out with real clarity, and she's got a beautiful swing of the bat. It was nice to see a few go to the rope from her.

"Personally, I just feel pretty level. I feel like I'm coming into different situations and adapting pretty well. But ultimately, you want to be part of winning performances, and hopefully we can win the next few and build some momentum."

The result moves SunRisers up to fourth in the table, but they trail third placed Manchester Super Giants by six points having played the same number of games.

Spirit drop to sixth and their hopes of advancing to the knockout stages appear to be all but over.

Sports.title: Falcons make Robinson highest-paid running back in NFL history
Sports.content:
The Atlanta Falcons have agreed to a three-year contract extension with Bijan Robinson that will make him the highest-paid running back in NFL history.

According to Spotrac.com, the extension, which runs through to the 2030 season, is worth up to $75m (£55m), with the $51m (£37m) guaranteed portion a record for a running back.

Robinson will need to achieve multiple incentives to earn the full $75m (£55m), but even without doing that, the base level three-year $66.75m (£49.6m) deal will give the 24-year-old highest annual salary an NFL running back has ever earnt.

The $22.25m (£16.5m) per year takes him past the previous high mark of $20.6m (£15.3m) being earnt by Saquon Barkley at the Philadelphia Eagles.

Robinson reposted the NFL's Instagram post detailing the extension on Tuesday morning, writing "God this is for you! Blessings. Love this team and this city!"

A panel of eight AP Pro Football Writers ranked Robinson the league's top running back in a pre-season poll. Robinson led the NFL with 2,298 yards from scrimmage and scored 11 TDs last season.

Robinson has been the focus of Atlanta's productive ground game since he was the No 8 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft. He flourished as a dual-threat back last season, finishing fourth in the league with 1,478 rushing yards while adding 820 receiving yards.

Steven Jackson in 2006 is the only other player ever with at least 1,400 rushing yards and 800 receiving yards in the same season.
