“The Brazilian international arrives at one of the best moments of her career to strengthen a squad built to compete for every trophy. With her talent, creativity and ability to decide matches, Kerolin adds even more quality to a team whose ambition remains unchanged: to challenge for every title and, once again, strive to win it all.”

Sports.title: Arsenal target Vinícius says Mourinho ‘wants me to be happy’ at Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Vinícius Júnior is settling into life under the new Real Madrid manager, José ⁠Mourinho, with a smile on his face even as uncertainty swirls around the Brazil forward’s future at the Bernabéu.

The 26-year-old, who has ⁠been ​one of the linchpins of Real Madrid’s attack in recent years, gave an upbeat assessment of his second ⁠day of pre-season training under Mourinho despite speculation linking him with a possible move to Arsenal.

“It has ⁠gone very well, getting to know the new coach and the new ​players, and training very hard,” ‌Vinícius told Real Madrid ‌TV. “Mourinho wants me to be as I have always been: happy, cheerful ‌and playing my football.”

Vinícius’s cheerful demeanour, however, masks a potentially thorny situation brewing behind the scenes. He is in the final year of his Real Madrid contract, with speculation that the club and player remain locked in negotiations while Arsenal explore a potential transfer.

Vinícius has scored 128 goals for Madrid and provided 100 assists, with the club reluctant to ​let one of their prized assets leave for free next year.

He had a busy summer playing for Brazil at the World Cup, where they were knocked out in the last 16, and his focus now is ⁠on preparing for the new campaign.

“We have to prepare physically ​so that during the ​season we have fewer ​injuries and can count on everyone,” said Vinícius, who was ​Brazil’s top scorer ‌at the ​World Cup with ​four goals.

“It was a good training session and we all left very tired, but now it’s time to rest for tomorrow. That’s how pre-season is and we have to be ready.”

Sports.title: Frank Lampard hails ‘huge’ signing as Coventry seal record £22.5m Rushworth deal
Sports.content:
Coventry have completed the club-record £22.5m signing of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth from Brighton as Frank Lampard’s side continue to prepare for their return to the Premier League after 25 years away.

The 25-year-old excelled on loan at Coventry in the Championship last season, playing an instrumental role in their promotion as champions, starting all 46 league matches and earning the Golden Glove award for keeping 17 clean sheets.

“It’s great to have Carl back with us on a permanent basis,” said Lampard, whose side begin their season at Arsenal on 21 August. “He’s a top professional, a great character and he had a huge impact on the team to help us get promoted last season. I’m looking forward to working with him again and welcoming him back into the group.”

Rushworth, who is also highly regarded within the Football Association and the England setup, joined Brighton from non-league Halifax in 2019 but departed the club without making a senior appearance. Before his season at Coventry he had enjoyed loans across the league pyramid with Walsall, Lincoln City, Swansea and Hull.

Brighton’s sporting director, Mike Cave, said: “While we would have liked to keep Carl with the club for longer, we respect his decision to secure regular first-team football in the Premier League.” Brighton are thought to have negotiated a sell-on clause and a buy-back option as part of the sale, which could rise as high as £30m including add-ons.

Rushworth represents Coventry’s fourth summer signing. Last month they eclipsed their previous transfer record when paying Eintracht Frankfurt £17m to sign the Switzerland defender Aurèle Amenda, and have also signed Loum Tchaouna and Frank Onyeka. Until Amenda’s arrival, their record outlay was £7.7m, to Antalyaspor, for Haji Wright in 2023.



Elsewhere, Aston Villa have welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) upholding their appeal to register 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo. The teenager, who was born in London but raised in Luxembourg, joined Villa from Metz in January but had been ineligible to play owing to Fifa’s regulations on international transfers of minors. Madjo, who has scored four goals in pre-season, is now available to feature for Villa.

Sports.title: ‘I can’t wait’: Dominik Szoboszlai hungry for Liverpool reset under Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Dominik Szoboszlai believes last season’s frustration can push Liverpool to challenge for the title again but admits the squad must produce “something special” if no reinforcements arrive before the transfer deadline.

The Liverpool midfielder upped his already impressive level last season, being named the club’s player of the year, but collectively the team went into reverse with Arne Slot losing his job as a consequence. The poor title defence from a team that won the Premier League comfortably in Slot’s debut season should, Szoboszlai insists, prompt a reaction in Andoni Iraola’s debut campaign as Liverpool head coach.

“I can’t wait [for the new season], honestly,” said the Hungary captain following Liverpool’s pre-season tour of the US. “I feel that we are ready to go again and take motivation from last season because it was not the best. We didn’t end up where we wanted to. So now we’re going to go for it again.

“Everyone is motivated. I think I see in everybody’s eyes that he wants to play and, if you want to play, you have to give your best. And from there the manager is going to decide who is going to play. But everybody is on zero right now.”

Liverpool have added the central defender Jérémy Jacquet and the versatile forward Victor Muñoz this summer but, while they remain in pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola, a squad that has seen Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konaté depart as free agents remains light in several positions.

Szoboszlai said of Liverpool’s transfer activity: “It’s not my job to tell you who we have to sign or if we have to sign someone. If the guys above and the manager decide to sign someone, then we are very happy and are going to welcome him – or them – well. If they decide not to, then we have to do something special with this squad.”

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s new head coach, Andoni Iraola, cuts a thoughtful figure during the US pre-season tour. Photograph: Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images

The Liverpool midfielder revealed Iraola prefers not to address his players in the immediate aftermath of a game, a trait he discovered after the pre-season friendlies against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds. “He doesn’t speak after the game,” Szoboszlai disclosed. “I think every manager is different in his own way. That’s how he is. He always would rather speak the day after the game, which is fine for everyone. We have to get used to this.”

Iraola has also not spoken to Szoboszlai – or any other player for that matter – about filling one of the vice-captaincy positions vacated by Robertson and Salah. But the 25-year-old, who captained Liverpool on the US tour, says it would be a huge honour to be asked.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He added: “There hasn’t been any conversation. We have Virgil [van Dijk] as the captain, we have Ali [Alisson], we have Joe Gomez [as vice-captains], so there was no conversation at all. Obviously Ali is not here and Joe is injured. Let’s see. It’s not fixed. If you get offered the vice-captain of Liverpool, you’re going to take it. It would be a proud moment for me but I respect everybody. Whoever it’s going to be, we’re going to follow them.”

The captain’s armband became an issue for Curtis Jones when Szoboszlai passed it to Kostas Tsimikas during the win over Wrexham in New York. But Szoboszlai, who recently signed a new five-year contract at Anfield, insisted there was no problem with his fellow midfielder.

“It was never a debate between us three,” he claimed. “We just discussed something on the pitch. After, you guys make it very big. But next time we will manage to do it in the changing room. Nobody was angry. It’s all cleared. We are cool, everybody.”

Sports.title: Concacaf countries considering withdrawing support for under-fire Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
A number of Concacaf countries are considering following Europe’s lead by formally removing their ­support for the Fifa president, Gianni ­Infantino.

All 41 members of Concacaf – the confederation which represents North America, Central America and the Caribbean – are understood to have submitted ­letters of endorsement for ­Infantino’s re‑election campaign before the World Cup finals tournament, but many are now giving serious con­sideration to withdrawing them.

Finland became the first of Fifa’s 211 member associations to publicly withdraw its letter of support last Thursday, followed on Monday by the Football Association of Wales. The former Wales international Laura McAllister, a Uefa vice-president, had proposed the World Cup boycott at an emergency Uefa meeting last week, while the FA is also understood to have written to Fifa withholding its backing for Infantino.

Concacaf held an emergency meeting last Friday, with a source who attended telling the Guardian that all members are strongly aligned with Uefa, which has led the calls for Infantino to go.

The Concacaf meeting is understood to have featured pledges from several countries to withdraw their backing for Infantino, and some may have already done so in private.

One potential difficulty for Concacaf is the fact that four of its members – the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica – are bidding to stage the 2031 Women’s World Cup in the next hosting decision to be taken by Fifa.

While there are no other bids on the table at present, the decision still has to be approved by Fifa at an extraordinary general meeting to be held in November.

The US Soccer Federation is understood to be deeply unhappy with Infantino – particularly with the ­backlash his dealings with ­Donald Trump created for them over the Folarin Balogun affair – but, given the political sensitivities, may not feel able to take him on.

Another complicating factor is the fact that the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, has been widely touted as the potential candidate most able to take Infantino on in the presidential election next March.

Although Montagliani has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s ­governance, the Canadian has yet to decide whether he wants to stand, and told the Guardian in an interview last month that his priority is being re‑elected as president of ­Concacaf, with those elections also taking place next year.

While Concacaf is united, the Asian Football Confederation, which also backed the Uefa-led opposition to Infantino’s proposed World Cup sell‑off, appears to have splintered since the dramatic events of last week. Significantly, the financial powerhouses of Qatar and the United Arab Emirates have both publicly backed Infantino to stay on, as have smaller countries such as Sri Lanka, Lebanon, Kuwait and Bhutan.

11:54 Is Gianni Infantino’s time up as Fifa president? - The Latest

While most of the AFC’s 47 members – including Saudi Arabia – have stayed silent, Uefa is hoping it can attract their support, but it remains unclear whether the rebels have the numbers to force a genuine electoral contest.

New Zealand Football’s Andrew Pragnell says Fifa’s abandoned private equity proposal delivered a shock to confidence in world football’s governance, and he urged ­Oceania’s members to be united on the question of Infantino’s leadership.

Oceania’s confederation, which includes New Zealand among its 11 members, has yet to take a position on the Fifa president’s leadership, although Pragnall said there had been “enormous gains” for football associations outside the traditional powerhouses of Europe and ​South America under Infantino – “but the proposal itself, the way in which it was delivered, developed, the way members found out, and the shock to confidence among the international football system, has cast a pretty big shadow”.

Pragnell said that New Zealand would consult with Oceania members and other regional confederations before adopting a position, and said it would be preferable for the member nations to be aligned on the matter. “There’s obviously more power in numbers,” Pragnall said.

“Certainly it helps when a con­federation acts in unison. You’ve seen in some confederations, even in the last week, members go dif­ferent ways from other members.”

Sports.title: Man City interested in signing £54m Premier League star as Savinho pushes for Tottenham move
Sports.content:
Man City interested in signing £54m Premier League star as Savinho pushes for Tottenham move

Manchester City are interested in signing Chelsea winger Pedro Neto as a potential replacement for Tottenham target Savinho, talkSPORT understands.

Savinho has been tipped with a summer exit having struggled for game time at the Etihad Stadium last season.

3 Savinho could leave City this summer amidst renewed speculation surrounding a move to Spurs

3 And City may look to replace Savinho with Chelsea star Neto

Spurs are keen on the Brazilian and Liverpool's Cody Gakpo as they seek to bolster their attacking options.

Neto is also a rumoured target for Roberto De Zerbi's side, though their priority at this stage appears to be Savinho.

The north London outfit have been monitoring the former Girona man for the past 12 months and will hope to secure his services this summer.

And City are interested in Chelsea and Portugal star Neto should the 22-year-old leave the Etihad Stadium.

Neto and new City boss Enzo Maresca worked together during their time at Stamford Bridge.

The 26-year-old has started 54 league matches since his £54million arrival from Wolves in 2024.

In his two years in west London, Neto's been directly involved in 21 goals, scoring nine times.

However, the Portuguese forward may find minutes hard to come by under new Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso in the upcoming campaign.

Chelsea's failure to secure a European finish combined with the £117million addition of Morgan Rogers could see Neto restricted to a bit-part role.

3 Morgan Rogers' arrival could push Neto towards the Stamford Bridge exit Credit: Getty

Back of the Net-o

City may face competition for Neto should Chelsea sanction his summer sale.

Premier League rivals Liverpool have been linked with a move for Neto as the Reds consider their options in their quest to replace Mohamed Salah.

Salah confirmed he'll be leaving Liverpool at the end of the season earlier this year, though the Merseyside outfit are yet to sign a new right winger.

In addition, Serie A giants AC Milan are also believed to be keeping tabs on Neto with a view to a summer move.

Neto's compatriot Ruben Amorim took over as AC Milan boss back in June following Max Allegri's departure after the Italian side failed to secure a Champions League finish.

Sports.title: Manchester United player closes in on Middlesbrough transfer
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough are closing in on the permanent signing of Manchester United goalkeeper Radek Vitek, talkSPORT understands.

Vitek enjoyed a productive loan spell with Championship side Bristol City last season.

2 Vitek impressed during a loan spell with Championship side Bristol City last season Credit: Getty

The 22-year-old kept 12 clean sheets in England's second tier last term, the fifth most in the division as the Robins finished 12th.

Vitek is now close to a permanent switch to the Riverside Stadium to provide cover and competition for Sol Brynn.

The move to Boro brings the curtain down on a six-year spell at Old Trafford.

The Czech stopper joined the United academy from Sigma Olomouc in his homeland in 2020, though failed to make a single appearance for United.

Karl Darlow's arrival from Leeds United pushed Vitek further down the goalkeeping pecking order for Michael Carrick's men.

'I hope there is interest'

And the young goalkeeper admitted during pre-season that he is ready to leave United in search of regular action.

Speaking after a second-half appearance during United's 1-0 pre-season defeat to Wrexham in Helsinki, Vitek said: "I feel great and ready to go again somewhere to hopefully be number one.

"I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when the things are more concrete."

When asked whether he'd hope for another loan or a permanent exit, he replied: "I'm ready for both to be fair.

2 Vitek has dropped down the Manchester United pecking order following Darlow's arrival Credit: Getty

"It depends on what the club wants and also depends on the options and, yeah, we'll see.

"There's been a few interests on the table, but we're hoping to get the best one and hopefully it will happen soon.

"I want to play every week and that's the goal for next season. Hopefully I find out soon where that's going to be."

Man Utd's summer business

Vitek will become the club's second high-profile sale of the summer after Rasmus Hojlund's loan move to Napoli was made permanent.

Casemiro left Old Trafford for MLS powerhouse Inter Miami, while Jadon Sancho and Tyrell Malacia departed after their respective contracts expired.

United have brought in Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans from Chelsea and Aston Villa, respectively, to ease Casemiro's exit.

Darlow, meanwhile, joined after his Leeds contract expired, and arrives as cover for first-choice shotstopper Senne Lammens.

Sports.title: Six Premier League clubs handed relegation warning with promoted teams for new season
Sports.content:
Six Premier League clubs handed relegation warning with promoted teams for new season

Premier League football returns this month and the relegation battle could be bigger than ever.

talkSPORT Breakfast hosts Jeff Stelling and Gabby Agbonlahor went through a list of teams that they believe could be contenders for the drop in the 2026/27 season.

8 Coventry and Ipswich will hope to avoid an immediate drop back to the Championship Credit: Getty

8 Hull will also be desperate to secure their status in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Coventry City, Ipswich Town and Hull City are the trio who earned promotion from the Championship to the top flight last season.

Typically, promoted sides find Premier League football too much to handle and head back down to the second tier a year later.

And even though Sunderland and Leeds United secured safety last season, Coventry, Ipswich and Hull will all be tipped to battle at the bottom end of the table.

But when discussing the fight against relegation, Stelling offered some hope for the Premier League newbies.

Who are talkSPORT's relegation candidates?

"The encouragement for all of those three promoted sides is there are going to be other candidates," he claimed, before hinting that Crystal Palace, Fulham, Sunderland and Brentford are at risk.

"Palace. New manager (Pierre Sage), they've sold (Maxence) Lacroix, no signings (other than Oscar Mingueza) through the door.

"Fulham. Unproven manager (Alvaro Arbeloa), they've lost (Raul) Jimenez, (Harry) Wilson, (Issa) Diop, (Samuel) Chukwueze.

"Sunderland. Brilliant season last season, can they cope with that second season syndrome, plus Europe?

"Brentford. Just because they're Brentford, to be brutally honest."

Agbonlahor then explained: "I think Fulham is one that scares me. If I'm a Fulham fan, I look at Marco Silva, he got that extra percentage from all those players.

8 Stelling and Agbonlahor are unsure about the future of Palace under Sage Credit: Getty

8 Fulham are another club to be tipped for a potential relegation battle Credit: Getty

8 Sunderland could find it hard to juggle Europa League and Premier League football Credit: Getty

"Like you said, Jimenez, Wilson, Diop, Chukwueze gone as well. New manager, what has he really done? Struggled when he came in at Real Madrid.

"He's signed two players, (Gonzalo) Garcia and (Cesar) Palacios. Garcia got six goals in 30 appearances last season in LaLiga. Palacios, five appearances, zero goals. A combined fee of £42million for both of them.

"LaLiga is different to the Premier League, it's going to be really tough for those players, we'll see how they get on with a physical league like the Premier League.

"New manager as well, a lot of the unknown with Arbeloa, so you can see it, they might struggle."

"You can say the same about Bournemouth, can't you?" Stelling said. "New manager (Marco Rose) there, and I mentioned Sunderland have got European football, but so have Bournemouth.

"Over the last couple of seasons, so many have left and this time round they've lost (Marcos) Senesi, (Eli Junior) Kroupi is out for a while, they may yet lose Alex Scott because there'll be so many admirers for him. You wonder how they will cope with all of that."

8 According to Stelling, Brentford are candidates - simply because they're Brentford Credit: Getty

8 Bournemouth are also at risk of going back down to the Championship Credit: Getty

"European football, a couple of injuries, and the squad is starting to look thin," Agbonlahor added. "You've got a game on Thursday and you travel back, and you've got a tough game on the Sunday.

"Sometimes, European football can be a bad thing. It was Burnley, wasn't it? They struggled with European football (Europa League) and the Premier League (in the 2018/29 season)."

Stelling then asked: "How do you think Newcastle are going to do?"

"I think they'll be down there," Agbonlahor claimed. "I don't see them having a season as bad as Tottenham over the last two seasons, but I don't see them in the top half, nowhere near.

"I feel that, that fanbase are angry, they're angry at what's happening with their football club. They're angry at losing all of their players, signing young players...

"They were all dressed in Saudi Arabian attire when the owners came in. They were thinking, 'Yes, we're going to go for (Kylian) Mbappe, we're going to get Neymar, we're going to get all these big players'.

"Now, there's no European football this season, just lost their manager. They've brought in a manager (Matthias Jaissle) who's managed in the Saudi league.

"It could start to turn a bit toxic there, if they start to lose a few of their early games. Joelinton's wanting to get out as well, this isn't what Newcastle fans thought was going to happen, did they?"

8 Agbonlahor believes Newcastle could become toxic in the new season Credit: Getty

"Let's not forget, as much as the problems with the Financial Fair Play rules and they've lost this player, that player, they didn't buy well last summer," he added.

"(Nick) Woltemade, (Yoane) Wissa, (Anthony) Elanga, over £160million for those three players, none of them produced last season. They've got to step up, all three of them, because Wissa looked very sharp for DR Congo at the World Cup, can he bring that form into next season?

"Jacob Ramsey is probably the only one who had a decent season last season, so those three signings have to step up."

Stelling then wanted to poke fun at Tottenham Hotspur, who finished 17th in the past two seasons to narrowly avoid relegation.

"Of course, we're talking about relegation. Well, you can never leave Spurs out of the equation, can you?"

However, to avoid the potential wrath from Spurs fans, he insisted: "I'm only joking!"

The 2026/27 Premier League season gets underway on Friday, August 21 when Arsenal host Coventry, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest explore shock move for Man City star as Lucas Bergvall alternative
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest are interested in Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders, talkSPORT understands.

Forest are out to strengthen in the middle of the park following Elliot Anderson's club-record £116million move to City last month.

2 Reijnders struggled for minutes in the second half of last season Credit: Getty

And they are considering a move for Reijnders as they look to add bodies in the middle of the park.

The Dutchman only joined the Manchester giants from Italian side AC Milan last year.

Reijnders enjoyed a promising start to life at the Etihad Stadium, scoring once and assisting another in a 4-0 win against Wolves on his Premier League debut.

However, the 28-year-old's game time dipped in the second half of the season as he made just two league starts between the start of February and the end of the campaign.

Despite the departure of Bernardo Silva and potential exit of Real Madrid target Rodri, City could be open to selling Reijnders as a result of the capture of Anderson and impending arrival of Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Even so, the Netherlands international joined the first-team squad for their pre-season tour of Asia.

Latest on Bergvall

Interest in Reijnders comes with Forest exploring other options to Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall.

talkSPORT understands that Bergvall had informed Spurs chiefs of his desire to leave the club this summer in pursuit of regular action.

2 Forest have cooled their interest in Spurs midfielder Lucas Bergvall

The Tricky Trees have seen at least one bid worth £38million rebuffed with the north London side keen to retain the 20-year-old Swede's services.

During the club's pre-season tour of New Zealand and Australia, head coach Roberto De Zerbi admitted that he made mistakes with how he handled Bergvall in the final knockings of the 2025/26 season.

Spurs beat the drop on the final day of the campaign and while the capital outfit are keen to retain the midfielder's services, the Italian reiterated that he will not stand in the way of players that wish to leave.

"I'm always being very clear with him and with you. I would like that he stays with us," De Zerbi said when asked about Bergvall's future.

"I think he's potentially a top, top, top player. But then I don't want to convince anyone to stay.

"Tottenham is already, without me, a top club and we are not to convince anyone to stay.

"He can find the space if he stays with us. The competition within the players will be very strong because we are Tottenham and we have to build a strong squad - not just 11 players - especially considering a lot of injuries we suffered in the last two, three seasons.

"Football is going in a clear direction – to compete for the highest places in the table, you have to manage 22, 23, 24 players. I don't want 24, but 21, 22 of a high level."

Spurs have strengthened their midfield with the additions of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, the duo replacing the outgoing Joao Palhinha and Yves Bissouma.

And with no European football on offer in north London this season, Bergvall may find playing time hard to come by.

Sports.title: US cities chasing FIFA for millions in ‘unpaid’ contributions in fresh blow to Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Host cities were 'repeatedly assured' by FIFA of legacy contributions, but millions of dollars remain unpaid

US cities chasing FIFA for millions in ‘unpaid’ contributions in fresh blow to Gianni Infantino

World Cup host cities across the United States are chasing FIFA for 'millions of dollars' they believe they were promised for the 2026 tournament.

Gianni Infantino announced last year that football's governing body would make a contribution of $1 million to each of the 11 cities that were hosting matches during the Club World Cup competition.

3 World Cup host cities are chasing FIFA over unpaid contributions Credit: AFP

That money was described as a 'legacy contribution' -- with funds to be used to build mini-pitches, and support 'social projects' in each area.

After Infantino’s initial announcement, the American cities scheduled to host World Cup games in 2026 asked if they would receive the same contribution for the more substantial task of hosting multiple games across the international tournament.

The Athletic reports that FIFA management 'repeatedly assured' that cities would receive the same $1m contribution towards legacy, despite no public statement.

Executives told the outlet that the promise was made 'verbally' by members of senior management, and 'reiterated' in meetings.

However, that money has not been paid, and several cities are now asking FIFA staff for updates on the payments.

World Cup games were hosted in Atlanta, Boston, Dallas, Houston, Kansas City, Los Angeles, New York and New Jersey, Miami, Philadelphia, San Francisco and Seattle across 39 days this summer.

Two of those host cities told The Athletic that it has been 'difficult to understand' why FIFA would be stalling or non-committal on what are described as 'relatively minor' payments, given the organization celebrated revenues in excess of $15 billion between 2023 and 2026, and had an operating budget of around $2.7bn for the 2026 tournament.

"The challenge is exacerbated for the cities as some of the host committees are now winding up operations following the tournament, meaning it is not easy to work out the vehicle which would now be best placed to benefit from the payments," the report read.

"Others are seeking to draw up financial reports to their jurisdictions and authorities but do not have certainty over whether to include the payments."

Unpaid payments add another layer of controversy for FIFA and its embattled president in the wake of the World Cup.

3 News of FIFA's unpaid contributions is a fresh blow for embattled Infantino Credit: AFP

Infantino is already facing a rebellion over his plans to sell off stakes in competitions to private investors, which have been scrapped.

In recent days, opponents of the president are threatening 'non co-operation' with the body unless he steps down.

How much did US cities pay to host the World Cup?

While the World Cup boosted tourism across the US this summer, host city committees were tasked with organising security, transport, fan events beyond each game day.

The Financial Times reported last month that New York and New Jersey predicted around $3.3bn of economic activity would be generated, while California’s Bay Area hoped the combined impact of football games, as well as last year’s NBA All-Star Game and February's Super Bowl LX, would be $1.4bn.

However, doubts have since been raised over the economic windfall for each city.

American taxpayers contributed hugely to the costs of the 2026 tournament, with the Kansas City host committee revealing to The Athletic that it received a total public investment of $86.8m.

3 Kansas City's host committee has revealed the cost of hosting World Cup games Credit: Getty

Nearly $75m more was also handed out in federal security assistance and in federal grants for transportation.

Private donations, which remain undisclosed, were also received

A $1m legacy contribution for each host city would appear a drop in the water compared to those massive numbers, but remains an incentive yet to be paid.

Sports.title: Premier League wonderkid tipped to have better career than Yan Diomande
Sports.content:
Premier League wonderkid tipped to have better career than Yan Diomande

Liverpool starlet Rio Ngumoha has been tipped to eclipse Yan Diomande on the road to superstardom.

The 17-year-old's stock has constantly risen since he enjoyed an unforgettable Premier League debut against Newcastle last August.

3 Liverpool haven't signed Diomande but they may have a better young winger already on their books Credit: Getty

Ngumoha scored what proved to be the winner in the tenth minute of stoppage time in the second half, making him the youngest goalscorer in club history at 16 years old.

The whiz-kid rewrote Liverpool's record books less than a month later when he became the club's youngest-ever player to feature in the Champions League.

Ngumoha capped off his debut season of dreams by earning a call-up to England's pre-World Cup camp, as several of the stars who made the 26-man squad did not link up until later due to their lengthy seasons.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel chose to let Ngumoha loose in the friendly against New Zealand and he certainly caught the eye, earning player of the match honours for his second half display.

In fact, talkSPORT's legendary broadcaster Adrian Durham labelled Ngumoha England's 'best right winger', which was a bold verdict given the teen predominantly featured on the left flank for Liverpool.

Ngumoha will be 'an absolute sensation'

Regardless, Ngumoha's bright displays had Peterborough United chairman and Liverpool fan Darragh MacAnthony waxing lyrical about his potential on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"He (Ngumoha) will be a sensation this year," MacAnthony said.

"I'll make a prediction that he'll win Young Player of the Year in the Premier League, without a doubt.

"I'm probably more confident because of him and because he can play left and right side."

But MacAnthony wasn't done there when it came to predicting Ngumoha's future.

3 Ngumoha got a taste of international football in June and looked comfortable at the level Credit: Getty

In the next breath, he boldly claimed Ngumoha would enjoy a 'better career' than RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande.

Diomande is poised to join Real Madrid this summer, but the deal still has some final details to iron out.

Although Diomande is likely to command a transfer fee in the region of nine figures, MacAnthony still believes Ngumoha will prove to be superior.

"You talk about Diomande and the money that's been talked around him, I'd even debate and argue that Rio will have a better career than him, in my opinion," MacAnthony said.

"I think he's going to be an absolute sensation."

Give me Moha

The 2026/27 campaign is shaping up as a major one for Ngumoha, especially given the Mohamed Salah-sized hole on the right wing.

3 Salah made the right wing position his own for nine years at Liverpool Credit: Getty

Salah chose to leave the Reds at the end of last season, bringing the curtain down on his legendary Anfield career which included over 250 goals and seven trophies.

Liverpool have already taken steps to address their shallow depth in the attacking areas earlier this window, signing Spain international Victor Munoz from Osasuna.

But with a few weeks remaining before the window slams shut, there may be more major incomings at Anfield.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino accused of ‘blackmail’ in damning statement from president of Jordan FA
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino accused of ‘blackmail’ in damning statement from president of Jordan FA

Gianni Infantino has been accused of 'blackmail' by the president of the Jordan Football Association (JFA) in an explosive statement.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein has hit out at the pressure placed on his FA to endorse Infantino's re-election campaign.



4 This is the latest controversy involving the under-fire FIFA president's name Credit: Getty

The FIFA president is under mounting pressure following his failed move to launch the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

His scrapped plans would have introduced the sale of private equity in FIFA events, including the World Cup.

Infantino has since shelved the plans after widespread condemnation and threats of tournament boycotts.



The FAs of both England and Wales have also withdrawn their support for his re-election bid.

Whilst UEFA have called for a blanket withdrawal, Prince Ali has now claimed FIFA refused to help with matters during the World Cup unless his FA endorsed Infantino.



In a statement, he cited issues with obtaining visas for supporters, taxes from the US government and prize money from the 2025 FIFA Arab Cup, where they finished as runners-up.

'Amounts to blackmail'

Taking to X, Prince Ali wrote: "There is no shortage of issues regarding FIFA.



"Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time.

"We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

"First, getting our fans into the USA, not all were granted visas, even though they had tickets, which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

4 Prince Ali claims FIFA refused to help Jordan during the World Cup unless they endorsed Infantino Credit: Getty



"Secondly, we are being taxed by the US government through FIFA for our participation. Money that should go to players and staff.

"This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico, but we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

"Thirdly, we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a FIFA event.

"The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve.



"It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters, until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

"We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now, but the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that."

4 Jordan made their World Cup debut in North America this summer Credit: Getty

Jordan's World Cup debut

Jordan made their first-ever World Cup appearance in North America this summer.



Having been drawn in group J, they faced Austria, Algeria and defending champions Argentina.

Although Jordan scored in all three of their matches, they ended the group stage without a single point and were eliminated in fourth place.

Each of those fixtures were played in the USA, with matches two matches in Santa Clara before their loss to Argentina in Dallas.

Meanwhile, as explained by Prince Ali, Jordan were based in Portland, Oregon throughout the tournament.



The national team subsequently trained at Merlo Field, the home of the University of Portland Pilots football team.

4 Prince Ali ran against Infantino in the 2016 FIFA presidential election Credit: Getty

Who is Prince Ali bin Al Hussein?

Prince Ali previously ran against Infantino in the 2016 FIFA presidential election, but finished third with just four votes in round two.

He had previously lost to Sepp Blatter in the 2015 election.

As well as his role as JFA president, Prince Ali is also the founder and president of the West Asian Football Federation.



The governing body currently has 12 member nations, including fellow 2026 World Cup participants Iraq, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands surprise new job just two weeks after retiring
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands surprise new job just two weeks after retiring

Anthony Taylor has landed a new role with the Turkish Football Federation two weeks after retiring from refereeing.

The former Premier League official confirmed he was hanging up his whistle following the World Cup.

3 Taylor has landed a new job two weeks after retiring as a referee Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Taylor took charge of three matches at the tournament, with his last being Spain's 1-0 win over Portugal in the round of 16.

Following a 24-year refereeing career, he announced he was retiring just days after the World Cup final.

New role

The 47-year-old has now revealed he has started a consultancy role with the Turkish Football Federation (TFF).

Taylor has been appointed as their new director of elite refereeing.

Confirming the news in a LinkedIn post, he wrote: "Following my recent announcement that I am retiring from elite refereeing after 16 seasons, I am pleased to share the next step in my career.

"From today, I will take up the consultancy role - ‘Director of Elite Refereeing’, with the Turkish Football Federation.

"Having officiated at the highest levels of domestic and international football, I welcome the opportunity to bring that experience to a role focused on the strategic and technical development of elite refereeing in Türkiye.

"I will work with colleagues across the Federation to support the continued development of its match officials and strengthen the wider refereeing programme, in line with UEFA and FIFA standards."

Taylor's arrival comes less than a year after the TFF was rocked by a referee betting scandal in October 2025.

The Football Federation found that professional referees were engaging in widespread gambling on football.

3 Taylor announced his retirement after the World Cup but has now joined the TFF Credit: Getty

It was discovered that 371 out of 571 active officials held betting accounts, whilst 152 of those were breaching FIFA and UEFA rules by betting on matches.

As part of plans to rebuild their reputation, the TFF subsequently revealed plans for a nationwide referee training programme.

Taylor's refereeing career

Taylor now joins the TFF to oversee their elite refereeing division.

Turkey did not have a single official present at this summer's World Cup.

Meanwhile, Taylor's involvement marked his second successive appearance at the finals.

Having started his refereeing career in 2002, he later became a FIFA referee in 2013.

3 Taylor enjoyed a 16-year refereeing career in the Premier League Credit: Getty

It came three years after he had first officiated in the Premier League, with Taylor amassing 433 matches during 16 years in the top-flight.

He also officiated two FA Cup finals as well as the final of the Europa League. He also refereed at the Club World Cup and Nations League during his career.

Sports.title: Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino is accused of BLACKMAIL by head of Jordan FA in extraordinary statement
Sports.content:
Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein has accused Gianni Infantino of blackmail as pressure continues to mount on the FIFA president.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes leaked last week.

The Swiss football administrator has since scrapped the proposals after widespread opposition - including an internal rebellion at FIFA.

UEFA and Concacaf - the body for North and Central America and the Caribbean - are both calling for Infantino to step down, with Europe declaring a lack of confidence in the FIFA president.

Jordan, meanwhile, are the first Asian nation to rebel against Infantino - taking the total to 91, assuming all UEFA and CONCACAF nations follow the stance set by their continental bodies. 106 nations are needed to depose Infantino as president.

In a statement Hussein ripped into Infantino, accusing him of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term at the helm of world football.

Gianni Infantino has been accused of blackmail by Jordan FA president Prince Ali bin Hussein

Hussein ripped into Infantino, accusing him of delaying prize money payments and refusing to address the problem unless Jordan endorsed him for a fourth term at the helm of world football

‘There is no shortage of issues regarding FIFA. Let me start by clarifying what some of these are from an FA perspective, in particular that of Jordan going into a World Cup for the first time,’ Hussein said

‘We are a small country with a minimal budget for our FA and had to deal with enormous hurdles.

‘First, getting our fans into the USA: not all were granted VISAS, even though they had tickets - which we also know were sold at exorbitant prices.

‘Secondly, we are being taxed by the US government through FIFA for our participation. Money that should go to players and staff.

‘This was not the case for those who played and set up camp in Canada and Mexico. But we happened to be in the USA so now we face these huge costs in taxes for having participated.

‘Thirdly we have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a FIFA event.

‘The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

‘It is clear the problem really is with leadership. For months, FIFA has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters - until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

‘We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

‘But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.’

Daily Mail Sport have contacted FIFA for comment.

Sports.title: Man United admit controversial ticket touting clampdown has caused 'distress' to supporters
Sports.content:
Man United admit controversial ticket touting clampdown has caused 'distress' to supporters

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have admitted that the club’s controversial crackdown on ticket touting has caused ‘distress’ to fans who feel as though they have been ‘treated harshly’.

United took action last month, notifying thousands of supporters – including one as young as six-years-old – that their accounts had been suspended due to suspicious activity and their season tickets could be revoked unless they provided a satisfactory explanation.

But the club now accept that they ‘underestimated’ just how many fans shared accounts and passwords, leading to them being investigated.

United have come under fire over the purge, with a number of groups including The ’58, Manchester United Supporters’ Trust and The Red Army issuing a joint statement accusing the club of making fans feel as though they are being ‘treated as suspects’ and urging more leniency. Last week’s Fans’ Forum also gave fan representatives an opportunity to confront United directly.

By bringing in an external agency using automated monitoring to find any trace of touting, United have been criticised for casting the net too wide and targeting innocent fans.

While the club has acknowledged that ‘a satisfactory explanation’ had been given in a ‘substantial number of cases’, it also justified the clampdown by saying it has ‘uncovered significant and organised touting’ – including one instance where 1,088 accounts were accessed off a single device.

Man United have admitted 'distress' has been caused to fans after their controversial crackdown on ticket touting - pictured is co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe

The statement read: ‘Thank you to the many supporters, fan representatives and supporter organisations who have shared their views with us over recent weeks.

‘Our intention throughout this process is a simple one; to protect fair access to tickets for genuine Manchester United supporters and to tackle organised ticket touting and abuse of the ticketing system.

‘We also intend to share the findings and supporting data once the process is concluded, allowing us to present the full picture. However, we also accept the importance of being as transparent as possible during the process, and we would therefore like to provide additional context at this stage.

‘We have listened carefully to the feedback we have received, both through formal meetings and through the many conversations, emails and calls that have taken place. We know that this issue has caused significant concern and distress for some supporters.

‘There is no doubt at all that this process has uncovered significant and organised touting which will enable us to remove tickets from touts and place them back in the hands of genuine fans. We believe this is something we are all aligned on.

‘One example has uncovered 1,088 accounts accessed on a single device. However, we recognise that the way this process was communicated, and the impact it has had on some loyal match-going supporters, has caused genuine upset and distress.

‘We also recognise that some supporters who saw their actions as legitimate and have not made any financial gain from tickets may have felt that they were being treated harshly.

‘We understand deeply the relationship between a supporter and their season ticket and that removing that bond should be reserved for serious breaches. In this process, we intend to reserve the most severe sanctions for cases where the evidence indicates organised touting, systematic misuse or activity for financial gain.

‘Where this is not indicated, season tickets will not be cancelled. Any season ticket which is cancelled will be offered to a supporter on the waiting list, as a season ticket.’

Sports.title: Christian Norgaard heading for Everton medical, Chelsea close in on Rayo Vallecano defender Pep Chavarria... and Man City step up interest in £65m Pedro Neto: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Christian Norgaard heading for Everton medical, Chelsea close in on Rayo Vallecano defender Pep Chavarria... and Man City step up interest in £65m Pedro Neto: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fulham lodge new £25m bid for Saints star

Fulham have made a revised £25million offer for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

The Championship side rejected Fulham's first bid for the Northern Ireland international but the Cottagers have improved their proposal with add-ons on top.

Fresh from signing £46million Real Madrid duo Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, manager Alvaro Arbeloa wants Fulham to strengthen further with the former Manchester City midfielder.

Fulham have made a revised £25million offer for Southampton midfielder Shea Charles

Leeds United walked away from talks for Charles last month after making what they felt were reasonable offers for the 22-year-old.

Southampton have been digging in their heels pushing for £30m but Charles wants to go for the chance to play in the Premier League which he missed out on in May.

Fulham remain talks to add Thiago Pitarch from Real Madrid too.

Hull move for Norway youth star

Hull City are finalising a £7million deal for 20-year-old Norwegian midfielder Jens Hjerto-Dahl from Tromso.

The U21 international set off for England this morning ahead of his medical and agreeing terms.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Sunday, Hull have beaten off competition from Rangers and Cardiff City.

Ipswich target Brazilian centre back

Ipswich Town are interested in Real Betis centre back Natan.

The 25-year-old joined from Napoli last season and was on the brink of making Carlo Ancelotti's World Cup squad but ultimately missed out.

Ipswich Town are interested in Real Betis's 25-year-old Braziliann centre back Natan.

Ipswich, meanwhile have signed midfielder Florentino from Burnley on a five-year contract.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the fee is an initial £16m plus a further £3m in add-ons.

Hull City had been in advanced talks over an initial loan for the 26-year-old.

Palace swoop for teenage US defender

Crystal Palace are closing on an £11million deal for Real Salt Lake wing-back Zavier Gozo.

Sports.title: Stacey King cause of death revealed: Medical report details why NBA legend suffered tragic fall at his Chicago home
Sports.content:
NBA legend Stacey King died from a heart disease caused by high blood pressure at his home in Chicago, it has been revealed.

King, a three-time NBA champion with the Chicago Bulls and beloved TV broadcaster for the franchise, passed away at the age of 59 on June 7, with his death sending shockwaves across the sporting world.

Shortly after the heartbreaking announcement, ESPN Chicago's David Kaplan reported that the Bulls great had died after a 'fall at his home' in the suburb of River Forest.

Yet according to the California Post, a spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has revealed that King died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease - which is caused by long-term high blood pressure.

Obesity is also said to be a factor in the disease and the manner of his passing was natural, the spokesperson added.

King was a foundational piece of the Bulls' 1990s dominance, entering the NBA as the sixth overall pick in the 1989 Draft. He stayed with the franchise during their most dominant period, before joining the Minnesota Timberwolves from the 1993–94 campaign.

NBA legend Stacey King died from a heart disease caused by high blood pressure on June 7

King (21) won three NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls alongside teammate Michael Jordan

The Oklahoma-born star played eight seasons in the league, anchoring the paint alongside Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen during the Bulls' historic 1991, 1992 and 1993 championship runs.

While his playing career cemented his place in Chicago folklore, King later found a new generation of fans in his post-playing career - as a commentator for Bulls TV broadcasts.

Tributes quickly poured in from devastated fans online, who mourned the tragic loss of a team icon.

In a statement, Bulls owner Jerry Reinsdorf said: 'Stacey King was a cherished member of the Bulls family and one of the truly unique personalities in our organization's history.

'His connection to Chicago, the Bulls and our fans spanned more than three decades - first as a player and later as the unmistakable voice that helped bring Bulls basketball into the homes of generations of fans.

'We will miss him deeply and remember the joy, energy, humor, candor, and passion he brought to our organization, our broadcasts, and our fans every day. Our thoughts are with his family and loved ones.'

While his playing career cemented his place in Chicago folklore, he found a new generation of fans in his post-playing career as a commentator for Bulls TV broadcasts

Meanwhile, team president and COO Michael Reinsdorf said: 'Stacey loved being a Bull. You could feel it in everything he did - the way he played, the way he called games, and the way he connected with our fans.

'He had a unique gift for bringing people together and making every game feel personal. Whether it was through a broadcast, a conversation, or a photo with a fan, Stacey made people feel seen and valued.

'We were fortunate to know him not only as a player and broadcaster, but as a friend. Stacey genuinely cared about people, and he made our organization better.

'We will miss him dearly, and his impact, memory and legacy will remain a part of the Chicago Bulls forever.'

Sports.title: Immigration probe launched over 'missing' Ugandan boxers who have not returned home from Glasgow's Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Immigration probe launched over 'missing' Ugandan boxers who have not returned home from Glasgow's Commonwealth Games

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Four Ugandan boxers have gone missing after competing in the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

The sporting news website NBS Sport said that members of the team did not rejoin the delegation before their scheduled return on Tuesday.

The athletes, Angel Katushabe, Nuhu Batte, Ibrahim Khemis and Emily Nakalema, were part of a six-member boxing team at the games.

Speaking anonymously to NBS Sport, one of the athletes admitted that they intended to seek asylum in the UK.

The boxer said they wanted to continue their careers in a country with better training facilities and opportunities.

They asked not to be judged by the Ugandan public for the decision.

A Police Scotland spokesman said: 'Police Scotland has received reports of several athletes who are unaccounted for.

'Inquiries are ongoing to assess the circumstances, and early engagement is taking place with the Home Office.'

Emily Nakalema is one of the four athletes who 'went missing' after the Games finished

Nuhu Batte also did not rejoin his teammates ahead of their departure from Glasgow

Ibrahim Khemis (blue) is another of the boxing team who did not report back to Uganda

Angel Katushabe is also missing following the closing ceremony of the Commonwealth Games

Speaking to the Press Association on Monday, Commonwealth Games chief executive Phil Batty said: 'We've welcomed nearly 3,000 athletes to the city from 74 nations.

'We want to deliver a safe and secure games, so we work really closely with Police Scotland, the Border Force, and UK visas and immigration to make sure everyone arrives and departs in line with regulation.'

The Press Association understands that the Home Office will take action accordingly if it is made aware of any breaches of immigration law, and that it takes all necessary steps to prevent people who could abuse the immigration system from entering the UK.

The Home Office maintains a policy of not routinely commenting on individual asylum cases.

Around 400 foreign athletes and officials have gone AWOL in the last six Commonwealth Games – three of which have been held in the UK, according to The Sun.

In Manchester 2002, 27 athletes were unaccounted for, including 21 from Sierra Leone, four Bangladeshi runners and a swimmer from Pakistan.

In Glasgow in 2014, 66 athletes fled, including two Ugandan rugby players.

And in Birmingham in 2022, 17 athletes outstayed their welcome, including two Pakistani boxers who went on the run.

The Ugandan Ministry of Education and Sports has been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Trump's golf rival reveals new details about president's latest 'win' after he declared huge victory in New Jersey club championship
Sports.content:
Trump's golf rival reveals new details about president's latest 'win' after he declared huge victory in New Jersey club championship

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

New details have emerged around Donald Trump's latest golf victory in New Jersey, including that he was playing with a barely believable handicap.

The president added two more trophies to his growing collection after winning both the club and senior championships at Trump National Golf Club Bedminster last weekend.

Trump, 80, carded an improbably low two-under-par score of 70, bringing his reported tally to over 40 total victories across his various golf properties.

Footage of the scoreboard after the competition had concluded was posted on Instagram by another competitor, Philip Zamloot, on Tuesday.

It showed that Zamloot and Trump had in fact shot the same net score of 70 during their respective rounds. In golf, a player's net score is their total number of strokes minus their handicap.

But the clip showed Trump actually carded a gross score of 70 as well, adding a fresh layer of doubt to his victory.

Footage of the scorecard shows Donald Trump won his recent golf tournaments with a barely believable handicap

Trump won both the club and senior championships at his course in New Jersey last weekend

That gross score means Trump was playing to a handicap of zero, which is a level only reached by extremely talented players.

Zamloot wrote over the video: '70 net scores... Trump and Zamloot... true grit... true winners.'

He captioned the video: 'President Trump and myself both had net scores of 70 at the senior club championships on Saturday. Proud to be on the same leaderboard and same net score as the president of the greatest country in the world.'

Social media footage showed the US President receiving a round of applause in front of the club leaderboard following the round, with a caption confirming he had collected two trophies for his performance.

The par at Bedminster is set at 72, meaning Trump allegedly finished two strokes under par to secure the double victory.

Trump eagerly shared footage of his crowning moment during the tournament, too.

'The Winning Shot in the Bedminster Club Championship!' Trump wrote on social media alongside video of him lifting his ball to within a few feet of the pin. 'Thank you very much to all of those who participated.'

'I won with a score of 70, and am so honored in that, unlike the rest of the field, I'm given very little time to practice, because I'm focused on many other things,' he wrote.

Trump eagerly shared footage from his latest golfing triumph at his course in New Jersey

Trump allegedly just won his 43rd Club Championship today at one of his courses. pic.twitter.com/8Lb8GFvnY0 — Ron Filipkowski (@RonFilipkowski) August 2, 2026

'It's called TALENT, and I have it, and they don't!'

The reported 70 comes a year after the White House published a scorecard claiming Trump had carded a 3-under 69 at the same annual tournament in 2025 to win by 10 gross strokes.

However, his remarkable track record and reported scores have frequently drawn skepticism from critics and sports journalists over the years.

Sportswriter Rick Reilly, who authored a book on Trump's golf habits, has previously questioned the legitimacy of his club championship wins, once stating: 'When it comes to cheating, he's an 11 on a scale of one to 10.'

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho is forced off injured in just his second Aston Villa match since sealing acrimonious Chelsea departure
Sports.content:
Aston Villa forward Alejandro Garnacho left the field injured in just his second game for the club after joining from Chelsea.

Former Manchester United man Garnacho has moved to Villa Park on a year-long loan, and sources say the conditions are easily achievable and the total package meets the Blues' initial £43million valuation of the player.

But he has got his career with his new side off to a nightmare start, being substituted injured in the first-half against BG Pathum in Thailand during Villa's pre-season tour.

Having made his debut against the Indonesia All Stars last week, he was hoping to kick on but had to be replaced after being fouled by Ryan Edwards.

He needed medical treatment on the field, and made way with what was understood to be a facial injury.

Villa won the game 3-1, but also lost captain John McGinn to injury after he hurt his knee.

Alejandro Garnacho was taken off injured in just his second game after joining Aston Villa

The winger is hoping to reboot his career again after leaving Chelsea for Villa Park

Emi Buendia, Victor Lindelof and Boubacar Kamara were on the scoresheet for Unai Emery's men.

Garnacho had previously been of interest to Villa before he left Man United last summer for the Blues.

The Argentine winger played 43 matches for Chelsea last season in all competitions, but missed out on a spot at the World Cup.

Garnacho featured 24 times in the Premier League for the Blues, scoring one goal and providing three assists.

He scored eight times in total for Chelsea, with half of his goals coming in the Carabao Cup.

He has struggled to nail down a starting spot since Ruben Amorim took over at Old Trafford but will be hoping life at Villa Park is a fresh start.

Emery is a big fan of the 22-year-old and is understood to have played a key role in the move.

Villa will face Borussia Monchengladbach and Bayern Munich in friendlies before kicking off their Premier League season away to Brighton.

They will also take on Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain in the Super Cup after winning the Europa League.

Sports.title: Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow
Sports.content:
Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow

Commonwealth Cup winner Venetian Sun has been ruled out for the rest of the season after trainer Karl Burke confirmed the sprinter has suffered a tendon injury

View 3 Images Tony Bloom (second left) with Venetian Sun, who followed up her success at Royal Ascot with a Group 1 victory in France (Image: PA)

Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine Venetian Sun has suffered an injury setback that will sideline her for the remainder of the campaign.

‌



Among last year's top juveniles, the lightning-quick daughter of Starman – owned by Brighton & Hove Albion chairman in partnership with Ian McAleavy – has maintained her brilliant form this season, claiming a second Royal Ascot triumph when storming to Commonwealth Cup glory.

‌



Her most recent outing saw her produce an excellent runner-up effort against older rivals at Newmarket in the July Cup, and she had been under consideration for a trip to France for this weekend's Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville, the venue where she captured the Prix Morny as a two-year-old.

‌



Rossa Ryan convinces BHA panel to reduce 28-day ban to 10 days at appeal hearing READ MORE :

Saffie Osborne to captain Ryan Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Shergar Cup at Ascot READ MORE :

Nevertheless, plans for the remainder of her three year old campaign have been shelved following the discovery of a tendon problem.

Her trainer Karl Burke said: "It's a big shame and unfortunately it happens. It's a long way from being a career- or life-threatening injury, but obviously is going to take time and it's very disappointing.

"We had more or less decided to swerve Deauville anyway because the ground was very fast out there last weekend with no sign of any rain and the French not watering like they used to do.

‌



View 3 Images Celebrations on the track after Venetian Sun's Royal Ascot victory (Image: Getty Images)

"It's just one of those things, we have a feeling she may have initiated it at Newmarket during the July Cup but she came back from there with a nasty little cut and she had been on antibiotics and anti-inflammatories and we think that may have masked it to a degree."

Venetian Sun has triumphed in six of her nine career starts to date, with her connections eagerly anticipating an autumn schedule that could have featured appearances in Haydock's Sprint Cup, at Ascot on British Champions Day and at the Breeders' Cup.

‌



Explaining the setback, Burke added: "It's basically a strain to the tendon, it happens a lot with jumping horses – it's unusual really at this stage in a sprinter's life, but can happen.

View 3 Images Venetian Sun sprinted to victory at Ascot (Image: Martin Dokoupil/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

"It's a time thing now and she will have the next six or seven months on the easy list and then be reassessed from there.

Article continues below

"The little bit of work she has done the last few days has just aggravated it and we've had the vets in this morning and they weren't 100 per cent happy with a little bit of heat in the leg and that is what it turns out to be.

"The plan before today was if she finished the season in good shape she would stay in training and that may still be the plan, but that is a discussion for later on."

Sports.title: Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part
Sports.content:
Harry Kane extending his Bayern stay is a no-brainer - and Ballon d'Or could play big part

The England captain will head back to his club in the next few days and Bayern will immediately resume talks over a new contract that will keep the striker in the Bundesliga beyond 2027

View 3 Images Harry Kane has had three very productive seasons with Bayern Munich (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Just over nine years ago, Harry Kane mildly surprised a small gathering of reporters when he declared winning the Ballon d’Or to be one of his prime ambitions. Nothing wrong with aiming high, of course. But, at the time, Kane was a 23-year-old striker who had made 17 appearances for his country and had scored five goals.

‌



His numbers with Spurs were very good - 78 goals in 113 Premier League appearances - but he had only been an established top-flight player for three seasons. But Kane believed in himself and lifting that Ballon d’Or is a realistic prospect when the awards ceremony, for the first time in its history, comes to London in October.

‌



Carabao Cup draw confirmed as final fixtures announced for round one READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Bookmakers do not normally get these sorts of things wrong and every odds-maker has Kane as the favourite to become the seventh British player to receive the accolade. The influence of the World Cup, though, should not be under-estimated.

‌



Some of the 100 journalists who make the choice could well forgive Rodri an injury-interrupted and otherwise mediocre season with his club for his imperious role in Spain’s summer triumph. Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe would appear to be the only other realistic contenders.

And they are worthy contenders. If Kane does not win the 2026 edition, he will have the award in his sights for next year - a year with no major international tournaments.

And if he stays at Bayern Munich, goals are a guarantee. In three seasons in Germany, he has 146 in 147 appearances. If he moved to Barcelona - a switch that seems slightly fanciful but has been mooted reasonably strongly - goals would be a guarantee.

‌



View 3 Images Rodri won the Ballon d'Or in 2024 and is a strong contender for this year's award (Image: Getty Images)

Kane is not coming back to the Premier League any time soon, we can be fairly certain of that. He will report back for training with Bayern after the Bundesliga champions have returned from a pre-season trip to Korea and Hong Kong on Saturday.

Contract talks will immediately resume, as his current deal expires in the summer of 2027. And quite frankly, it is hard to see why Kane would not want to extend his agreement.

‌



He could ask for a release clause at the end of next season if he feels he might have the urge to come back and break the Premier League goalscoring record - he is currently 47 short of Alan Shearer’s total of 260 - but he seems extremely content in Bavaria. Plus, the style of play, the quality of play, the guarantee of competing for honours on all fronts, are all factors that will help him stay in top shape for the international challenges that still lie ahead, most notably leading England into Euro 2028.

He turned 33 a week ago but Kane has looked a better, all-round player for his time in Munich. He was certainly more impressive for England at World Cup 2026 than he was at either Euro 2024 or World Cup 2022. He is not unusual but playing in a dominant team suits him.

View 3 Images Harry Kane has plenty of international challenges left despite his World Cup disappointment (Image: Getty Images)

‌



When he sits down with his advisers and the Bayern hierarchy in the next week, there will, of course, be no escaping the relevance of his age. But over the past few years, the longevity of marquee players - and of strikers, in particular - will have probably had a bearing on his plans.

Since his 34th birthday, Kane’s predecessor at Bayern, Robert Lewandowski, has scored 125 club goals. Kane could return to the Premier League as a 35-year-old - in two seasons’ time - and still fancy his chances of beating Shearer’s number.

But before then, he will have his eyes on another individual accolade. And if the Ballon d’Or does not come his way on the 70th anniversary of the award (the first one, in 1956, was won by Stanley Matthews, hence why the ceremony is in London), you can guarantee he will be a contender again if he stays at Bayern Munich. The Premier League and Shearer’s record are going to have to wait.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands new job in football following retirement
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee Anthony Taylor lands new job in football following retirement

Anthony Taylor called time on his refereeing career last month, but he's already found a new position that will see him take his wealth of experience as a match official abroad

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor retired after 20-year refereeing career (Image: Ayman Aref/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Anthony Taylor has landed a new job in football just weeks after announcing his retirement from professional refereeing. The former Premier League match official has been appointed the director of elite refereeing for the Turkish Football Federation (TFF).

‌



Taylor, 47, hung up his whistle after his last match at this summer's World Cup, taking charge of Spain's 1-0 win against Portugal in the round of 16. But now he's back in football with the TFF.

‌



"I am delighted to be joining the Turkish Football Federation and very much looking forward to beginning this new role," Taylor said. "Elite refereeing has been at the centre of my professional life for many years, and this appointment gives me the opportunity to use that experience in a different way."

‌



His appointment comes 10 months after the conclusion of a five-year investigation which found that 371 of 571 match officials in Turkey had betting accounts. TFF president Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu stated at the time: "If we want to bring Turkish football to the place it deserves, we have to clean up whatever dirt there is."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino ripped apart as explosive FIFA email leaked after botched World Cup plan READ MORE :

Some of the clean-up job will be given to Taylor, who refereed 831 matches over a 20-year career. "I am excited by the Federation's ambitions for its match officials and by the opportunity to help shape the strategic and technical development of its refereeing programme," Taylor added.

‌



"There is already a great deal of talent and commitment within Turkey, and I look forward to working with colleagues across the Federation to build on those foundations and support the continued development of referees at every stage of the elite pathway.

View 2 Images Anthony Taylor will bring his expertise to Turkey (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

"Retiring from elite refereeing was a significant decision, but I was always clear that I wanted to remain closely involved in the game and contribute to the future of officiating. This is an exciting opportunity to begin that next chapter, and I look forward to getting started."

‌



Taylor, from Altrincham, worked as a prison guard before becoming a professional referee. The 47-year-old suggested when announcing his retirement that the 'intense' pressure and 'constant' scrutiny had played a role in his decision.

In May 2023, Taylor and his family were harassed by Roma supporters at Budapest Airport following their Europa League final defeat to Sevilla and criticism from then-Roma manager Jose Mourinho. Taylor revealed last year that his family no longer came to watch matches that he refereed.
