World.title: President Hichilema Promises Revival of Chambishi metals
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has called on the residents of Chambishi to vote for the United Party for National Development (UPND) in the forth coming general elections on August 13th to enable the government to continue implementing its agenda.

The Head of state explained that voting for the UPND means continued development in the country.

Speaking during the community engagement at twalubuka schools grounds in Chambishi, in Kalulushi district on the Copperbelt Province, President Hichilema says his government will work on the reopening of Chambishi metals if re-elected in the August 13 general elections.

“We are going to re-open the Chambishi metals if you are going to vote for us in the forthcoming elections,” President Hichilema said.

The Head of state said government will continue engaging stakeholders over the Chambishi dumpsite to enhance mining activities, while stressing the need for legal and safe mining practices.

” We want to work on legalising mining activities, no parent wants to see their children dying anyhow like that,” said President Hichilema.

He stated that he will work on paying all the ex-miners that were not paid a long time ago.

He advised the residents of Chambishi not to make a mistake of voting for political parties that were busy copying the UPND manifesto.

The Head of State also disclosed that if re-elected into office, the UPND administration will pay for 16,000 people in Kabaso area to be connected to the national gride.

President Hichilema added that farmers will not be sharing a bucket of fertiliser once the UPND is re-elected.

” When you vote for us in these coming elections, I assure you that you will not be sharing a bucket of fertiliser,” said President Hichilema.

He stated that the Food Reserve Agency will be paying farmers within two days through their mobile money accounts.

He further directed Zesco limited to connect about 16,000 people from Kabaso area to the national electricity grid, stating that high connection charges should not prevent citizens from accessing power.

President Hichilema further announced that government will improve radiology services at Chambishi Hospital and rehabilitate township roads in the area.

He added that government remained committed to resolving the outstanding payments for former miners who are yet to receive their dues.

The President noted that the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) has been increased from K1.8 million to K40.8 million per constituency to accelerate community development in the country.

World.title: Nora demands action as Beijing ‘withholds’ Mukoma from WAFCON
World.content:
The Football Association of Zambia has officially complained to FIFA and CAF over the failure by Chinese Women’s Super League side Beijing to release Copper Queens striker Fridah Mukoma for the ongoing Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco.

Mukoma was among the 26 players summoned by Zambia coach Nora Häuptle for WAFCON and was expected to join camp by 20th July.

Speaking ahead of Zambia’s decisive Group C match against Malawi on Wednesday night, Häuptle confirmed the matter has been escalated.

“Fridah Mukoma was not released by her club in China. She is one of our top players and she is not getting released by her club,” Häuptle said.

“We have escalated this matter to CAF and now to FIFA. We expect action from CAF and FIFA because clubs must respect the release of players to national teams,” she said.

“I mean national teams have authority over players. I expect punishment from her team in Beijing. This is a clear issue,” Häuptle added.

The non-release has deprived the Copper Queens of a key attacking option as they fight to advance to the quarterfinals.

Zambia must beat Malawi on Wednesday night to progress from Group C.

FIFA regulations compel clubs to release players for official national team duty during international windows, with sanctions possible for non-compliance.

World.title: The Dangerous Return of PF Staged Political Violence
World.content:
By Michael Lombe

Zambia has been here before. And we must not go back. The Patriotic Front has a documented history of manufacturing crises to play the victim and stoke division. The most notorious chapter came under Mr Steven Kampyongo as Minister of Home Affairs, but the script was written earlier.

Under the late President Michael Sata, the PF conjured an imaginary group called “Tonga under Oaths”. The then Lusaka Province Police Commissioner, Ms Charity Katanga, was deployed to give it weight. The claim was grotesque: that the group had killed a Bemba child in Mazabuka and was ordering all Bemba people out of Southern Province.

President Sata saw through it. While swearing in Mr Wynter Kabimba as Justice Minister, he dismissed the tale outright. Turning to the then Defence Minister, Mr Geoffrey Bwalya Mwamba, one of the architects of the plot, he said the idea was fake and must be dropped immediately before it caused war.

The PF did not stop. Next came the story that Bemba fishermen were being chased off the Kafue River. The Disaster Management and Mitigation Unit delivered tents to “displaced” people who did not exist. The lie collapsed.

Then came the market fires and the gassings. Hundreds died including schoolchildren. Paid voices were lined up to blame the then opposition leader, Mr Hakainde Hichilema and the UPND. That too failed, because Zambians refused to be baited.

Now, in opposition, the PF and its Tonse Alliance appear to be dusting off the same playbook.

Leaked reports reveals a plan to stage attacks on their own campaign teams as they tour Southern Province. Recruits, it is said will be hired, masked, and instructed to stone their own vehicles in Monze, Choma and Kalomo. Media teams will be on standby. The purpose is clear: run back to Eastern and Northern provinces with video and say, “This is what Southerners are doing to us.”

If these allegations are true, they are not politics. They are sabotage.

This is the politics of arson, not argument. It seeks power not through policy, but through fear, tribal baiting, and staged blood.

Zambians rejected this in 2016. They rejected it in 2021. They will reject it again in 2026.

We owe it to the market traders, the schoolchildren, and the farmers who paid the price last time to say it plainly: do not light this country on fire for votes.

The law must act. The public must watch. And the media must not be used as a prop in a staged drama.

The past has instructed us. Let us not repeat it.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 4, 2026
World.content:
DR Congo Audit Confirms Oil Pollution Findings

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministry of Hydrocarbons expects to complete and publish a full environmental audit of oil company Perenco by the end of September. This comes after preliminary findings that identified pollution linked to the company's operations. A ministry official said the audit found negative impacts on soil and air quality, with ageing infrastructure and pipelines contributing to environmental damage. The findings broadly support a recent Human Rights Watch report alleging that Perenco's activities, including gas flaring, open burning of oil waste and oil spills, have polluted air, soil and water sources and posed health risks to nearby communities. Perenco has denied causing pollution. However, the government said that the final report will recommend environmental remediation measures and infrastructure upgrades.

Benin Launches New Senate Chamber

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Benin has launched its new Senate, a second chamber of parliament designed to beef up legislative oversight and protect the country's constitutional order. The Senate will scrutinise laws, request second readings of bills and has the power to block constitutional, electoral and political party reforms it deems a danger to democracy, peace or national unity. It can also suspend or revoke the political rights of public officials accused of undermining state institutions or social cohesion. Supporters say the chamber will provide better checks and balances and preserve Benin's democratic traditions. Its legitimacy has been challenged by critics, who warn that, because its members are appointed, not directly elected, it could undermine democratic accountability.

AI-Enabled Cybercrime on the Rise Across Africa

More than half of all reported cybercrimes across Africa are now powered by artificial intelligence, according to INTERPOL's 2026 African Cyberthreat Assessment Report. The report found that 55% of reported cybercrime incidents involved AI-enabled tools. Cybercrime is becoming increasingly automated and transnational, with financial losses across the continent more than doubling since 2024 to an estimated $484 million, the report said. The most common threat remains online scams, where criminals are increasingly using AI-generated synthetic identities to bypass biometric security systems and commit fraud. INTERPOL also highlighted the growing threat of phishing, ransomware and mobile money fraud, calling on governments and businesses to shore up cybersecurity as organised criminal networks exploit AI to mount faster and more sophisticated attacks across Africa.

Zimbabwe's Examination Board Releases June 2026 Exam Results

The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results. Candidates are able to access them online via the ZIMSEC portal. The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell to 3%, down from 5.87% in 2025. The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates passing at least two subjects rose by 11.88% points to 67.74%. ZIMSEC said the online results portal will remain open for five days. Printed results will be available for collection by examination centre heads from regional offices.

Close 

UN Opens Major Ebola Treatment Centre in DR Congo

The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing its largest-ever Ebola outbreak. The virus has spread to 49 health zones across several provinces, with Ituri accounting for the vast majority of infections and deaths. In response, the United Nations and its partners are opening the country's largest Ebola treatment centre, with a capacity of 100 beds, alongside a new transit centre to improve early detection and referrals. WHO has warned that a major scale-up of response efforts is urgently needed. They cite conflict, displacement, cross-border movement and worsening humanitarian conditions as key factors driving the rapid spread of the disease.

World.title: South Africa: Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban - South African News Briefs - August 4, 2026
World.content:
Water Crisis Turns Deadly in Durban

Residents of Adams Mission, south of Durban, have accused government water tanker drivers of selling water that should be supplied free of charge, following the death of 43-year-old Celani Zungu, reports EWN. Community members allege Zungu was trying to stop a tanker from leaving without delivering water to residents when he was struck and killed by the vehicle. Local councillor Thembelihle Makhanya said there is no concrete evidence of water being sold. He condemned the allegations if proven true. Police are investigating a case of culpable homicide, while the eThekwini Municipality has launched an internal investigation.

Westbury Residents March Against Gang Violence

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Residents of Westbury in Johannesburg are set to march, demanding decisive action to curb persistent gang violence and drug-related crime, reports SABC News. Community leader Bishop Dulton Adams said residents are calling for long-term solutions rather than temporary police deployments. He argued that law enforcement has a lack of a visible presence in the neighbourhood. He criticised authorities for failing to patrol the area adequately and urged stronger policing and sustained interventions to tackle gangsterism.

Parliament Defends GBVF Council Picks

Parliament's Portfolio Committee on Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities has defended its recommendations for the newly appointed Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Council, rejecting criticism from COSATU over the absence of a labour representative, reports EWN. Committee chairperson Liezl van der Merwe said the selection process was fair, legally compliant and based on candidates' experience and expertise. COSATU maintains the council should include organised labour and plans to challenge the appointments. Parliament has said that legal advice confirms that labour representation is not a legislative requirement under the GBVF Act.

World.title: Somalia: Cabinet Officials Brace to Relinquish Kenyan Passports After Presidential Ultimatum
World.content:
A mounting cohort of senior Somali government ministers is poised to surrender their Kenyan passports and national identity documents within days, heeding President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's ultimatum that dual citizens holding public office must forswear their foreign nationality or immediately vacate their posts, according to multiple informed sources.

The impending wave of surrenders represents the most aggressive enforcement of citizenship integrity standards within the executive branch in recent memory, building on Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji's unilateral decision to return his Kenyan travel documents,a move that effectively set a binding precedent for his cabinet colleagues.

Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdirashid Haji became the first senior figure to bow to the directive when he formally handed over his Kenyan passport to the Kenyan Embassy in Mogadishu earlier this week.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In a terse statement, Jibril asserted the move was designed to guarantee "complete transparency" in the execution of his official duties and to preempt any challenge to his national allegiance.

Sources who spoke to Dalsan on condition of anonymity, citing lack of authorisation to engage publicly on the matter, disclosed that several ministers and state ministers are now finalising arrangements to submit their Kenyan travel credentials and identification cards to the diplomatic mission. The sources indicated that the officials are acting with haste to avoid being perceived as defying the President's edict, which was first articulated during a closed-door cabinet sitting last Thursday.

"The President made it unequivocally clear that retaining a foreign passport while occupying a senior government portfolio is untenable," one source told Dalsan. "Those who intend to retain their cabinet seats are moving swiftly to comply, and a series of handovers is widely anticipated before the week concludes."

The directive has cast a harsh glare on the prevalence of dual citizenship among Somalia's political elite--a sensitive issue long left unaddressed but now thrust into the open.

Although Somalia's provisional constitution does not explicitly outlaw dual nationality for public officials, the President's order effectively imposes a new litmus test for the upper echelons of power, compelling officials to choose definitively between their Somali responsibilities and foreign entitlements.

The enforcement drive comes against the backdrop of heightened scrutiny of senior officials' travel documentation, with some figures having recently encountered obstacles at Kenyan ports of entry.

State Minister at the Presidency Abdirashid was among those reportedly turned away by Kenyan immigration authorities, although it remains unclear whether that incident directly precipitated the presidential directive.

Close 

Villa Somalia has yet to issue a formal communiqué on the enforcement timeline, and the Kenyan government has likewise refrained from commenting on the expected influx of surrendered documents. However, insiders suggest the list of compliant officials will expand as the President's unannounced deadline looms, with further developments expected imminently.

World.title: West Africa: Ecowas Pledges U.S.$250,000 for June 29 Flood Victims
World.content:
An area in Accra flooded after heavy afternoon rain (file photo).

THE Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has pledged US$250,000, equivalent to about GH¢3 million, to support victims of the June 29 floods that ravaged parts of Ghana.

The donation, announced by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, is expected to bolster ongoing relief efforts for thousands of people affected by the disaster.

In a Facebook post, Mr Ablakwa said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had received official notification from the ECOWAS Commission on the assistance.

He said the funds would be transferred in full to the appropriate state institutions immediately after they are received by the ministry.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Related Articles

"The transfer will be done in the interest of transparency and accountability," the minister assured.

Mr Ablakwa expressed the government's gratitude to ECOWAS for the gesture, describing it as a demonstration of solidarity and genuine African compassion at a difficult time for the country.

The June 29 floods affected communities in seven regions, claiming lives, displacing thousands of residents and destroying homes, roads and other infrastructure.

Government agencies, supported by humanitarian organisations and other stakeholders, have since been providing relief to affected families while efforts continue to restore livelihoods in the flood-hit communities.

The ECOWAS support is expected to complement the government's ongoing response to the disaster and bring relief to victims.

The June 29 floods, triggered by hours of torrential rainfall, submerged several communities across seven regions, including Greater Accra, causing widespread destruction to homes, businesses, roads and other public infrastructure.

The disaster claimed several lives, displaced thousands of residents and left many households stranded, with emergency response teams undertaking rescue operations while government agencies and humanitarian organisations provided relief items to affected families.

President John Dramani Mahama subsequently visited some of the worst-hit communities, describing the situation as a national tragedy and assuring victims of government's commitment to provide immediate relief and support reconstruction efforts.

The ECOWAS intervention is expected to complement ongoing government and humanitarian assistance aimed at easing the plight of affected families and supporting the recovery of flood-hit communities.

World.title: Uganda: 14 Killed As Truck Crashes Into Taxi in Lwera
World.content:
At least 14 people have been confirmed dead in a grisly accident in Lwera swamp along the Kampala -Masaka Highway.

The accident according to Greater Masaka Regional Police spokesperson, Twaha Kasirye, happened at around 11pm on Monday at Kamunga Trading Centre in Lwera Swamp, Kalungu District.

"The accident involved a Toyota Hiace taxi (UA 662AQ) and a Sino truck (UBS 040F) transporting sand. Fourteen (14) people died on the spot, all from the taxi," Kasirye said.

He added that four other people, including two occupants from each vehicle, sustained injuries and were rushed to Masaka Regional Referral Hospital, where they are currently receiving treatment.



He said police officers visited and documented the scene, while investigations into the cause of the crash are ongoing.

"Investigations are underway as efforts to trace the fleeing driver are ongoing."

The development comes as concerns over fatalities on Ugandan roads continue.

At least 37 people died in major road accidents within 10 days in July 2026, with four major crashes involving public transport vehicles, including three school buses carrying learners on educational trips and one passenger service bus.

The deadliest incident occurred on July 17 in Kapchorwa District, where 21 people, including 20 pupils of King David Junior School in Ndejje, Kampala, and one adult, died after their bus crashed while returning from a study tour at Sipi Falls.

The Isuzu bus, registration number UA 108BQ, reportedly developed mechanical problems before the fatal crash at Chekwatit Village, Kimawa Parish, Kawowo Sub-county.

Police preliminary investigations indicated that the driver lost control of the vehicle, which veered off the road, struck a large stone and overturned.

The tragedy raised concerns over the safety checks conducted before school trips and whether vehicles transporting learners meet the required safety standards.

Days earlier, on July 7, 2026, another fatal crash at Bobi Trading Centre along the Kampala-Gulu Highway claimed 14 lives and left 28 others injured.

The crash involved a passenger bus, registration number UBE 110H, belonging to OPIT Travellers Company, and a Mercedes-Benz Actros trailer, registration numbers KBS 564D/ZE 7948.

According to police findings, the bus driver was speeding and lost control while attempting to avoid a pedestrian crossing the road, resulting in a head-on collision with the trailer.

The police annual traffic report for 2025 indicated that Uganda registered 26,044 road crashes, indicating a 3.7% increase from the figure registered in 2024.

Close 

Of these, 4,602 were fatal, rising from the 4,434 reported in 2024 while 18,444 people got serious injuries and 3,668 got minor injuries.

In the accidents, men accounted for 83% of all the deaths while October with 523 deaths registered the highest fatalities.

World.title: South Africa: Anger After Farmers Dump Rotting Fruit Near Homes
World.content:
Farmers would never do this in their own suburbs, say Eastern Cape residents

Residents of Patensie, Eastern Cape, say farmers dumped truckloads of rotting fruit, nets and other farm waste on land earmarked for a housing project.

Kouga Local Municipality removed 14 truckloads of waste and says the illegal dumping has been referred to law enforcement for investigation.

Acht Boerdery says it has a longstanding arrangement to provide waste fruit for animals and denies dumping the nets and cables. Waterwiel Boerdery says it only left flood-damaged netting at the site after people requested it, and has since removed the material. Quacha Boerdery did not respond.

Residents of Patensie in the Eastern Cape have accused farmers of dumping truckloads of oranges and lemons, as well as farm equipment on land near their homes. They say farmers "would never do this in their own suburbs".

The rotting fruit attracted insects, as well as pigs and cattle, and created a heavy stench over Ramaphosa Village. Meanwhile, discarded nets, cables and irrigation pipes littered the site.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Kouga Local Municipality has cleared the area, removing 14 truckloads of waste.

The open land in Stuurmanskop is earmarked for a housing project.

Community leader Eric Blaauw posted on the What's Happening in Patensie Facebook page on 19 July: "New illegal dumping site by our farmers around Patensie. This is not good at all for the health and safety of our kids. This area is for housing development, not dumping. We're really being undermined."

Ward 10 councillor Mbandana Msingathi Gerald said he was alerted on 19 July to complaints about the stench from rotten lemons. Residents accused Acht Boerdery and Quacha Boerdery of dumping the fruit.

"I contacted local farmers' association chairperson Grewar Oosthuizen and gave him the names of the alleged dumpers. He promised to act immediately. Nets, wires and irrigation pipes were scattered across roads in Ramaphosa Village," Gerald said.

He said cattle ate the oranges but not the lemons.

Residents had previously buried fruit and vegetables at the site, but this stopped once the site was designated for housing.

Gerald said Patensie's only dumping site closed a year ago. Residents now have to travel 15km to Hankey to dispose of waste, and many cannot afford it. He said there is no local transit site, which is a serious issue for a town that exports fruit internationally.

Kouga Local Municipality spokesperson Monique Basson said officials had acted immediately after seeing reports on social media.

Basson told GroundUp: "We removed 14 truckloads of waste. The waste management section conducted a site inspection which confirmed illegal dumping.

"The matter was referred to law enforcement for investigation with the aim of identifying those responsible and taking legal action in terms of municipal by-laws," she said.

Acht Boerdery director Christof Opperman said the farm had a longstanding arrangement with the local livestock farmers' committee and the councillor's office to provide waste product for cattle, pigs, goats and chickens in an area where the animals already graze.

Opperman said recent floods and market pressure linked to the conflict in the Middle East had affected export and juicing channels, leaving fruit it believed still suitable for livestock.

"We also use the Hankey municipal dump for other waste and were not advised that the livestock product was excessive," he said.

Opperman said the farm was not involved in dumping the nets and cables. "We remain committed to sustainable farming and would not knowingly endanger the community, its people or its animals."

Opperman said staff may take waste fruit home for personal use and for their livestock, while remaining waste fruit is taken to the agreed grazing area and residual waste is mulched.

Close 

Charl Malan of Waterwiel Boerdery said his farm only dropped off flood-damaged covering nets at the site after people requested them. He denied dumping any fruit.

"After the floods, people asked me for netting that was damaged. After it was dropped off in heaps, it was scattered around by people taking the nets. I was unaware that fruit was dumped there. That must have happened afterwards and was not done by me," Malan said.

Malan said he did not anticipate the netting would become a health hazard.

Malan said the farm regularly experiences vandalism and theft. He said he hoped giving away damaged netting would reduce theft from the farm.

Malan said that as soon as he became aware of the problem, he sent his own workers and machinery to remove the netting. GroundUp saw workers using one of Malan's tractors to collect the nets.

Quacha Boerdery did not respond to requests for comment.

World.title: Zimbabwe: ZIMSEC Releases 2026 June Exam Results - O-Level Pass Rate Drops, A-Level Performance Improves
World.content:
The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has announced the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results, with candidates able to access them online from 6pm Monday.

The Ordinary Level pass rate for candidates who wrote five or more subjects fell by 2.87%, from 5.87% recorded in 2025, to 3% in June 2026.

The Advanced Level pass rate for candidates who passed at least two subjects (Grade E or better) increased by 11.88% from last year, to 67.74% in 2026.

Speaking during a media briefing in Harare, ZIMSEC board chairperson Professor Paul Mapfumo said the results would be available on the examination body's online portal for only five days.

"The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council board and management would like to advise the nation of the release of the 2026 June Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results.

"With effect from today, 3 August 2026 at 6pm, Ordinary and Advanced Level examination results will be accessible to all candidates and authorised personnel online through the ZIMSEC portal accessed via the ZIMSEC website.

"Please take note that this portal will be open for five days only," said Mapfumo.

Mapfumo also said heads of examination centres would begin collecting printed results for their respective schools and centres from ZIMSEC regional offices on Tuesday.

World.title: Africa: Over Half of Africa's Cybercrimes Are AI-Enabled - Interpol
World.content:
Nairobi — More than half of all cybercrimes reported across Africa are now AI-enabled, the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) has revealed, warning that digital attacks have rapidly evolved into an industrialized, borderless ecosystem that is becoming increasingly difficult to detect and combat.

According to the newly released INTERPOL African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026, 55 percent of cybercrimes reported across the continent now involve Artificial Intelligence (AI), underscoring a major shift in the cyber threat landscape.

The report says cybercrime has evolved into an increasingly automated underground economy, where criminal networks are using AI and other advanced technologies to launch attacks faster, at greater scale, and across multiple countries simultaneously.



The report further shows that cybercrime-related financial losses across Africa have more than doubled since 2024, reaching an estimated $484 million.

The assessment, based on survey data from 36 member countries and intelligence from private sector partners including Fortinet, Mastercard, the Shadowserver Foundation, S2W and TrendAI, found that 72 percent of surveyed countries reported the presence of organized scam centres, with the highest concentration in Southern and West Africa.

Among the most alarming developments highlighted in the report is the growing use of AI-generated synthetic identities to bypass biometric security systems.

Criminals are combining stolen personal information with fabricated data to deceive identity verification processes, enabling them to open bank accounts, obtain mobile loans and register SIM cards under false identities.

Online scams remain the most frequently reported form of cybercrime across the continent, while the financial services, telecommunications and government sectors continue to bear the brunt of AI-enabled credential theft and automated social engineering attacks.

The findings mirror Kenya's own evolving cyber threat landscape.

In June, the Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) announced that it detected 3.37 billion cyber threat events between January and March 2026. Although this represented a 26.15 percent decline from the previous quarter, the authority cautioned that attacks had become increasingly sophisticated, with system attacks targeting critical information infrastructure accounting for 3.23 billion of the incidents.

The INTERPOL report also noted that Kenya ranked among SOCRadar's top phishing detections globally in September 2025.

Recent cyber incidents have further illustrated the growing risks facing the country. One notable case occurred on July 18, 2026, when hackers compromised the official website of the President William Ruto, defacing its homepage with messages targeting President Ruto and demanding a ransom of five Bitcoins, worth about Sh41 million at the time.

The attackers threatened to leak unspecified information if their demands were not met. The government immediately took the website offline, with Information, Communications and the Digital Economy Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo assuring the public that response protocols had been activated and that there was no evidence of unauthorized access to sensitive government data. The presidential website was restored two days later.

The growing sophistication of cyberattacks has prompted coordinated international operations aimed at dismantling transnational cybercrime networks.

Under Operation Red Card 2.0, conducted between December 8, 2025, and January 30, 2026, across 16 African countries, law enforcement agencies arrested 651 suspects and recovered more than USD 4.3 million. Investigators identified 1,247 victims, whose reported losses exceeded USD 45 million.

In Kenya, authorities arrested 27 individuals linked to online investment fraud schemes that relied on messaging applications, social media platforms and fabricated testimonials to lure victims.

Investigators said suspects convinced victims to make initial investments of as little as USD 50, displaying fake investment dashboards showing fictitious profits before blocking withdrawals and disappearing with the funds.

A separate global operation, Operation Synergia III, conducted between July 18, 2025, and January 31, 2026, brought together law enforcement agencies from 72 countries and territories.

The operation resulted in the takedown of more than 45,000 malicious servers and internet addresses linked to phishing, ransomware and information-stealing malware campaigns, while leading to 94 key arrests worldwide.

"Cybercrime in 2026 is more sophisticated and destructive than ever before, but Operation Synergia III stands as a powerful testament to what global cooperation can achieve," said Neal Jetton, Director of INTERPOL's Cybercrime Directorate.

Jetton said organized cybercriminal syndicates continue to inflict severe financial and psychological harm on individuals, businesses and communities through increasingly sophisticated online fraud schemes, emphasizing that Operation Red Card demonstrates the critical role of international collaboration in combating transnational cybercrime.

Close 

The report also highlights significant regional variations in cyber threats. East Africa has emerged as a hotspot for mobile money fraud and ransomware attacks targeting critical infrastructure, while West and Central Africa remain major centres for business email compromise and romance scams.

Southern Africa continues to attract global threat actors seeking to maximize disruption due to its high levels of digital connectivity.

Meanwhile, cybersecurity partner TrendAI recorded approximately 600,000 detections linked to AI-generated deepfakes, digital sextortion and other forms of synthetic media abuse.

As cybercriminals increasingly harness AI to automate attacks and expand their operations across borders, INTERPOL is urging governments, businesses and individual users to strengthen cybersecurity awareness, verify digital communications before acting on them, and safeguard personal information against an increasingly sophisticated and rapidly evolving cyber threat landscape.

World.title: El-Sayed pals around with far-left streamer Hasan Piker the day before crucial Michigan Senate election

Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed spent the night before Election Day at a pool party with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, sparking pushback both from his primary opponent and his Republican opposition.

The event was hosted by a content creator in Detroit, Michigan, and also attended by progressive House candidates Melat Kiros and Chris Rabb, both members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), The Associated Press reported.

Michigan Democratic state Rep. Donavan McKinney was also reportedly in attendance.

Piker, who has roughly 10 million followers across multiple social media platforms, has made multiple appearances on the campaign trail with El-Sayed, raising questions about the ideological similarities between the two. Last month, Piker drew backlash after addressing a group of college students while wearing an outfit resembling that of former communist dictator Mao Zedong.

HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS

"I never would and never will criticize Mao Zedong," Piker said earlier this year in a clip that recently resurfaced on social media. "One of the great leaders of this world."

Piker has also said in the past that "America deserved 9/11" and has made controversial comments about Hamas and the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

While El-Sayed has said he doesn't agree with all of Piker’s positions, he has faced criticism for not distancing himself from the controversial streamer.

Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI), running against El-Sayed in Tuesday night's Senate primary, was asked about the relationship between El-Sayed and Piker in a press gaggle hours before polls closed.

"I don't believe Mr. Piker lives here in our state. I do think his rhetoric should be denounced. I do think that my opponent should distance himself from him. I don't know what they were doing last night at this pool party that was going on, but I was with Congresswoman Hillary Scholten and Debbie Stabenow," Stevens told Fox News.

Referring to Piker, Stevens said "some of this stuff makes people uncomfortable. Frankly, it makes me uncomfortable. You know, we don't need these demagogues or people citing allegiance to Mao coming into Michigan."

And pointing to El-Sayed, Stevens added, "Maybe instead of being with Mr. Piker, you know, if he ends up winning the nomination, maybe he'll come with me and hear from some of the small businesses who don't want this extreme politics coming into our state."

ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK

"Instead of spending his final hours campaigning with Michiganders, Abdul El-Sayed spent it poolside with an antisemite and terrorist sympathizer who believes America deserved 9/11," NRSC Regional Press Secretary Samantha Cantrell told Fox News Digital in a statement on Tuesday.

The campaign of presumptive GOP nominee Mike Rogers also weighed in as voters headed to the polls on Tuesday.

"We’re getting ready to prosecute the case against Abdul, but it looks he’s already giving us a head start," Alyssa Brouillet, Rogers' campaign communications director, said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "This is giving fraud, not serious. And Michiganders are battling serious issues they need a senator to deal with—not someone who dances around with LA and NYC influencers who think ‘America deserved 9/11.’"

Hours before the pool party, Piker was at a campaign event with El-Sayed where a reporter asked him if he plans to campaign with the progressive Senate candidate after Tuesday night’s primary.

JAMES CARVILLE VOWS TO ABANDON DEMOCRATIC PARTY IF FAR-LEFT HASAN PIKER BECOMES LEADING VOICE

"Are you crazy?" Piker responded. "Of course."

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign and Piker’s team for comment.

El-Sayed, according to recent polling, is expected to advance to the general election in November to face Rogers in a race that could determine the balance of power in the U.S. Senate.

World.title: 'Spider-Man' showing was reportedly evacuated due to someone's uncontrolled gas release
World.content:
The last time I went to the movies, there was a group of teenagers sitting a row behind me who talked through the entire movie.

"Man, this has to be the worst bit of poor social etiquette that could ever happen in a movie theater," I remember thinking, as I tried to block it out and zero in on the finer plot points of "Minions and Monsters" (which was great, by the way).

Well, according to reports coming from a showing of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" in Colombia, I was mistaken.

'SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY' REVIEW: TOM HOLLAND, ZENDAYA RETURN FOR ACTION-PACKED, EMOTIONAL SEQUEL

According to The New York Post, someone had to pull the e-brake on a showing of the latest Tom Holland-led Spider-Man flick because someone in the theater just could not stop dropping more gaseous bombs than the Green Goblin.

This is just absurd...

You get one fart, maybe a second if I'm feeling generous with the benefit of the doubt, but enough to clear a packed theater?

No. Unacceptable. Not in my America... or Colombia.

And not just any theater. A theater full of Marvel nerds.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE

A mouse gasser could clear out an arthouse theater, but if you've ever been to a comic book convention, you'll know that those folks are willing to put up with a lot on the olfactory front.

So for them to be like, "This is too much, we must bail," it must have meant that theater was truly uninhabitable.

I'm not sure what the theater looked like, but it makes me wonder if this was the kind of theater with recliners. I've been saying for a long time that modern theaters are getting too comfortable.

I don't like the big cushy couches. It makes people feel too comfortable, too at home.

What happens when you feel that way? Someone clears out an entire auditorium of paying customers.

Give me old-fashioned seats any day of the week.

World.title: Women's advocacy groups respond to Caitlin Clark's answer on demonstrations at Fever games
World.content:
Caitlin Clark's answer to a question about the WNBA's convergence with the "Save Women's Sports" movement became a point of internal debate within the movement and her fan base in recent days.

Dave Portnoy and Megyn Kelly, two known Clark supporters, even went at it on X about it.

Clark was asked Sunday about the WNBA's ongoing controversy related to demonstrations outside of Indiana Fever games. Her teammate Sophie Cunningham voiced her support for protecting women's sports from biological males in late July, and rallies in support of Cunningham have followed the Fever to their last three games. Counterprotests have also appeared outside each of the last three games.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

Clark did not reveal her stance on the issue when she answered, but deferred to the governing bodies and leagues that oversee women's sports.

"I think, for us, it's not really a discussion we really have in our locker room," Clark answered. "I think it's for leagues and the governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. Our focus is on basketball. That's what we talk about and how we can get wins, and, obviously, we didn't do that tonight. So we need to find an area to improve in that way."

Clark then declined a related follow-up question, saying "I just answered for you."

Multiple advocacy groups leading the "Save Women's Sports" movement have addressed Clark's answer in statements to Fox News Digital.

Some of the groups appeared to defend Clark.

The Independent Council on Women's Sports (ICONS)

"Female athletes should never be forced to 'pick a side' to defend their right to the same opportunities afforded to men or be pressured to surrender that right in the middle of their careers. Yet because sport leaders have failed to adopt clear, fair policies, players are left carrying that burden themselves, creating unnecessary conflict among teammates, friends, and competitors," ICONS co-founder Marshi Smith told Fox News Digital.

SJSU VOLLEYBALL SCANDAL PROBE FINDS TEAM ALLEGEDLY RECRUITED MALE FOR ADVANTAGE WITHOUT TELLING FEMALE PLAYERS

"We saw the devastating toll of this during the Mountain West volleyball controversy, where women were placed in the impossible position of choosing between standing up for what they believed was fair or forfeiting games at the expense of their teams.

"The resulting tension fractured relationships and divided women’s teams. That division was not created by the athletes. It was the product of institutional failure. Women’s leagues should be for women. It is the responsibility of sport leaders, not individual players, to protect the integrity of women’s competition so athletes can focus on what they came to do: compete. But when policymakers fail women, courage falls to the athletes. History has always revealed the difference between the timid and the bold, between those captive to ideology and those willing to stand for what is right."

Independent Women

"Everyone should be able to make the point that a women's league should be for women. This shouldn't be hard. It’s understandable that Caitlin Clark wants to dodge this question because the leadership of her league has been so embarrassing in their response," Independent Women President Carrie Lukas told Fox News Digital.

"That's a disservice to every female professional basketball player and every young girl who hopes to play in the future. Of course, men shouldn't be allowed in women's basketball. Full stop. You can support both equality and protecting women's sports for females only. That's why the women's basketball league exists."

THESE FEMALE ATHLETES NEED TO SPEAK UP ABOUT KEEPING WOMEN'S SPORTS FOR WOMEN, LIKE SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DID

Independent Women's Law Center

"Caitlin Clark had an opportunity to stand up for women and girls, and she chose not to. This isn't a question that should be punted or treated as someone else's responsibility. Female athletes deserve leaders and role models willing to say what the science, common sense, and now the U.S. Supreme Court have recognized: sex matters in sports," Independent Women’s Law Center senior legal counsel Beth Parlato told Fox News Digital.

"Protecting women's sports isn't controversial; it is essential to preserving fairness, safety, and equal athletic opportunity for female athletes. More athletes need to take a stand like Sophie Cunningham has and have the courage to speak clearly in defense of the very category that made their own success possible."

Concerned Women for America

"Athletes like Sophie Cunningham who are standing up for women and girls to have fair competition are exceptional and courageous. We hope that Clark and every other WNBA player will stand up in support of female athletes. But ultimately, the WNBA and other sports governing bodies must facilitate fair and safe competitions so their athletes can focus on competing. The WNBA should immediately adopt a policy that establishes only biological women can play basketball in the league. Does the WNBA stand for fairness in women’s sports or not?" Concerned Women for America CEO and President Penny Nance told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Moms for Liberty

"Women in the public eye have a responsibility to set an example for the young girls watching them, and that starts with standing up for the fundamentals of basic biology. It should never be difficult to defend common sense, and it should never be controversial to protect young girls. Every woman with a platform has a choice: stand up for the next generation of girls, or stay silent while their opportunities, their privacy, and their safety are taken away. Parents across America know where Moms for Liberty stands, and we will never back down." Moms for Liberty CEO and Co-Founder of Moms for Liberty Tina Descovich told Fox News Digital.

World.title: Carrie Underwood is back for SNF, Angel Reese celebrates Barbie Night & NFL WAGs are training-camp ready
World.content:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Happy to report I am back in the beautiful state of Tennessee.

The husband, dog and I had a nice time on our pilgrimage to the Great White North, but I am happy to be back in my own cozy home, sleeping on my own elite mattress and caring for my own little house plants.

And there's much to do now that I'm back.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

We have some exciting things coming up in OutKick Outdoors. No spoilers, but if you're into hunting, fishing, hiking, camping or even just drinking beer on patios, you should definitely be following us on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube.

Ain't too proud for a shameless plug, baby.

But that's enough of that for now. We've got some Nightcaps to do.

There's an old saying that goes, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it."

And that's exactly why NBC invited back Carrie Underwood to perform the theme song ahead of Sunday Night Football — for the 14th season in a row.

I mean, who else are you gonna get? That lady from the Women’s Pro Baseball League?

It's like they pulled three random drunk women out of a crowd and handed them microphones.

Point is, Carrie Underwood is a crowd pleaser. So come September, she and her glorious legs (I say that as an entirely straight woman) will — once again — bless our TV screens before we watch someone play against the Dallas Cowboys or Kansas City Chiefs.

Seriously, those teams make three SNF appearances each this season. You know who doesn't get any Carrie Underwood games? The Dolphins, Jets and Raiders.

Womp.

Not that I blame the schedule-makers there. I'm a Dolphins fan, and even I believe no one should be subjected to that dumpster fire in prime time.

Fun game of would you rather: three hours of Miami Dolphins football or the Martha Reeves national anthem on repeat?

Faced with that option, it almost makes Malik Washington to Jalen Tolbert sound exhilarating.

Anyway, Carrie's ready. I'm ready. You're ready. Let's get to September already.

You know who else is ready for football season? The NFL WAGs, who are pushing their boyfriends and husbands out of the house for a few weeks of uninterrupted quiet time during training camp.

Back when I worked for the Titans, anyone with fewer than three seasons (I think that was the cutoff) in the league had to stay at the Millennium Maxwell House. What a s— hole that was. It sounds fancy, but I promise: certified s— hole.

One time one of our running backs got bed bugs there, and the whole place had to be fumigated. Then, all the players lined up in a queue of shame to dump all of their worldly belongings into the laundry bin at the facility.

I was careful not to touch anything in the locker room that week. No creepy crawlies in my house, thank you.

I don't know how the Titans do training camp now, but I hope — for the players' sake — they found nicer accommodations. Or let them live at home.

Here's Drew Allar's girlfriend stocking him up with all the snacks he'll need to back up Aaron Rodgers.

Here's Isaiah Likely's wife, Melanie, sending him off in style.

Here's Myles Garrett's girlfriend — Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim — passive aggressively wishing herself a happy National Girlfriends Day since Myles apparently forgot to.

To be fair, he's trying to learn a whole new playbook out there in LA. Also, no sane person on planet earth knows when National Girlfriend Day is.

And finally, here's Jaxson Dart's girlfriend, Marissa Ayers, who has no time to care about football right now. Because it's summer, and she's in Oahu.

This is probably no news to you. Because I'm sure you've had it in your calendar for months. But the Atlanta Dream held a Barbie theme night for Angel Reese.

It was either to celebrate the release of her special edition Barbie Doll or her Barbie pink signature Reebok shoes. Or both, I don't know.

Say what you want about the woman, but she is printing money.

Angel said this Barbie collaboration means a lot to her because when she was growing up, there weren't a lot of dolls who "looked like her" and hooped like her.

Of course, she's insinuating there weren't Black dolls. Or Black dolls who played basketball. Which is just categorically false. I'm older than Angel Reese (by more than a couple years), and dolls of all skin colors were readily available when I was a kid.

ANGEL REESE GOT A BARBIE DOLL, SIGNATURE SHOE AND WNBA THEME NIGHT, THEN PLAYED VICTIM AGAIN

As a user on Twitter / X pointed out today, Christie, Barbie's Black friend, entered Barbie’s world in 1968. The first official Black Barbie arrived in 1980. And in 1998, four years before Reese was born, Mattel was already selling Black basketball-playing Barbie dolls in authentic NBA uniforms.

If you ask me (and no one did), the real injustice is the shortage of brunette Barbies. For much of my childhood, I had to settle for Barbie's less popular friend Teresa. Where is my representation?! Where is my theme night?!

I'm in the weeds. Good for Angel and her doll and her signature shoe, I guess.

Apparently, Barbie Night was a real star-studded event at State Farm Arena — with celebrities like Flo Milli, Dess Dior and Chaylyn, the OMG Girlz, Saucy Santana and Mariah the Scientist (who I'm almost certain is not a real scientist) all in the building.

Look, I know I live three hours from Atlanta, but I honestly could not tell you who a single one of those people are — aside from Michael Harris, who plays for the Braves.

I'm glad they had a nice time, though.

Football season is around the corner, which means so is your fantasy draft.

And you better take it seriously or else you might end up forced to take the last-place punishment.

We've heard all the popular ones:

Spending 24 hours in a Waffle House

Getting a tattoo of the winner's choice

Performing a stand-up comedy show at open-mic night

Taking the SAT in a room full of high schoolers

Replace a personal license plate with a humiliating vanity tag

And then, there's this:

As someone who used to compete in bodybuilding shows, I can promise you that standing up on stage — nearly naked with an ungodly spray tan — and performing a posing routine is one of the more terrifying and humbling things you'll ever do in your lifetime.

Or never do, if you're smart.

And don't even get me started on the intense cardio, training and dieting you have to do for months ahead of time in order to look like you belong. Alternatively, I guess you can just say "f— it," trot on out there, and shamelesslystrut what the good Lord gave you. Like this guy did.

So is this the worst fantasy football punishment ever? Or can you top it?

Let me know.

World.title: Alarming missile report draws forceful response from Trump as Iran war tests America’s arsenal
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Trump administration is rejecting concerns that the war with Iran has left the U.S. low on some of its most advanced long-range missiles, after a report found the Army burned through "virtually all" of its stocks of two of its primary long-range precision weapons.

The Army has used "virtually all" of its inventories of Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM) during the five-month conflict with Iran, Reuters, citing people familiar with internal U.S. military data, reported Tuesday. Officials fear the drawdown could complicate the military's ability to respond to future crises involving adversaries such as China and Russia, according to the report.

The White House disputed any suggestion the U.S. military lacks the weapons needed to carry out its missions.

WEAPONS STOCKPILE SHORTAGES IMPACTING MILITARY STRATEGY IN THE MIDEAST

"We have far more munitions than anyone in the world, and far more than we need, despite the fact that an unprecedented amount was given away by Crooked Joe Biden and the Biden Administration to Ukraine and Europe at no cost, in one of many of their extremely dumb moves," President Donald Trump said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

"Our defense companies are, at this moment, making more munitions than they have ever made before, in addition to expanding their plants and equipment at record levels. And as we build up, we will start issuing more to our allies in Europe and elsewhere."

If accurate, the report underscores a longstanding Pentagon concern: America's most sophisticated precision weapons can be expended in months but often take years to replace.

Reuters also reported that the conflict significantly reduced inventories of Patriot and THAAD missile interceptors, along with Tomahawk cruise missiles, though the Pentagon has maintained the U.S. military retains the capabilities needed to carry out operations worldwide.

HEGSETH DISMISSES ‘FOOLISH’ US STOCKPILE CONCERNS AS IRAN CONFLICT TESTS MUNITIONS

Exact U.S. weapons stockpile figures remain classified for national security reasons.

The Pentagon also pushed back on the reporting. "America’s military is the most powerful in the world and has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the President’s choosing. We have executed multiple successful operations across combatant commands while ensuring the U.S. military possesses a deep arsenal of capabilities to protect our people and our interests," chief spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement.

Independent analysts have also warned that months of combat have strained U.S. inventories of high-end munitions. The Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated last week that the U.S. had expended roughly 65% of its Patriot interceptor stockpile and that inventories of THAAD interceptors had fallen by at least 38% since the start of the Iran conflict, based on open-source analysis and budget data. Reuters reported Tuesday that its sources said those figures broadly aligned with internal U.S. data.

ATACMS and the newer Precision Strike Missile are among the Army's premier long-range precision strike weapons, capable of striking targets hundreds of miles away without putting pilots in harm's way.

ARMY CUTS HELICOPTERS, PUSHES ‘AMAZON FOR WAR’ AS DRONE COMBAT RESHAPES MILITARY

Military planners consider them particularly valuable against heavily defended adversaries because they can destroy command posts, air defenses, logistics hubs and other high-value targets from beyond many enemy air-defense systems.

Patriot and THAAD serve a different mission. Rather than striking enemy targets, they defend U.S. forces and allies by intercepting incoming ballistic missiles, while Tomahawk cruise missiles allow the Navy to conduct long-range strikes from ships and submarines.

The report comes as Pentagon leaders have increasingly warned about the challenge of sustaining prolonged, high-intensity conflicts against major powers while replenishing advanced weapons consumed in combat.

That concern has accelerated efforts to pair expensive precision missiles with far larger numbers of lower-cost, "attritable" drones and autonomous systems that can be produced rapidly and fielded at scale. Officials argue the approach would allow commanders to reserve million-dollar precision weapons for the highest-value targets while relying on less expensive systems for surveillance, electronic warfare and many strike missions.

Military leaders caution, however, that inexpensive drones are not a replacement for long-range precision missiles such as ATACMS and PrSM. Those weapons remain essential for striking hardened command centers, air-defense batteries and other heavily defended targets at distances many lower-cost drones cannot yet reach or survive.

Trump has met repeatedly with executives from the nation's largest defense contractors, pressing them to accelerate production and expand manufacturing capacity as conflicts in Iran and Ukraine strain U.S. stockpiles.

Following a White House meeting in March, Trump said the companies had agreed to quadruple production of what he called "Exquisite Class Weaponry," including some of the military's most advanced missile systems. At a second meeting in June and again at a defense summit in July, the president urged industry leaders to move faster, telling executives, "We have the best quality in the world, but we need a little more speed."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The production push is also reflected in the administration's budget priorities. Trump's proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget would more than triple spending on drones and autonomous systems while boosting investment in munitions production, missile defense and Tomahawk cruise missile procurement.

World.title: Tennessee coach unloads on NCAA's 'bulls–t', after star linebacker suspended for outdated rule
World.content:
KNOXVILLE, TN - After the NCAA decided it was going to suspend Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter for the opening two games of the upcoming season, his head coach did not hesitate to call out the organization for the current rule structure.

Following the 2025 season, Carter decided it was time to pursue his NFL dreams by declaring for the draft and hiring a professional agent to start the process. It was at that moment that the Tennessee linebacker lost his collegiate eligibility according to the antiquated rules currently in place.

Because Carter also accepted a $427 plane ticket from his professional agent to attend a training session, which is when the linebacker first discovered that he had suffered a foot injury that would prevent him from fully reaching his potential of being drafted high.

NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR

In reality, Arion would have lost millions because of the injury, so he decided the best course of action was a return to college, which transpired just weeks after he first initially announced his decision to go pro.

Carter also paid back the $427 and the school self-reported the 'violation' to the NCAA.

After informing Tennessee that he wanted to return, the question whether the Vols had a roster spot for him. So, he entered the transfer portal for a quick stop, before rejoining the Tennessee football program.

Tennessee coach unloads on NCAA suspension

Speaking on Tuesday before the Vols open Fall camp, head coach Josh Heupel did not mince words on the NCAA's punishment of a 2-game suspension for the linebacker.

"He's done everything the right way..The ruling that came out from the NCAA of a 2-game suspension I truly believe is bullshit," Heupel fiercely noted. "You look at the landscape of college football, the rules of NIL and everything, I think the ruling is completely outdated. I am disappointed for him, and for us, with the result of that ruling."

NCAA suspends Tennessee linebacker for $427 plane ticket, as college sports hands out millions in NIL

What did the NCAA have to say in response to upholding a 2-game suspension for Arion Carter?

"NCAA rules are clear: student-athletes may not sign with agents to pursue NFL Draft opportunities, and this student-athlete knowingly violated those longstanding rules. When student-athletes violate NCAA rules, the school declares them ineligible and works with the national office to determine requirements for reinstatement, which can include repayment and/or withholding from competition."

The problem is that there is no way back for an athlete if they decided to declare for the draft, but potentially get hurt in the early training process before all-star games, and also before winter workouts are set to begin in college.

Josh Heupel stands with his player against NCAA ruling

The whole process is laughable when it comes to what is actually transpiring in college athletics right now.

There are schools using agents to circumvent that rev-share cap so athletes can make millions, while high school prospects are signing are agreeing to terms with schools that include private airfare travel for the player themself and their family.

Ted Cruz urges Senate to stay in Washington until Protect College Sports Act passes this week

Right now, college athletes are making millions of dollars for their schools, and the NCAA, but a rule that is outdated is preventing a football player from garnering national exposure like Carter would when Tennessee plays Georgia Tech in a primetime game during the second week.

"AC at the end of last chose to enter his name in the NFL Draft process in the middle of January, right before the deadline where you have to make the final declaration," Josh Heupel noted. "He found out he needed a medical procedure that was gonna require surgery. He made the choice, and the right choice for him, to come back to college football.

"He was upfront and honest, and paid back the four-hundred-dollar flight. He's done everything, and handled everything, the right way. Very truthful, and upfront about everything. I think it's unfortunate that a young man that represents everything inside of this game the right way is faced with that ruling."

Now, even though he is a leader on the Tennessee football team, Arion Carter will miss the opening games of the 2026 season.

The young man could have sued the NCAA, and probably won pretty easily, and this would have been another court case the organization would have had to deal with.

But, Carter is going about his business in preparation for the season and handling it with grace.

There are plenty of people who don't agree with the NCAA upholding a suspension, and the Tennessee administration is high on the list. And most likely, college football fans across the country.

World.title: Embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller requests an Ethics investigation into himself
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Embattled Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, on Tuesday requested that the House Ethics Committee investigate domestic abuse allegations made by his ex-wife — an unusual move to try to exonerate himself amid a messy custody battle that is playing out in public view.

“In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and family. I have absolutely nothing to hide,” Miller, who has vehemently denied the allegations, said in a post on X.

“We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves,” Miller continued.

01:39 Rep. Miller vows to stay in reelection race amid abuse allegations 00:00 00:00

Hours later, the Ethics panel said it had launched an investigation into whether Miller may have engaged in “domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use in violation of the Code of Official Conduct.”

Miller denied multiple allegations in a livestream on X over the weekend, saying: “I have never abused our daughter. ... No court, no agency has ever substantiated any allegation of abuse against me. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me.”

He also released several audio recordings and transcripts that he said proved his case. In one of them, Miller’s ex-wife Emily Moreno is identified as telling Miller she believes he has a drug problem and that she found needles by his bed — allegations he denied to her. Another transcript identifies Miller telling Emily Moreno that he was injecting himself with testosterone.

A spokesperson for Emily Moreno, Stefan Mychajliw, accused Miller of lying “about his ex-wife to desperately try to save his political career” in an earlier statement. “There is a documented trove of evidence that Miller has a history of violent and dangerous behavior and no amount of victim shaming will change that,” Mychajliw said.

An Ethics investigation will likely take weeks, if not months to complete. The House is out on its August recess and will return in September.

But the fact that he made the request suggests Miller is not planning to drop out of his race for re-election, despite a declaration from his former father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno, a fellow Ohio Republican, that Miller is not fit to serve in Congress.

Earlier this week, Moreno issued a stunning statement saying Miller “needs serious psychological help” and is “a danger to my daughter,” Emily Moreno, adding, “I hold my breath every minute he has custody of my granddaughter.”

“If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them,” Moreno added. “He should not serve in the House of Representatives.”

In the Capitol on Tuesday, Moreno became emotional when telling reporters about the toll this public feud with Miller has taken on his daughter, granddaughter and wife.

“This is truly the seventh level of hell. This has been a horrific experience for my entire family,” Moreno said.

Moreno said his daughter lives in constant fear of Miller and said he met Miller at a police station on Sunday to pick up his granddaughter.

So far, President Donald Trump is standing by Miller, though the allegations are unsettling for some congressional Republicans. Trump on Monday called the situation “a very sad thing” and said Miller, a political ally, is a “good person.”

The president said he wanted to let the families figure things out.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said the allegation that Miller engaged in domestic abuse is “none of my business.” But the senator added: “It just— it doesn’t help. Just gives people more one more reason to be disgusted with Congress.”

Lawmakers typically do not request Ethics investigations into themselves, but it has happened before. In 2008, then-House Ways and Means Chairman Charlie Rangel, D-N.Y., asked the Ethics Committee to investigate allegations that he had improperly used congressional letterhead to rally support for an educational center named after him.

But the strategy backfired for Rangel. After a two-year Ethics probe, the panel found the longtime congressman guilty of violating 11 House ethics rules, and he was censured by the full House. Rangel had to relinquish his powerful Ways and Means gavel in the process, and he did not seek re-election in 2016.

World.title: McDonald’s struggles to attract bargain-hungry customers
World.content:
Having trouble figuring out this economy? So is McDonald’s.

The fast-food giant reported its slowest U.S. sales growth in over a year as its value push fell flat with customers who continue to struggle with higher prices.

Overall U.S. customer count declined. Company executives said it provided too many value offers, including a $3-and-under menu and $5 bundled meal deals, that ended up muddling the chain’s message to people who are as hungry for bargains as they are for convenient food.

“We simply didn’t execute at the level we needed to in the second quarter,” CEO Chris Kempczinski said in a statement Tuesday. The company must “raise the bar in the U.S. and accelerate performance in our largest market.”

Despite widespread reports of resilient U.S. consumer spending, the economic landscape remains highly uneven, with low-income households still facing acute affordability issues. Fast-food spending in particular has taken a hit as establishments known for offering value have been forced to compete with rising food and labor costs. And despite a relatively low unemployment rate, wages have barely kept up with inflation.

McDonald’s also shook up the top ranks of its U.S. segment. Skye Anderson, a longtime McDonald’s employee, will take over as president of the division immediately, though the company called it a planned transition. Predecessor Joe Erlinger, who held the job for over six years and often served as the face of McDonald’s in TV news segments, will be an adviser through early next year, the company said.

Analysts were unsparing in their assessment of McDonald’s newfound troubles.

“This is a bit of a damning earnings call,” Jonathan Maze, editor-in-chief of Restaurant Business, said on X. He said the company had fallen into a “very jumbled” strategy in the U.S., with multiple value offers and changes to its loyalty program alongside numerous promotions.

“All that angered customers and led to slowing traffic,” Maze said.

Combine that with persistent inflation, and it’s a big problem.

McDonald’s CFO Ian Borden called it “a challenging consumer environment,” noting that overall fast-food industry traffic in several of its largest markets continued to be “flat to negative.” Indeed, federal data shows that U.S. household spending on fast-food establishments has declined in seven of the last nine months.

Industry analysts say value is now paramount — and sit-down chains are outperforming, with the likes of The Cheesecake Factory, Chili’s and Outback Steakhouse all seeing significant growth. These chains are capturing market share from longtime value stalwarts, while traditional fast-food diners are increasingly declining to eat out at all.

“Consumers want to go out and spend their hard-earned money, and we think we’re taking some wallet share from fast food and fast casual,” Rick Cardenas, CEO of Darden Restaurants, which owns LongHorn Steakhouse and Olive Garden, said during an earnings call in June.

Olive Garden’s latest offering: the return of its “Never-Ending Pasta Pass.”
