Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that the group he leads, Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), which is in the process of splitting from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, will soon form a party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes” over abortion or same-sex marriage. However, Morawiecki made clear he retains a hardline position on migration, saying he wants “zero Muslim migrants”, even legal ones, in Europe. He also categorically ruled out ever working with current Prime Minister Donald Tusk, but left the door open to potentially cooperating with the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), which is part of Tusk’s current ruling coalition, and with the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja), an opposition group. Morawiecki u Rymanowskiego: „Do 15 października założymy partię” No coraz ciekawiej 👀 pic.twitter.com/0FrMafvTEl — chrzanik (@chrzanikx) August 3, 2026 Development Plus was founded as an association by Morawiecki, a former PiS prime minister and current deputy leader of the party, in April this year. That immediately prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. Matters came to a head last month, when PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński demanded that all the party’s lawmakers sign a pledge of loyalty and commit to leave any political associations they are part of. Morawiecki and his allies refused to do so, prompting Kaczyński to declare that meant they had effectively resigned from the party. Last week, Development Plus announced it had formed its own separate parliamentary caucus with 40 MPs in the Sejm, the most powerful lower house of parliament. The move immediately made it the third-largest group in the parliament, while also meaning PiS was no longer the biggest. Former Polish PM @MorawieckiM says 41 lawmakers aligned with him will form their own parliamentary caucus, deepening a split in conservative opposition party @pisorgpl. The proposed group would become the third-largest bloc in Poland's Sejmhttps://t.co/coOdpS7pia — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 Most MPs in Development Plus, including Morawiecki himself, are still technically members of PiS, a situation that will only change if they decide to quit the party or if they are thrown out following a disciplinary process that could take weeks to complete. However, on Monday, in a lengthy interview with journalist Bogdan Rymanowski, Morawiecki confirmed that he would establish a new, separate party. That will happen “at the latest on 15 October”, when Development Plus is planning to hold a major convention, he added. Morawiecki claimed that a small group of hardliners, associated in particular with the nationalist Sovereign Poland (Suwerenna Polska) party that was absorbed into PiS in 2024, were “devouring” PiS from the inside, pushing it in a more “radical” direction and seeking to take control of the party and its finances. The former prime minister argued that it had been a “colossal mistake” by PiS to try to compete with two rising far-right groups, Confederation and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), while abandoning the centre ground. He noted that this had coincided with the party’s support in polls falling to below 25%, its lowest level in 14 years and well below the 35% that the party won at the 2023 parliamentary elections, when Morawiecki was prime minister. Morawiecki also traced PiS’s problems back even further, pointing to the decision in 2020 to push for a near-total abortion ban. He claimed that he had, at the time, “warned [Kaczyński] repeatedly…that it would lead to disaster”. Subsequently, PiS fell from support of over 40% in polls to around 30% within a year. Morawiecki told Rymanowski that he and many of his colleagues in Development Plus support a return to the pre-2020 abortion law. “Poland doesn’t need the fervour of ideological disputes” over issues such as abortion and same-sex marriage, especially during a time of “crises, wars and disruptions”, said Morawiecki. “I want us to talk about strengthening the economy, strengthening security, restoring the job market, and how to prevent young people from thinking about leaving Poland again.” Poland’s prime minister has admitted it was a “mistake” for the ruling party to push for the constitutional court to introduce a near-total abortion ban in 2020. He claims “he has always been a supporter” of the abortion law that existed before the ruling https://t.co/QObza3Raxk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 6, 2023 The former prime minister also made clear that his overriding aim is “removing [Tusk] from power and overthrowing the Tuskist system”, which he characterised as a combination of “idleness” and “profound cynicism”, with the lack of any significant reforms disguised by “political marketing”. Asked if he would seek to achieve this by forming a coalition with the far-right Confederation, Morawiecki refused to rule it out, saying that “voters will decide” on the strength of various parties. “But I certainly won’t form any coalition with Tusk,” he clarified. However, Morawiecki suggested he would be willing to work with PSL and its leader, current deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, if they left the coalition with Tusk. PSL is the most conservative part of the current government. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 While Morawiecki generally laid out a vision of a relatively moderate centre-right party that he wants to create, he also made clear that he retains a hardline position on opposing Muslim immigration. “I would say zero Muslim immigrants at all. In Poland, absolutely zero…even into Europe,” he declared. Asked by Rymanowski to clarify if he was talking about only illegal migrants, or legal ones as well, Morawiecki said he was also referring to legal Muslim migrants. “We cannot accept them, because they will destroy our culture,” said Morawiecki. “After what I see Muslims doing in Europe, I don’t want to turn Europe into a Muslim caliphate….The French and Germans…are making a colossal mistake: destroying their own culture, destroying security, and destroying peace.” An Islamic group wants to establish a new prayer centre in Kraków for the growing local Muslim community The idea has drawn concern from some local residents and protests from right-wing groups, who say Poland should avoid "the mistakes of western Europe" https://t.co/ClCwusyhhp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 23, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Pole becomes first person to swim 160km Baltic Sea route between Sweden and Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish swimmer Bartłomiej Kubkowski has become the first person in history to swim across the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Poland, covering a distance of just over 160 kilometres (99 miles). On Sunday evening, an exhausted Kubkowski clambered onto the beach in the town of Dziwnów on Poland’s northern Baltic coast, around 56 hours after he had set off from Kaseberga in Sweden on Friday. The achievement marks a personal triumph for Kubkowski, for whom this was the fifth attempt to complete the route. His effort this year has raised over 715,000 zloty (€166,000) for children’s cancer treatment so far, with donations to his fundraiser still coming in. View this post on Instagram A post shared by PURELY ATHLETICS (@purelyathletics) During the crossing, Kubkowski was unable to sleep and, although a support boat accompanied him and provided food and drink, he was not allowed to touch the vessel itself. His journey of around 160km was not far off the longest-ever continuous, unassisted open-water swim ratified by the Marathon Swimmers Federation, which was the 168.3 km swum by American Sarah Thomas in 2017 in Lake Champlain, between the US states of New York and Vermont. Kubkowski has been attempting to swim the route between Sweden and Poland since 2022, getting progressively closer to achieving the goal. Last year, he came within 11km of the Polish coast before extreme exhaustion and deteriorating weather forced him to give up, reported Eurosport. However, Kubkowski, a former competitive swimmer who now devotes himself to ultraswimming, did last year manage to break the world record for the longest distance swum in a swimming pool over 24 hours, after he managed to cover 103.6 km (64.5 miles). Another Polish swimmer, Karolina Szczepaniak, is also currently attempting to swim from Sweden to Poland along a slightly different route to Kubkowski’s. At the time of writing, she is around 110km into the 172km journey, and has raised almost 400,000 zloty for charity. Szczepaniak, a former Olympic swimmer, also attempted the feat last year, but was forced to give up after 57 hours amid worsening weather. However, the 146.7km she swam set a new record for the longest distance covered by a female swimmer in the Baltic Sea and a Polish record for open-water swimming by a woman. A Canadian multinational operator of convenience stores, Alimentation Couche-Tard, has announced plans to acquire Poland’s Żabka Group, which runs Europe’s largest chain of convenience stores. The company has offered 32 zloty per share, valuing Żabka at 32.6 billion zloty (€7.56 billion). Żabka’s main shareholders have agreed to sell their stakes, with final approval still required from stock market investors. If the transaction is completed, Żabka is likely to be delisted from the Warsaw Stock Exchange just two years after its market debut. Właściciel Circle K chce przejąć 100% Żabki. Cena w wezwaniu ma wynieść 32 zł za akcję =>https://t.co/61XEGuQnnB via @PawelBiedrzycki https://t.co/61XEGuQnnB — Strefa Inwestorów (@strefainw) July 31, 2026 The acquisition will be carried out through Alimentation Couche-Tard’s Polish subsidiary, Circle K, which runs petrol stations, and will cover all of Żabka Group’s more than one million shares. Heket, an entity linked to CVC Capital Partners owning 37.6% of Żabka’s shares, and PG Investment Company, holding 10%, have agreed to sell their entire stakes. A group of major individual shareholders, together controlling 9.6% of Żabka’s shares, has also agreed to sell its holdings to the Canadian buyer. The investors include members of the company’s management and former executives. They have also agreed to reinvest part of the proceeds from the sale into Alimentation Couche-Tard shares. The tender offer for the remaining shares was announced on Friday by Ipopema Securities, which is acting as the intermediary in the transaction. Alimentation Couche-Tard and Żabka expect subscriptions for the offer to open around 26 August, following a review of the tender document by the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF). The companies foresee the transaction closing by the end of the year. The Canadian company expects Żabka to continue operating independently, under the leadership of its current management team, and to retain its brand. Żabka shares jumped after the announcement, rising from 29.26 zloty to around 31.60 zloty on Friday afternoon, an increase of about 8%. World.title: The split in Poland’s opposition could help them unseat Tusk’s government [Opinion]
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. By Daniel Tilles If Mateusz Morawiecki cuts his final ties with PiS and forms a new party, it may help broaden the opposition’s appeal by offering voters a more moderate, centre-right option. While the strings have not yet been fully cut, Poland’s main opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), is splitting in two. A group of 40 MPs led by former Prime Minister (and PiS deputy leader) Mateusz Morawiecki have now formed a separate parliamentary caucus of their own, after last week refusing to sign a pledge of loyalty and quit the association they had formed – as had been demanded by PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński. Former Polish PM @MorawieckiM says 41 lawmakers aligned with him will form their own parliamentary caucus, deepening a split in conservative opposition party @pisorgpl. The proposed group would become the third-largest bloc in Poland's Sejmhttps://t.co/coOdpS7pia — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 The move means that Morawiecki’s caucus, known as Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), is now the third largest in parliament, while PiS, which is down to 147 MPs, has lost its status as the biggest. For now, most of Morawiecki’s followers officially remain members of the PiS party, a situation that will only change if they either resign or are thrown out following a disciplinary process that could take weeks. But unless either or both sides make major concessions, it seems only a matter of time before Development Plus becomes a separate party. A lot of international reporting has suggested that these developments will harm Poland’s right-wing opposition and boost the re-election chances of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s more liberal coalition at next year’s parliamentary elections. In fact, PiS’s split could well help the opposition win a majority. Over the last year, PiS has found itself in an increasingly difficult position. Its support in the polls has fallen below 25%, the party’s lowest level in 14 years. Meanwhile, combined support for two far-right opposition groups – Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) – has risen to over 20%, threatening PiS’s longstanding dominance on the right. In response, Kaczyński has pushed his party in a more rightward direction, picking a hardline figure, Przemysław Czarnek, as PiS’s prime ministerial candidate in March. That signalled that PiS was aiming to compete head to head with the far right on many issues, taking tougher positions on Ukraine, the EU, migration and climate policy. In many cases, that meant disowning the legacy of the PiS government led by Morawiecki from 2017 to 2023. It also meant that the party was ceding the centre ground, something Morawiecki, who represents the more moderate, technocratic side of PiS, was particularly concerned about (alongside his own waning influence). When in power, PiS launched a revolution in Poland's energy transition. But now, in opposition, it has disowned those achievements and returned to an emphasis on coal. This could be a missed opportunity to win back centrist voters, writes @OrzelBartlomiej https://t.co/8cGvubn7N2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 29, 2026 Should Morawiecki now, as expected, launch his own centre-right party, focused on economic development, it would appeal to moderate conservatives who are opposed to the Tusk government but put off by the far right and PiS’s own hardline turn. Inevitably, some of the support for Development Plus would come at the expense of PiS – but not all of it, and possibly not even most of it. An example of something similar happening can be seen elsewhere among the opposition. Until last year, KKP was part of Confederation. However, its leader, Grzegorz Braun, was expelled after announcing a run for the presidency against Confederation’s official candidate, Sławomir Mentzen. In June 2025, KKP formed its own parliamentary caucus. Since then, support for Confederation has remained stable at around 13-14%, while KKP has risen to over 9% in the polls. So, by splitting, the two groups actually increased the size of their potential electorate, with KKP successfully appealing to an even more radical pool of voters than Confederation. It is possible that Morawiecki could do the same in the opposite direction – his new party winning over moderate conservatives while PiS continues to appeal to its most loyal supporters as well as competing with the far right. There certainly seems to be fertile ground for such a party. Regular polling by the state research agency CBOS shows that the proportion of Poles with a negative view of Tusk’s government rose to its joint-highest level this month, at 48%, while only 29% have a positive view. The last time that positive views outnumbered negative ones was in February 2024, the second full month of the current ruling coalition’s time in power. Among those who voted for Tusk and his allies in 2023, dissatisfaction is strongest among moderate conservatives. Both Tusk’s centrist KO and one of his coalition partners, The Left (Lewica), are polling only slightly below the proportion of votes they received in that year (30.7% and 8.6%, respectively). However, the most conservative part of the coalition, the centre-right Third Way (Trzecia Droga) alliance, has fallen from 14.4% of the vote in 2023 to only around 4-5% today for the two parties that constituted it, Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) and the Polish People’s Party (PSL) (which last year decided to go their separate ways). An IBRiS poll for Polsat News in April this year found that, whereas 84% of KO voters and 57.1% of Left voters have a positive view of Tusk’s government, that figure falls to 42.5% for Third Way voters, a majority of whom (51.6%) have a negative opinion. PSL and Poland 2050, the two parties that make up the Third Way alliance, have confirmed that they are splitting and will stand separately at the next elections. They will, however, remain part of @donaldtusk's ruling coalition https://t.co/NduEJY25eE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 18, 2025 Moderate conservatives’ disillusionment with the government, combined with PiS’s shift away from the centre ground, gives a clear opportunity for Morawiecki. And Tusk’s coalition itself showed in 2023 the advantages for the opposition in offering a broader set of options. While some – in KO in particular – had pushed for centrist and left-wing parties to stand jointly on a single list at that year’s elections, instead they campaigned as three main blocs. That gave voters opposed to the PiS government a genuine choice, and likely played a big part in the record turnout that helped bring Tusk’s coalition to power. It is similarly possible now that a four-branched opposition, ranging from Morawiecki on the centre right, through PiS and Confederation, to Braun on the radical right, could together win a parliamentary majority. Polls currently show those four groups with combined support of around 50% (though polling regarding support for Morawiecki’s prospective party should for now be treated with caution). Jestem dumny z tego, co wspólnie zrobiliśmy dla Polski. I wiem jedno – nasza misja wciąż trwa💪🇵🇱#RozwojPlus pic.twitter.com/xOnxKDoroS — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 31, 2026 However, even if they do win a majority, it is far from certain what would happen then. In 2023, the three opposition blocs were, although standing separately, clearly aligned with one another and focused on removing PiS from power. When they together won a parliamentary majority, it was absolutely clear they would form a coalition government. By contrast, today’s opposition is deeply divided. Confederation and KKP regularly attack PiS. It is not at all clear that Confederation would be willing to form a coalition government with PiS, while Kaczyński has explicitly ruled out working with the pro-Russian, anti-American Braun. Meanwhile, Morawiecki’s split has followed months of bitter infighting within PiS, which has often been carried out in public. The manner in which he and his allies are now departing the party means that relations with PiS are likely to remain difficult. The national-conservative opposition PiS party's newly named candidate for prime minister has made overtures to the far-right Confederation. But he also ruled out Grzegorz Braun, an even more radical far-right figure, serving in a PiS-led government https://t.co/i3zOZJWdUN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 9, 2026 It would therefore be hard for the opposition to form a government, even if they do win a majority. In this situation, the role of President Karol Nawrocki may be vital. Though elected with the support of PiS last year, he was technically an independent and maintained good relations with Confederation and even, to some extent, Braun (who endorsed Nawrocki after being eliminated in the first round). When Morawiecki this week announced the “ten pillars” of Development Plus’s programme, he made clear his loyalty to Nawrocki: the second of those pillars is “respect for the president”. Nie ma silnej Polski bez wielkich ambicji. Nie ma wielkich ambicji bez ludzi, którzy je zdefiniują i będą gotowi wziąć odpowiedzialność za ich realizację. Bezpieczeństwo. Rozwój. Suwerenność. Ambicja. Tożsamość. Patriotyzm. To nie hasła wyborcze, ale fundamenty państwa, które… pic.twitter.com/G0YBbfhLye — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 28, 2026 Many on the right hope that Nawrocki can play a role next year in helping the opposition present a more united front during the election campaign. It is also the president who decides who gets the opportunity to try to form a government after the elections. That role would be of particular significance if, as is very possible, Tusk’s KO emerges as the biggest individual party but the opposition together may be able to form a parliamentary majority. Given that we are still over 14 months away from the elections, and Morawiecki has not even yet officially split from PiS, it is still far too early to make confident predictions. However, while Morawiecki’s likely departure is clearly a personal blow to Kaczyński – and a sign of the 77-year-old’s waning influence over not only the Polish right but even his own party – it may conversely provide a boost to the opposition as a whole. World.title: Poland bans use of smartphones by children in primary schools and preschools
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has banned children from using smartphones and other electronic devices in primary schools and preschools in a bid to improve their wellbeing and safety. The new legislation, signed into law by President Karol Nawrocki on Thursday, will take effect at the start of the school year on 1 September, but schools will have until the end of 2026 to adjust. Prezydent podpisał nowelizację, która zakazuje korzystania z telefonów komórkowych w przedszkolach i szkołach. (PAP)#PAPInformacje pic.twitter.com/CK7YFU7sru — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) July 30, 2026 Under the new rules, pupils in primary schools and preschools will be prohibited from using smartphones and other electronic devices allowing communication or audio and video recording for the entire school day, including breaks and lessons held outside of school grounds. Schools will be allowed, but not required, to create designated places where pupils’ devices can be stored in a safe way and with respect for their privacy. The law, however, allows for some exceptions. When pupils need a device because of illness, disability or other special needs, school headteachers can permit their use. Phones could also be used in emergencies where there is a direct threat to life, health or property. Furthermore, pupils will be permitted to use mobile phones if a teacher deems them necessary for educational purposes and gives approval. The law also allows secondary schools to introduce bans on smartphone use if they choose, but does not make this compulsory, with such schools retaining autonomy to set their own rules through their statutes. The draft law banning phones from primary schools was first approved by the government in June. It then went to the Sejm, the lower and more powerful chamber of Poland’s parliament, which introduced amendments, including extending the measures to preschools. The Sejm then approved the bill in a rare near-unanimous vote, with only some MPs from the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) voting against it. Subsequently, the Senate passed the bill without amendments, sending it to Nawrocki, who could have signed it, vetoed it, or sent it to Poland’s constitutional court for review. Poland’s government has approved a ban on mobile phones in primary schools as well as tougher age-verification requirements for online pornography. Both measures still require parliamentary and presidential approval before becoming law https://t.co/y4Ycf46FQD — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2026 The president ultimately decided to sign the law, with his office noting that the measures aim to “create safer learning conditions” and support the “healthy and responsible” use of digital technologies by pupils. Poland’s education minister Barbara Nowacka said last month that the law would “improve teachers’ power, autonomy and agency, as well as order and digital wellbeing in schools”. She added that, although many schools already have such bans in place, teachers had asked for legal backing to help enforce them. For more on the measures, see our earlier report from when the bill was approved almost unanimously by parliament, with only the far right voting against it https://t.co/9Mx0SfkE5V — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 According to a survey conducted in April by the Polish state research institute CBOS for the Polish Press Agency (PAP), 85% of Poles support a ban on the use of smartphones in primary schools. Poland has been recently stepping up efforts to protect young people from various digital threats. The topic has been a rare area of consensus between the government and Nawrocki, who has vetoed a record number of bills. Earlier this month, Nawrocki signed a law banning online content depicting illegal acts or other forms of abusive and degrading behaviour – known in Polish as “patostreaming”. Another measure approved by the government that is now being considered by parliament is the introduction of stricter age-verification requirements for accessing online pornography. In January, the digital affairs ministry also announced that it hoped to introduce measures blocking children from access to social media. Poland hopes this year to introduce measures preventing children from accessing social media, says the country's digital affairs ministry. It is working on tools that would require platforms to verify the age of users https://t.co/G7qeEl2q9x — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 5, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Czechia Tightens Temporary Protection Rules for Ukrainian Men Aged 23 to 60
World.content:
New rules affecting Ukrainian men seeking temporary protection in the Czech Republic will take effect on August 5, 2026.

Under the changes, men aged 23 to 60 applying for temporary protection will have to demonstrate that they are exempt from military service in Ukraine.

The requirement will apply to new applications and certain other applications for protection, but not to people who already hold valid temporary protection.



The Czech Interior Ministry says the new rules follow an EU Council decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union on August 4. The decision also extends temporary protection for people fleeing Russia’s war in Ukraine until March 31, 2028.

For applicants aged 23 to 60, military registration documents will be checked as part of the application process. Applicants will use Ukraine’s Reserv+ system to demonstrate their military status, with the electronic military registration document showing whether they are exempt from military service.

The rules are different for younger applicants. People aged 18 to 22 will only need to demonstrate that they are registered in the Reserv+ system.

The new requirement concerns people applying for temporary protection for the first time, as well as repeat applications and applications connected with family reunification. It does not apply to people who already have valid temporary protection.

The military-service requirement will also not be introduced as part of the regular extension process. Ukrainians whose temporary protection is already valid will therefore not have to provide this additional documentation when extending their status through March 2028.

Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said the Czech government had pushed for stricter conditions for new applicants. According to the ministry, the change is expected to reduce the number of new arrivals and ease pressure on public services, including health care and social security.

World.title: Filming of American Spy Series to Bring Restrictions to Prague 7
World.content:
Filming for the American series Birdwatcher will take place at the Prague 7 tax office on Kapitána Jaroše Embankment from August 8 to 24, bringing temporary restrictions to the area.

The production will use the tax office building at Kapitána Jaroše Embankment 1000/7, while part of the sidewalk outside the building will be closed to accommodate filming equipment.

The restrictions will not affect the normal operation of the tax office.



Drivers should also expect temporary parking restrictions on nearby Na Ovčinách Street. Vehicles will still be allowed to pass through the street, but parking will be prohibited during the designated filming periods.

The restrictions will not be in force continuously throughout the filming period. They will apply only on specific dates, with Prague 7 publishing a map showing the affected areas and individual dates on its website.

Prague has become a major filming location

Birdwatcher is an American spy fantasy series set during the Cold War. The production is being led by Legendary and Apple TV, with Andy Goddard directing. Wyatt Russell plays the lead role.

The story follows Colonel Lee Shaw as he embarks on a covert mission behind enemy lines to prevent the Soviet Union from unleashing a new Titan capable of devastating the United States and altering the balance of the Cold War.

The series is set in the 20th century against the backdrop of the Cold War, and parts of the production are being filmed in Prague.

Czech production company Stillking Films is handling the local production. The company has previously worked on major international productions filmed in the Czech capital, including The Gray Man.

World.title: Seven Prague Rooftops to Visit Before Summer Ends
World.content:
Summer is already moving on, and Prague’s rooftop season won’t last much longer.

August is the time to make the most of the city’s terraces, sunset views and outdoor events before they disappear for another year.

Here are seven rooftops and terraces worth visiting before autumn arrives.



1. REASON at Masaryčka

Eleven floors above Masaryk Station, REASON offers one of Prague’s newest rooftop dining spots, with views over the city and the Zaha Hadid-designed Masaryčka development.

This summer, its terrace is also home to the seasonal Frerejean Frères Champagne Bar, serving champagne by the glass, cocktails, oysters and light bites. The menu includes THE REASON KIR, made with herbs grown on the rooftop.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and cocktails above Masaryčka.

2. W Prague – ABOVE Rooftop

ABOVE Rooftop at W Prague brings a Mediterranean feel to the top of Wenceslas Square.

The daily Mediterranean Hour runs from 5 to 6 PM, with two spritzes and a Taste of the Mediterranean platter for CZK 990. Oysters are also served from Thursday to Saturday, alongside a programme of summer events and pop-ups.

This summer: Mediterranean Hour, sunset drinks and oysters in the centre.

3. MINUTY Rooftop Terrace

The rooftop at Fairmont Golden Prague offers views across Pařížská, Letná and the city centre from nine floors up.

MINUTY Rooftop Terrace by Golden Eye focuses on champagne, oysters, caviar and cocktails. The terrace is seasonal and is expected to remain open until September, weather permitting.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and caviar with a view.

4. Sky Lounge 360°

For the view alone, Sky Lounge 360° is hard to beat. The rooftop looks across Prague’s historic centre and becomes livelier during the summer months, with DJs, sunset events and Prague Rooftop Festival activities.

It is more about drinks and atmosphere than a long dinner — a good option for an evening that starts at sunset and continues after dark.

This summer: Sunset events, DJs and panoramic views.

5. The Cloud One Rooftop

The Cloud One Prague on Hybernská has its own rooftop cocktail bar overlooking the Masaryčka area.

The relaxed terrace works well for an after-work drink, while summer events bring DJs and a livelier atmosphere at sunset. It has also joined the Prague Rooftop Festival programme.

And if you want to make a night of it, REASON is just a short walk away.

This summer: Cocktails, sunset events and views of Masaryčka.

6. Casablanca Sky Bar

On the sixth floor of The President Hotel, Casablanca Sky Bar looks out over the Vltava and Prague skyline.

With DJs, cocktails and regular sunset events, it has more of a party atmosphere than a traditional hotel rooftop. It is also one of the venues taking part in the Prague Rooftop Festival.

This summer: DJs, cocktails and sunset parties above the Vltava.

7. Monkey Bar

Monkey Bar at Falkensteiner Hotel Prague is a quieter alternative, with a green, jungle-style terrace close to the main railway station.

Every Thursday until the end of August, the terrace hosts BBQ & Beats, combining barbecue, live music and summer drinks. Frozen margaritas are also on the menu.

For daytime plans, there is Jungle Brunch, including a bottomless mimosa option.

This summer: BBQ & Beats every Thursday through August.

World.title: Prague Kettlebell Brand Železná Koule Opens 600-Square-Metre Gym in Karlín
World.content:
Czech kettlebell training brand Železná Koule has opened its largest location yet at Danube House in Prague’s Karlín district.

The new 600-square-metre gym expands the brand’s presence in Prague and comes ahead of the next edition of its flagship Amazing 12 fitness programme.

Železná Koule has built a community around kettlebell training and coached workouts rather than the traditional self-service gym model. The company says more than 20,000 people have trained through its programmes since its launch.

At its Karlín location, members train under the guidance of coaches in small groups. The approach is designed to provide more personal instruction and a structured training environment, rather than simply giving members access to gym equipment.



The new location is also the latest venue for the company’s Amazing 12 programme, a 12-week fitness and body transformation course that combines regular training with nutrition guidance and ongoing support.

What is the Amazing 12 programme?

The programme is aimed at both people who are new to structured strength training and more experienced gym-goers looking for a more organised approach to their workouts.

Although the programme itself lasts 12 weeks, participants first complete a preparation week, making 13 weeks in total. During the programme, they take part in 64 training sessions, with one-hour workouts held every weekday under the supervision of a coach.

Groups are limited to a maximum of five participants, allowing coaches to work closely with each person throughout the programme.

The programme is designed to provide a structured routine covering exercise, nutrition and recovery, with progress tracked throughout the 12 weeks.

The next Amazing 12 programme starts on August 31, 2026, with places available at the new Karlín location as well as Železná Koule gyms in Smíchov and Strašnice.

The Karlín opening is part of the continued expansion of a Czech fitness brand that has developed a following around kettlebell-based training and small-group coaching. For people unfamiliar with the name, Železná Koule roughly translates from Czech as “iron ball,” referring to the kettlebell at the centre of its training approach.

More information about the Amazing 12 programme, including registration, is available at amazing12.cz.

World.title: A New Bus Line to Prague Airport Could Launch This Autumn
World.content:
A new private bus service could soon connect Prague’s main railway station directly with Václav Havel Airport, offering passengers another option for getting between the city center and the airport.

Transport company Dinarica is planning to launch the service at the end of October. The route would run between the main railway station and the airport, providing a direct alternative to the Airport Express operated by České dráhy.

The company says it wants to address one of the main practical problems passengers face when travelling by bus to the airport — luggage storage.

Dinarica plans to use Setra and MAN buses equipped with air conditioning, seat belts and more spacious seating. Each vehicle will accommodate between 70 and 90 passengers.



The planned service would operate from morning until evening, with buses running approximately every two hours.

A one-way ticket is expected to cost around CZK 125, making the service considerably cheaper than the Airport Express. Its fare is set to rise to CZK 200 following the latest price increase.

Prague’s public transport system already offers cheaper ways to reach the airport. Trolleybus 59 and bus 100 connect Václav Havel Airport with the Prague public transport network, but neither provides a direct connection to the main railway station.

Both services are primarily designed as part of the regular city transport system.

If approved and launched as planned, the Dinarica service would give passengers another direct option between Prague’s main railway station and the airport, with a lower fare than the Airport Express.

World.title: More Than Half of Czech Households Could Be Overpaying for Electricity
World.content:
A large number of Czech households may be paying more for electricity than necessary because they are using a distribution tariff that does not match their actual consumption.

A new analysis estimates that switching to a more suitable tariff could save households more than CZK 1.3 billion a year in total.

The analysis was conducted by energy company bezDodavatele.

The company examined electricity consumption at 1,132 household consumption points using the two most common household distribution tariffs, D01d and D02d.

According to data from the Energy Regulatory Office (ERÚ), D01d and D02d are used by around 65 percent of the approximately 6.5 million household consumption points in the Czech Republic.



The analysis found that changing the distribution tariff could reduce electricity costs for more than half of the households examined.

Many households never reconsider their tariff

One reason is that households often keep the same tariff for years without checking whether it still suits their electricity consumption.

A tariff that made sense when a household first connected to the electricity grid may no longer be the cheapest option after its consumption patterns have changed. Many consumers, however, do not regularly review the distribution tariff listed on their electricity bill.

According to the analysis, 53 percent of the households examined could have benefited from a different tariff. Their average potential saving was CZK 728 per year.

For some households, the difference was considerably larger, with potential savings reaching several thousand crowns annually.

Prague households show the highest potential

The analysis found differences between the country’s main electricity distribution areas.

In Prague, where electricity is distributed by PRE, changing the tariff could have been beneficial for 68 percent of the households included in the study. That was the highest proportion recorded among the three distribution zones.

In the EG.D distribution area, which covers much of southern Bohemia and Moravia as well as parts of the Vysočina, Zlín and Olomouc regions, the figure was 51.5 percent.

The lowest share was recorded in the ČEZ distribution area, where 46.3 percent of the households analyzed could potentially benefit from a different tariff.

The picture changes slightly when looking at the size of the potential savings. Although Prague had the highest proportion of households that could benefit from a tariff change, the largest average annual saving was recorded in the ČEZ Distribuce area, at CZK 833 per household.

World.title: Prague Welcomes STARLUX Airlines With New Taipei Connection
World.content:
Taiwanese carrier STARLUX Airlines has launched its first European route, connecting Taipei with Prague.

The airline’s first flight arrived at Václav Havel Airport Prague on Saturday morning after a journey of more than 14 hours. The service is initially being operated with an Airbus A350-900.

STARLUX plans to operate the Prague-Taipei route three times a week at first, with a fourth weekly service scheduled to be added from October.

For passengers traveling beyond Taiwan, the route also offers connections through Taipei to more than 25 destinations across Asia. These include cities in Japan and South Korea, as well as destinations in Southeast Asia, Hong Kong and Macau, according to Simon Liu, STARLUX Airlines’ director of strategy.

The new route makes Prague the airline’s first European destination. STARLUX launched operations only in 2020, two years after the company was founded, but has since positioned itself as a premium international carrier. Skytrax has awarded the airline a five-star rating.



A first-class cabin aimed at luxury travelers

STARLUX is introducing its Prague route with all four of its travel classes: Economy, Premium Economy, Business and First Class.

The First Class cabin has just four seats and comes with a price to match its exclusivity. Return fares can start at around $12,000, or roughly CZK 280,000, although prices vary depending on travel dates and other factors.

The experience begins before passengers reach the aircraft. First Class travelers departing from Prague can use an airport pickup service included with their ticket. In Taipei, the journey can continue with a limousine transfer from the airport to the passenger’s final destination.

Passengers also receive dedicated check-in facilities, priority airport processing and access to a private suite in the airline’s lounge.

On board, each First Class passenger has a private cabin with additional space and privacy, along with an enhanced dining and service offering.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by STARLUX Airlines (@starluxairlines)

Special AIRSORAYAMA aircraft coming to Prague

The aircraft serving Prague will also change later this year.

STARLUX plans to introduce its two specially designed AIRSORAYAMA Airbus A350-1000 aircraft on the Prague route. The planes were created in collaboration with Japanese artist Hajime Sorayama and feature metallic silver and gold liveries.

The airline has confirmed that the A350-1000 will replace the A350-900 on the Prague route from September. The two AIRSORAYAMA aircraft are scheduled to enter regular service on routes including Prague from October 1, when the airline also plans to introduce themed in-flight amenities.

The aircraft were created in partnership with Sorayama, whose work is known for its highly polished metallic representations of robots and the human form.

For Prague passengers, the arrival of the AIRSORAYAMA aircraft will add an unusual visual element to the new long-haul connection. The silver and gold A350-1000s are among STARLUX’s most distinctive aircraft and form part of the airline’s wider effort to combine aviation with contemporary design.

World.title: Inside the Mind: A Conversation with Neuropsychologist Helena Reina Calzado
World.content:
For many people, years of struggling with concentration, memory, or organisation are dismissed as personality traits or everyday stress.

It is often only when life becomes more demanding that they begin to wonder whether something else is going on.

That is where Helena Reina Calzado comes in.

A clinical psychologist and neuropsychologist based in Prague, Helena works with English- and Spanish-speaking patients, providing neuropsychological assessment and cognitive intervention for children, adolescents, and adults experiencing difficulties with attention, memory, executive functioning, and other cognitive abilities.



“Neuropsychology studies the relationship between the brain and behaviour,” Helena explains.

“We look at how someone thinks, processes information, pays attention, and solves problems, and then use that understanding to guide assessment and treatment.”

Neuropsychological assessment focuses on cognitive functioning. The process typically begins with a detailed clinical interview, followed by standardised tests tailored to the person’s specific concerns. When appropriate, neuropsychological intervention aims to improve everyday

cognitive functioning and help patients adapt to daily challenges.

One of the most common reasons people seek her help is a long history of unexplained difficulties that have never been fully understood.

“I often see adults who have spent years developing strategies to cope with attention or learning difficulties without realising there may be an underlying neurodevelopmental condition,” she says.

Conditions such as ADHD or specific learning disorders can go unnoticed well into adulthood, particularly among people who have learned to compensate for their challenges. Many continue functioning successfully until increased stress, career demands, or major life changes make those coping strategies harder to maintain.

“People often come for an assessment because something has changed,” Helena explains. “The strategies that worked for years suddenly aren’t enough, and they want to understand why.”

While awareness of mental health has grown significantly in recent years, Helena believes neuropsychology remains relatively unfamiliar to many people.

“People are much more open to talking about mental health than they were a decade ago,” she says. “But neuropsychology is still less well known. The more accurate information people have, the easier it becomes to challenge misconceptions.”

Outside the consulting room, she also finds moments of perspective in Prague. “Sometimes you forget how beautiful it is,” she says with a smile. “Then you go up to a rooftop, look around, and think, ‘Wow.'”

World.title: Czech business paper explains how and why Tesco will withdraw from Hungary
World.content:
A Czech business paper has reported on how the British-owned supermarket chain Tesco may pull out of Hungary, with its Hungarian interests potentially being sold soon by well-known financial services firms.

Tesco to leave Hungary — and not just us

Another concrete step may have been taken towards the possible sale of Tesco’s Central European interests. According to reports, the British supermarket chain has hired two major American investment banks, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs, to prepare the sale, the Czech business daily e15 reports.

A particularly important detail from the Hungarian Tesco perspective is that, under the current plans, the Hungarian network would not be sold together with the Czech and Slovak stores. The interests in the three countries could instead be offered in two separate packages.

According to the report, which was also summarised by Portfolio, the two investment banks have already sent documentation to potential buyers. This suggests the matter may have moved beyond the stage of merely weighing up a possible sale: the materials sent out also set out the companies’ financial position, prospects and the planned structure of the disposal.

According to Tesco’s data published in June, showing the position at the end of February, it operated 200 stores in Hungary, 184 in the Czech Republic and 182 in Slovakia. The British chain has been present on the Hungarian market since 1995 and employs more than 8,000 people in the country.

Who could the buyers be?

The Czech and Slovak store networks are reportedly to be sold together. Potential buyers are said to include the Schwarz Group, owner of Lidl and Kaufland, as well as Poland’s Biedronka. There is as yet no information on which companies might be interested in the Hungarian business. Tesco, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs have neither confirmed nor commented on the reports. They have not denied them either.

Retail giants such as Spar, Aldi and Tesco may quit Hungary this year

If the sale of the Central European interests does in fact go ahead, it would mark a significant shift in Tesco’s strategy. Chief executive Ken Murphy was still describing the regional business as an integral and successful part of the group in 2023. Behind the scenes, the company may be increasingly focused on the British market. In the ferocious competition there, against Asda and Morrisons, it could gain an advantage if it were able to use money from the Central European sale to cut prices.

Inside the Tesco market. Photo: Daily News Hungary

For the British company, dismantling overseas interests would not be unprecedented. In recent years it has withdrawn from several markets, including Poland, one of the region’s major economies. A sale of further Central European interests and a retreat from the region would therefore fit the direction Tesco has taken in recent times.

The first reports of the possibility of a regional withdrawal surfaced at the beginning of July. At the time, the Financial Times reported that the company was examining the sale of its Central European interests. On the basis of the latest information, it appears that what was then only being floated has since moved into the preparation stage.

Source: Daily News Hungary

World.title: Highest-level heatwave warning extended in Hungary
World.content:
Based on the latest forecast from weather service HungaroMet, the Chief Medical Officer has extended the highest-level nationwide heatwave warning — originally due to expire at the end of Tuesday — until the end of Friday.

Highest-level heatwave warning extended, list of air-conditioned rooms revealed

Persistent heat is expected to continue over the coming days, a joint statement by the national centre for public health and the national directorate-general for disaster management said today. “It is particularly important during this period to look after our own health and look out for one another,” it added.

The elderly, young children, pregnant women, people with chronic conditions — particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions — those with metabolic disorders, and outdoor workers are particularly at risk, the statement said.

Photo: Anadolu/Németi Róbert

More than 2,000 air-conditioned rooms are available to the public across the country, and anyone may use them during hot weather, the government said on Facebook on Tuesday. The list of premises can be found on the disaster management authority’s website.

PM Péter Magyar: last Paks turbine still operating safely

The last one of eight turbines at the Paks nuclear power plant is still operating safely, Prime Minister Péter Magyar said in a post on Facebook early Tuesday. Magyar said officials had been “a couple of millimeters” away from a full shutdown of the NPP around 1:30 in the morning, but “then water levels stopped falling and rose 1.5cm by morning“.

Output of the NPP has been gradually scaled back over the past week as water levels on the Danube, used to cool the plant, have reached record lows. In another post later in the morning, Magyar said a weeks-long decline in water levels on the Danube at Paks had been reversed and levels in the NPP’s cooling water channel had slowly started to rise.

Drought in Budapest. Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

“Pump performance has recovered and the situation has stabilised. Water levels at Paks rose 2cm by morning and the last turbine was operating stably,” he added. Magyar said the turnaround gave “reason for hope”, but added that “the most difficult days still lie ahead. He noted that temperatures were expected to rise over 40 degrees Celsius in the coming days before cooling down from Friday.

Heat record broken again, Hungary one of the hottest countries in Europe

Magyar acknowledged steps by businesses and households that resulted in a 600-700 MW reduction in electricity consumption on Sunday and Monday. He said a working group established to manage the situation would meet in the afternoon to take any necessary decisions

He said a working group established to manage the situation would meet in the afternoon to take any necessary decisions. In a video message from the site of the NPP in the afternoon on Tuesday, Magyar said water levels were now 3cm higher. He added that keeping the last turbine running would depend on water levels and water quality.

Péter Magyar and government spokesperson Vanda Szondi at the Paks NPP. Photo: MTI

He said that the three blocks that were shut down earlier were being kept at a temperature of 260 degrees to allow their restart after water levels rise. He added that restarting the blocks would require “several days”. Magyar noted that rain was forecast for Thursday for areas of Austria and Germany that feed into the Danube and that water could arrive in Hungary within a week, allowing the NPP’s blocks to be restarted.

World.title: Photos, video: new Budapest bridge to be built as project reaches important milestone
World.content:
Budapest’s chief architect has approved the concept for a new pedestrian Budapest bridge to Óbuda Island, with the 138-metre-long, 3.5-metre-wide crossing to be built entirely from private funding, developer Biggeorge Property said on Tuesday.

New Budapest bridge

In a statement to MTI, the company said the slender, clean-lined, step-free bridge — fitted with a lift and cycle wheel channels — will run from the central square of its Waterfront City scheme and span the HÉV line, the embankment and the branch of the Danube to create a direct link with Óbuda Island.

Equipped with street lighting and decorative illumination, the crossing will be the island’s fourth bridge — and the first designed for pedestrians — after Árpád Bridge, K Bridge and H Bridge.

The new pedestrian bridge. Photo: PrtScr/Facebook/Biggeorge property

The concept for the pedestrian bridge was drawn up by Speciálterv. The documentation, which has been coordinated with the relevant authorities and utility providers, could be submitted for permitting within weeks, the statement said.

The developer said the multi-billion-forint public-benefit investment is being financed 100 per cent from private sources, and together with residents of the Waterfront developments it will give several thousand people in the neighbouring housing estates a direct link to the island’s parks within a few minutes’ walk.

Photos: renewed square in Budapest inaugurated

Municipal rental flats will also be built

The statement also said that, as part of the Waterfront Park project, significant transport improvements will be carried out alongside the pedestrian bridge, while the 70-year-old utility network will also be renewed. In addition, several hundred new or refurbished public parking spaces will be created in the area to meet the increased parking demand generated by previously built residential blocks.

Work on the Promenade will continue as planned, and a new street linking Szentendre Road and the Filatorigát HÉV stop will also be completed, with the developer providing the land free of charge.

A further 130 municipal rental flats will also be built in Waterfront Park, which the Budapest city council will lease from the developer at a preferential rate, while the Óbuda district council will receive 1.2 billion forints from the company for social infrastructure development and rental housing construction.

World.title: Former Orbán spin doctor, Árpád Habony, appears to have left Hungary, new address reveals
World.content:
Árpád Habony never held a formal position in Viktor Orbán’s governments, but he was widely regarded as the chief architect of the prime minister’s communications machine and one of the key figures behind the Orbán era’s propaganda network. He was also credited with importing the political tactics of character assassination into Hungarian politics and with helping to orchestrate media attacks on Orbán’s opponents.

Árpád Habony was once one of Hungary’s most influential men

According to the Hungarian media, Habony was Viktor Orbán’s most influential political adviser and spin doctor. Yet no direct link between the two was ever officially established, apart from the fact that Habony had a permanent pass to the Hungarian Parliament at the request of the Prime Minister’s Office. Beyond that, he was able to remain largely invisible to Hungarian voters.

It is widely believed that Habony was behind the Orbán governments’ so-called national consultations. He adapted the campaign techniques of Arthur J. Finkelstein, based on the constant creation of enemies — migration, the Soros plan and Brussels — and on extremely simplified messaging. He also helped to build a Fidesz-aligned media empire and launched political tabloid outlets, including 888.hu and Ripost. He was further linked to the London-based news agency V4NA, described as a branch of Orbán-friendly propaganda media. Fidesz’s official website once referred to him as the prime minister’s adviser.

Árpád Habony and former propaganda minister Antal Rogán. Source: PrtScr/Youtube

No longer a Budapest resident?

That is why a Hungarian court ruled that he should be regarded as a public figure. As such, the Hungarian press has the right to investigate the source of his wealth and his lavish lifestyle. At an Italian sailing competition, for example, he was seen wearing an exceptionally rare Richard Mille watch reportedly worth HUF 160 million.After Viktor Orbán’s defeat on 12 April, and with Péter Magyar’s Tisza movement gaining a supermajority capable of rewriting even the constitution, Habony’s position has come under renewed scrutiny.

According to 24.hu, he no longer lists a Hungarian address in company records. The change was registered on 30 July. He now gives an address in northern Italy, having previously used a central Budapest address in Aranykéz Street. Not long ago, he also withdrew HUF 8.8 billion from Enter-TNMNT, one of his companies, in dividends.Habony owns a 33 per cent stake in LVC Diamond alongside the Fidesz-linked businessman István Garancsi. The company runs five Budapest casinos and the vegas.hu online platform, generating billions of forints in annual profit.

Árpád Habony and former Fidesz parliamentary group leader Máté Kocsis. Photo: PrtScr/Youtube

If you missed: Péter Magyar scraps Orbán’s giant office deal and demands about €1 million back from Orbán-linked businessman

Luxury villa, murky ownership

According to Átlátszó, the Italian address refers to a several-hundred-square-metre villa in one of Varese’s most exclusive districts, about 50 kilometres from Milan. The property was bought for €4.3 million by Influentia Ltd, owned by a private equity fund called Progressus. Hungarian media reported that the fund can be linked to Árpád Habony and former defence minister Kristóf Szalay-Bobrovniczky.

Átlátszó said there are two villas at the address: one measuring 253 sq m and the other 101 sq m. In May 2021, the properties were joined and the interior was altered. The registered owners are Stefano Castelnovo and Ugo Castelnovo, local estate agents. Átlátszó said it sent questions to Habony’s legal representative, Influentia Ltd and the two estate agents, but had not yet received a reply.

PM Orbán’s spin doctor, Árpád Habony, allegedly tried to connect Trump with Georgia’s “pro-Russia” government

World.title: Small planet named after Hungarian music legend Gábor Presser
World.content:
The International Astronomical Union has named a small planet after Gábor Presser, the Hungarian pianist, songwriter and singer.

According to a Facebook post by Hungarian astronomer László Kiss, the celestial body was discovered by Hungarian astronomer Krisztián Sárneczky in August 2013.

In its description, the IAU said that Presser, born in 1948, is “a Hungarian composer, pianist and singer” and “a key member of the former Omega and Locomotiv GT bands, considered among the most significant Hungarian bands”. It added that he is the musical director of the Vígszínház in Budapest and “one of the most prominent figures in Hungarian popular music”.

Presser is not the first Hungarian cultural figure to have his name placed among the stars. Sárneczky has also named discoveries after the writer and Nobel laureate László Krasznahorkai and the film director Béla Tarr. Earlier celestial bodies were named after the 19th-century writer Mór Jókai, the poet János Arany and the industrialist Ábrahám Ganz.

World.title: Horror over Paks II NPP overpricing: did Orbán-linked and Tisza-affiliated businessmen and politicians pocket the cash?
World.content:
It is hardly surprising that the Paks expansion required the purchase of a number of former fields, woodlands and pastures from their owners. What is less easy to explain is why the state company responsible for the project reportedly paid a price that was 100 times higher than expected. Once again, the deal appears to feature businessmen and names close to the Orbán system.

Huge corruption scandal saw money disappear in Paks

The first, and second, glance at the case is enough to make it deeply troubling. Attention was drawn to it by Ákos Hadházy, the former independent MP, who previously sat with Momentum, and who announced on Facebook that he had also filed a criminal complaint. Documents published alongside his post suggest that, in 2020, the company responsible for the expansion bought a 24-hectare forest-and-pasture plot at a price 100 times higher than normal.

The Paks II NPP extension project: first concrete. Photo: Facebook/Levente Magyar

Mr Hadházy says that at the time land of this quality in the area would have been worth no more than 1.5 million forints, yet the contract was signed with the then owner at 150 million forints per hectare. The total purchase price therefore came to 3.5 billion forints.

The stolen money could have prevented the present crisis

In all, Paksi Ipari Park Nkft, the state-owned company carrying out the long-delayed Paks II project, bought similar land for a total of 32 billion forints, again, according to Mr Hadházy, at vastly inflated prices. He argues that the money siphoned off would have been enough to prevent the current cooling problems, improve the pumps and ensure the plant could keep operating even when the Danube’s water level is low.

Szekszárd’s council did not want to release the purchase contracts, and Transparency International had to warn it twice that it was obliged to disclose the documents and could not even black out the names of the owners receiving the purchase price.

According to Mr Hadházy, one of the beneficiaries was the company of Zsolt Kapitány, a longstanding Fidesz loyalist. “He made more than one billion by buying the dilapidated buildings of the former meat plant in Szekszárd from the state for a pittance, then selling them on to Paks 2 at a much higher price a year later,” Mr Hadházy wrote. He reported the businessman at the time, but says the prosecution service threw out the complaint on what he regards as a ridiculous pretext.

If you missed: Péter Magyar scraps Orbán’s giant office deal and demands about €1 million back from Orbán-linked businessman

Did later Tisza politicians also benefit?

The former MP says there is another twist. While he does not see any other familiar Fidesz figures on the list apart from Mr Kapitány, he does see Tisza-linked names.

He says the reason such enormous sums ended up with Fidesz figures — and later with people who went on to become Tisza politicians — was that the land had first had to be reclassified, because the nuclear plant could not acquire agricultural land directly. The fat profits were pocketed by those who acted as intermediaries and arranged the process.

PM Péter Magyar in Paks. Photo: MTI

“Who exactly these clever fixers were, and how much they made from the affair, will have to be decided by an investigation. If we really are moving towards a change of regime, one can only hope that an inquiry will not be refused even if people close to the new government are among those implicated,” Mr Hadházy wrote.

World.title: Heat record broken again, Hungary one of the hottest countries in Europe
World.content:
Hungary was one of the hottest countries in Europe on Monday, with maximum temperatures mostly ranging between 36 and 40 degrees Celsius. Yesterday the temperature in southern Budapest dropped to just 26.8 degrees Celsius at dawn, which is another heat record.

Heat records broken on Monday

On 3 August, the temperature in southern Budapest dropped to just 26.8 degrees Celsius at dawn, surpassing the previous national record of 25.1C, measured in 2017, weather service HungaroMet reported on Tuesday.

Hungary one of hottest countries in Europe on Monday

Europe continues to be characterised by hot weather, with maximum temperatures exceeding 30C across much of the continent.

World.title: The aluminium cans gain ground in Romania: its share of DRS packaging has risen to 29.3%
World.content:
News from Companies

Official RetuRO data analysed by Every Can Counts shows an increase from 21.6% in the first quarter of 2024 to 29.3% in the second quarter of 2026. One driver of this growth is the younger generation, drawn to the graphic freedom the can offers and to its infinite recyclability.

Since the launch of the Deposit Return System at the end of 2023, the aluminium can has risen visibly within Romania's beverage packaging mix. According to official RetuRO reports, metal's share of all DRS packaging placed on the market grew from 21.6% in the first quarter of 2024 to 29.3% in the second quarter of 2026. The same trend appears in returns, where metal reached 28.8%, up from 18.7% at the start of the system.



That is an increase of almost eight percentage points in two years, in a market where plastic remains dominant but is declining: from 61% to 51% of volumes placed on the market over the same period. Glass has held steady, at around 20%.

Metal rises quarter after quarter



The can's share has grown steadily since 2024, peaking in the second quarter of 2026, which points to a structural trend. The explanation lies in several overlapping factors: the widening range of beverages sold in cans, a clearer consumer preference for lightweight, portable packaging, and a context in which aluminium is becoming the material of choice for brands building their identity around sustainability.



The trend also holds internationally. According to an April 2026 McKinsey analysis, the metal packaging segment continued to show steady volume growth, and in certain categories metal is gaining market share thanks to portability, recyclability, and premiumisation trends.



The aluminium can is recycled indefinitely, with no loss of quality, and can return to the shelf in as little as 60 days. Every recycled can saves up to 95% of the energy needed to produce a new one from raw materials.

The can as a space for brand expression



The can's rise also has a cultural dimension, most visible among younger consumers. The surface of the can works as a continuous canvas, with no separate label and no interruptions, giving designers a creative space that other packaging materials cannot match. Today's metal printing technologies allow intense colours, matte finishes, phosphorescent inks, and limited editions, and producers offer dozens of sizes and decoration techniques for brands looking to stand out on the shelf.



For young consumers, packaging has become an extension of personal style. An article published by Ad Age in 2024 found that 81% of Gen Z consumers have tried a product because of its packaging, and 63% repeated the purchase for the same reason. The same generation sees metal as the most environmentally responsible choice, according to 2024 McKinsey research indicating that 60% of young people prefer recyclable packaging. Across Europe, a study conducted by the agency Caramel for Sonoco found that 82% of consumers are more likely to buy a product that comes in metal packaging.



These preferences explain why more and more beverage brands are choosing the can: on the shelf, it becomes part of how they are recognised.

Romanians want recycling to become an experience



The Deposit Return System built the habit of recycling quickly. Romania's national recycling rate for aluminium cans reached 75% in 2025, more than double the level of 2022, when European Commission data indicated just 35%. Yet the Every Can Counts Global Study 2025, based on a sample of more than 16,000 participants across 16 countries, including 1,013 in Romania, shows that Romanians want more from the act of recycling.



Three in four Romanians (75%) say they would recycle more if the experience were more enjoyable or more interactive, through rewards, games, or apps that track and celebrate recycling. At the same time, Romanians are among the most engaged consumers in the world: 71% feel personally responsible for recycling, the highest figure globally, and 91% believe producers should be required to use packaging that is fully recyclable or made from recycled materials.



The data points to a market ready for more than automated collection: Romanians want more accessible return points (38%) and a faster process (41%), but above all an experience that gives the gesture meaning.

"The fact that more and more brands are choosing the aluminium can is good news for circularity. It is a packaging that is infinitely recyclable and already collected at scale, which means that every can recycled can become another can, in as little as 60 days. When people see how quickly the loop closes, recycling becomes a gesture with meaning. That is what we set out to do at Every Can Counts: to bring circularity closer to people, so that every can truly counts." said David Van Heuverswyn, Global Director of Every Can Counts.

From the shelf to an art installation



Every Can Counts Romania responds directly to this need through visible projects and interactive activations with the public. The "I CAN" installations, made entirely from aluminium cans by Romanian artist Sergiu Chihaia, turn recycling into an experience people can see and touch. Through campaigns and public art projects, the programme brings circularity closer to people and gives an everyday gesture a moment of cultural impact.



Counties with strong sustainability initiatives, such as Bucharest, Timiș, Cluj, Ilfov, and Constanța, lead the national rankings for recycling rates.

Data sources: RetuRO; the Every Can Counts Global Recycling Habits and Attitudes 2025 study; Ad Age, 2024; McKinsey research, 2024; the McKinsey analysis "No ordinary disruption: State of the packaging and paper industry," April 2026; and the Caramel study for Sonoco.



*This is a press release.

World.title: Romanian PM says no fuel supply problems expected as energy system remains under pressure
World.content:
Romanian authorities do not currently expect problems with fuel supplies for households, agriculture, or transport companies, interim prime minister Ilie Bolojan said on Tuesday, August 4. His comments came after three government meetings on the country's energy situation, fuel supplies, and measures to maintain the stability of the national power system.

Ilie Bolojan, who is also the acting minister of energy, said the situation had improved, with the OMV refinery processing at full capacity and Petromidia operating at around 85% of capacity. The latter is expected to return to normal operations by the end of the week.

“At this moment, we do not anticipate problems regarding fuel supplies for the population, agriculture and transport operators," Bolojan said.

The assurances come amid a sharp rise in fuel prices. Diesel has climbed above RON 10.80 per liter in Bucharest after more than a week of sustained increases, while gasoline is selling for more than RON 9.50 per liter at some filling stations, Euronews Romania reported. According to the broadcaster, Romania recorded the highest increase in fuel prices in the European Union over the past week, at 7.5%, adding around RON 57 to the cost of a full tank.

In this context, president Nicușor Dan announced on Tuesday that he had signed the decree promulgating legislation introducing measures aimed at stabilizing the petroleum products market amid rising fuel prices.

"Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and extreme volatility on the international oil market have generated rapid increases in fuel prices, including in our country," Dan said. "Rapid state intervention was once again necessary because these price increases translate into higher costs throughout the economy for citizens and businesses, with direct effects on purchasing power, economic competitiveness, and the stability of critical national sectors."

According to the president, the legislation provides for declaring a crisis situation on the petroleum products market, reducing the excise duty on diesel, capping commercial markups, and temporarily banning diesel exports without prior approval from the Energy Ministry in order to prioritize domestic consumption. It also introduces a solidarity contribution for large oil companies.

The government also reviewed the situation at the Cernavodă nuclear power plant amid low Danube levels. Dredging and rock removal works are continuing, while an operation involving the sinking of barges is planned once all technical conditions are met.

The measures are intended to extend the operation of Unit 2 for as long as possible, according to the prime minister.

“The water level at Cernavodă has not fallen further. This is a good sign, but the situation remains difficult, and we are continuing all measures to keep the unit operating for as long as possible," Bolojan said. "Every day of operation means additional energy for the National Energy System.”

The prime minister also met with major electricity suppliers to discuss measures aimed at maintaining balance in the energy system. The talks covered ways of ensuring market liquidity through the payment of outstanding amounts under the compensation scheme, as well as cooperation with grid operator Transelectrica on voluntary reductions in electricity consumption by large industrial consumers.

The government also agreed with energy regulator ANRE to accelerate the issuance of documents required for projects already at an advanced stage, allowing new power generation capacity to come online as quickly as possible.

At the same time, the government is preparing a backup mechanism that could temporarily limit electricity consumption by major industrial users if voluntary reductions prove insufficient during peak hours.

“In the coming days, we will adopt a government decision implementing the mechanism provided by law for situations in which voluntary consumption reductions are not sufficient to cover electricity demand during peak hours," Ilie Bolojan said.

Under the mechanism, large consumers could receive 24 hours' notice of temporary consumption limits, depending on the nature of their operations and the capacity of the National Energy System.

World.title: DP World pilots Western Europe-Romania rail route for finished vehicles, with Aiud as regional distribution hub
World.content:
DP World announced that it completed its first delivery of finished vehicles by rail from Zeebrugge in Belgium to Aiud, Romania, launching a new intermodal corridor between Western and Southeastern Europe. The company plans to develop Aiud into a regional distribution hub for finished vehicles serving Romania and neighboring markets.

The initial shipment is destined for Chișinău, Moldova, with the vehicles continuing their journey by road from Aiud. According to DP World, it is the company's first vehicle rail operation in Europe managed end-to-end.

Following the pilot, DP World plans to introduce a regular service with twice-monthly operations during the second half of 2026. The company also plans to establish similar connections between Aiud and other European ports, including Koper in Slovenia.

“Automotive companies are looking to reduce their exposure to long-distance road transport. By combining rail and road in a single integrated service, we are giving customers greater reliability, lower emissions and a solution that can scale as trade flows across Europe continue to evolve,” said Dragoș Călin, Director Freight, Balkans at DP World.

The company estimates that using the intermodal rail and road service can reduce CO2 emissions by up to 55% compared with equivalent long-haul road transport. It said the service could also provide greater cost certainty and predictability by reducing exposure to changing European road transport regulations, road usage charges, and cross-border administrative procedures.

“Our strategy is to build a more connected European logistics network, creating new trade corridors and giving customers greater choice in how they move goods across the continent," said DP World Romania CEO Svitlana Balaban. "Aiud is an important part of that vision, creating new links between western European ports and markets across southeastern Europe.”

DP World's multimodal logistics terminal in Aiud opened in 2024 following a EUR 21 million investment. The 180,000 sqm facility is located next to the A10 motorway and connected to Romania's national rail network, providing container handling, storage, customs and freight forwarding services.
