World.title: Estonian firefighters facing tough conditions battling Sardinia wildfires
World.content:
Estonian firefighters who have headed to Italy to battle large-scale wildfires there will face rapidly changing conditions, very different from those seen in wildfires at home, the Rescue Board said on Tuesday.

Estonia will send 20 firefighters to Sardinia, at a time when southern Europe battles blazes and extreme heat. The island off the west coast of Italy is both mountainous and heavily forested.

Speaking to Vikerraadio on Tuesday morning, the Rescue Board's (Päästeamet) Kaarel Langemets noted how firefighting in that region differs greatly from the situation at home, though some of the Estonians have experience of fires like those in Sardinia.

"Compared with our forest fires, wildfires in Southern Europe are very different. The terrain, climate and vegetation are different. On our latest missions, about half of the team members had been there before, while the other half are newcomers," said the leader of one of the teams heading to Sardinia to help fight the blazes.

"A previous deployment to Spain gave the firefighters valuable experience and an idea of what to expect this time. "Naturally, Sardinia is somewhat different from Spain. Sardinia is full of deciduous trees, but it is also mountainous and hot, which poses a major challenge for firefighters," Langemets went on.

Kaarel Langemets Source: ERR

Not only are conditions different, but methodologies too. "While Estonian firefighters mainly attack fires with hoses, laying kilometers of hose through the forest, in Southern Europe the focus is more on monitoring and scouting where the fire is spreading and where it can actually be stopped. Firebreaks are created instead, and that is exactly what our firefighters have been trained to do. It is possible to create strips of bare ground because the soil layer there is virtually non-existent," Langemets explained.

Estonia faces a very different problem because fires can burn underground, usually when peat is present. "The fire does not even have to be very large, and we can contain it quite quickly, but it can spread several meters deep into peat soils. In Sardinia, the main concern is the mountainous terrain, where fire spreads very rapidly uphill. Add high temperatures, almost zero humidity and wind, and you have the perfect storm. Those are exactly the conditions in Spain and France today," Langemets continued.

"The main firefighting work takes place from early morning until sunset," Langemets added. The Estonian personnel will be integrated into local rescue units.

Langemets was under no illusion about potential hazards. "The most dangerous situation in mountainous areas is when the wind changes direction. Firefighters must always leave themselves an escape route back to a safe area. Continuous reconnaissance of the fire is the single most important thing," he added.

Estonian fire fighters helped control wildfires in Spain in August 2025. Source: Estonian Rescue Board

As for immediate causes of the Sardinia fires, these can vary, though human factors are usually present. "Not maliciously, but because of human actions. It could be a cigarette butt, or something from a vehicle, such as a hot exhaust, which ignites vegetation," the expert said.

As for natural causes, Spain, for instance, is also known for thunderstorms which produce little to no rainfall. "It was an incredible thunderstorm that ignited a great many wildfires," he noted.

The Estonian team is being based in Monte Pisano, northern Sardinia, and is due to return mid-month. The deployment follows the intense wildfires seen in Southern Europe recently, mainly in France, Spain, northern Portugal, and northern Italy, following the latest heatwave, which brought temperatures of over 40 C to a region which has already seen a long summer of heatwaves.

The Estonians are to use all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), and teams of up to three may also assist helicopter crews in firefighting where needed.

World.title: Gallery: New Tallinn exhibition explores the aesthetics of abandoned spaces
World.content:
At Tallinn's Okapi Gallery, "Private Property" brings together artists Alexei Gordin and Dasha Trofimova in an exploration of abandoned spaces, memory and social change.

The joint exhibition, which opened Friday, examines the visual and emotional layers left behind in abandoned buildings and their links to geopolitical shifts, trauma, the absurd performative qualities of spaces and the human experience of neglect.

Trofimova, a Kazakhstan-born artist based in Riga, and Gordin approach abandoned spaces as a form of archaeological research, uncovering layers that reveal traces of different eras and the experiences tied to them.

Their works recreate these encounters through installations, interventions and documentation that capture the temporary nature of site-specific artistic processes.

Gordin uses abandoned environments as backdrops for ironic commentary on contemporary society and its contradictions, often writing his messages directly onto walls with spray paint.

Trofimova creates temporary large-scale installations from furniture and everyday objects found in abandoned buildings. Her works focus on fragile structures and balance, reflecting how political systems and economic crises can eventually trigger collapse.

"Private Property" will remain open at Okapi Gallery through August 30.

World.title: Viljandi Folk unveils 'Three-Four!' theme for 2027
World.content:
Viljandi Folk Music Festival has unveiled "Three-Four!" as the theme for its 34th edition next summer, highlighting the popular festival's signature crowd chant.

Longtime festivalgoers will recognize the phrase as part of a familiar call-and-response: when someone onstage or in the audience shouts "Kolm-neli!" ("Three-four!"), the crowd responds, "Hea bänd!" ("Good band!").

Organizers say the two-part chant has become an unofficial code or password connecting the Viljandi Folk community.

"Three-four!" is also part of a familiar musical cue used by performers for generations to count in the start of a song, and further reflects the role of musicians, or "good bands," in keeping traditions alive.

Day two of the 33rd Viljandi Folk Festival. Friday, July 24, 2026. Source: Martin Kosseson

Next year, Viljandi Folk will focus on hopeful beginnings and the power of inspiring examples in keeping traditions alive.

Chief organizer Ando Kiviberg said traditions are best passed down not under pressure, but through participation and enthusiasm, encouraging people to sing along to a song they know, learn a tune or even make them their own.

"A compelling example is far more likely to encourage people to follow the beautiful customs that enrich our cultural heritage," he added.

The 34th Viljandi Folk Music Festival will take place July 22–25, 2027.

World.title: Coop celebrates bigger market share but won't hike prices in wake of Prisma acquisition
World.content:
At the end of August, Coop Eesti Keskühistu will acquire Prisma Peremarket's stores in Estonia. By the end of November, all former Prisma stores will operate under the Coop brand.

According to Coop representative Rainer Rohtla, Coop and Prisma are currently working to finalize the transaction.

"We have signed a purchase agreement under which Coop will acquire Prisma Peremarket as a company, and based on that agreement, the Competition Authority has approved the completion of the transaction. Right now, all the preparations needed to complete the deal are underway, which means a great deal of work internally for both Coop and Prisma. The acquisition will take place on August 31, less than a month from now, after which Coop Eesti Keskühistu will become the sole owner of Prisma Peremarket," Rohtla said.

He added that during the second or third week of September, the current Prisma stores will be transferred to various Coop regional cooperatives, which will begin operating them.

On product selection, Rohtla said the goal is to preserve the assortment customers are accustomed to, though doing so will require a major effort from the company.

"Prisma's product range is very distinctive. It includes many Scandinavian products as well as many Coop private-label products that are not currently sold in Coop stores. This is one of the areas creating a significant workload for us. To keep Prisma's entire product range available in stores as it is today, we need to expand our logistics and supply chain capabilities. Nothing will be removed, but we will also add many of the products Coop customers already love. The rollout of Prisma's best-selling and most popular products to other Coop stores will take place during the first half of next year. By July next year, Prisma's most popular products will be available in Coop stores across Estonia," Rohtla said.

Rohtla also said there is no reason to fear price increases, citing current market conditions.

"Even if we wanted to raise prices, given how intense competition is in Estonia's retail sector, how much food prices have already increased in recent years and the fact that consumers' purchasing power and confidence remain low, there is simply no room in the market for price increases," he said.

One of the aims of the acquisition is to increase Coop's market share.

"Our market share in Tallinn is around 5 percent, compared with 23 percent nationwide. Now our market share in Tallinn will increase to 17 percent," Rohtla said.

Rohtla again declined to disclose the purchase price for Prisma's stores or say how quickly Coop expects to recoup its investment.

"Time will tell. We are very optimistic, knowing what we plan to do to make the investment pay off, but that's certainly not something I want to disclose today," he said.

Analyst: Prisma's exit will have no effect on food prices

Economist Raul Eamets agreed that a larger market share for one retail chain does not necessarily lead to higher prices.

"There is actually fairly strong competition in the grocery market, particularly since Lidl entered Estonia a few years ago. I don't think Prisma's transition to the Coop brand will have any significant impact on prices. If you look at the profit margins of the major retail chains — how much profit they make as a share of sales — we're talking about just a few percent. Simply having a larger market share doesn't suddenly give a retailer the ability to manipulate prices," Eamets said.

He added that food prices in Estonia are driven primarily by global factors.

"Price levels are influenced less by domestic competition than by food producers' prices and, above all, global market prices. Those are what determine food prices. We are highly dependent on imported food ingredients and finished products. According to the latest figures, prices for imported goods increased by 7 percent," the economist said.

Rocca al Mare keskuse Prisma, one of the largest outlets. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"The reality is that Estonia cannot fully feed itself, so we depend on what happens outside the country. Unfortunately, there is little we can do to influence that," he added.

On April 7, Coop Eesti Keskühistu and Finnish retail group SOK signed a purchase agreement under which Coop will acquire AS Prisma Peremarket and its 13 stores in Estonia, located in Tallinn and Harju County, Tartu, Narva and Rapla. The parties will also begin a strategic partnership to bring Finnish food and consumer goods to more than 300 Coop stores across Estonia.

The transaction does not include the Prisma brand or the Sokos Hotel Viru. The parties have not disclosed the value of the deal.

World.title: Iraq’s liquidity crisis causes delays in paying public servants
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is experiencing a serious financial and liquidity problem, causing delays in paying state employees.

The fall in income from oil, due to the difficulties of exporting via the Strait of Hormuz, has put the Finance Ministry of Iraq in a deficit by trillions of dinars.

The Iraqi government is considering home loans to finance its enormous monthly salaries.

Crude oil exports, which account for approximately 90 percent of Iraq’s federal income, fell dramatically because of the military operations in the region and maritime shipping difficulties.

Iraq requires between 8 and 11 trillion Iraqi dinars ($6.1 billion to $8.4 billion) every month to pay millions of governmental staff and pensioners.

The country’s income fell significantly below expenditure demands, resulting in a large monthly shortfall and an acute cash crisis.

Payrolls have experienced extraordinary delays, causing public concern and reducing local economic activity.

Financing shortfalls have put a burden on government-owned enterprises, particularly drug delivery in the health sector.

Authorities aim to engage in temporary local borrowing to avoid incurring further international debt, as well as long-term calls for diversified state resources.

World.title: Dana Gas, Crescent Petroleum supply Baghdad with gas for electricity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum said on Tuesday that they started supplying the electricity ministry with natural gas from the Khor Mor field in Iraqi Kurdistan under an agreement to support the country’s electricity output.

An agreement was reached last December between the Electricity Ministry and the two companies to supply 100 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the Khor Mor facility to the Taza gas-fired power plant in Kirkuk province for a period of one year.

The step took place after a project to increase the production capacity of the Khor Mor gas field to 750 million cubic feet per day was completed.

The completion of the expansion project increased the availability of additional gas quantities to local markets through the pipeline network, as reported by Shafaq News.

Majid Jafar, CEO of Crescent Petroleum and Managing Director of Dana Gas, stated that the gas transfer to the Electricity Ministry in Baghdad marks an important milestone in Iraqi Kurdistan’s gas sector growth.

Jafar explained that this development will address the growing demand for electricity and enhance the services offered to residents.

Richard Hall, CEO of Dana Gas Group, described the deal as an important step reflecting the outcomes of the production growth program.

According to Hall, the agreement paves the way for enhanced collaboration within Iraq’s energy sector, strengthens energy security, and contributes to the stability of the electricity grid.

The Khor Mor gas project provides the fuel required to produce more than 80 percent of the energy in Iraqi Kurdistan, which supplies power to over eight million people.

World.title: Iraq unveils tourism vision 2035 to attract 10 million visitors
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has unveiled an ambitious long-term strategy to transform its tourism sector, aiming to attract 10 million visitors by 2035 through infrastructure upgrades, workforce development, and the preservation of the country’s rich historical, cultural, and religious heritage.

The Iraqi Tourism Authority announced on Tuesday that it has finalized the Iraq Tourism Vision 2035, a roadmap launched under the slogan “A Prosperous and Competitive Iraq.” The initiative is designed to position Iraq as a leading tourism destination in the region while supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

Ali Yassin, spokesperson for the Tourism Authority, said the agency will begin organizing workshops in Baghdad, Mosul, Basra, Karbala, and Erbil to present the vision’s objectives and implementation mechanisms to stakeholders across the country.

The workshops aim to engage local governments, tourism professionals, and investors in executing the strategy over the coming decade.

According to the authority, the plan seeks to attract 10 million tourists by 2035, with a focus on promoting Iraq’s archaeological, cultural, religious, and natural attractions.

Officials said achieving the target will require significant investment in tourism infrastructure, including improving transportation, accommodation, visitor services, and restoring key heritage sites across the country.

The strategy also calls for the rehabilitation and maintenance of archaeological landmarks, museums, religious sites, and other destinations that showcase Iraq’s diverse historical legacy.

The Tourism Vision 2035 is built around three strategic pillars: integration, sustainability, and quality.

Officials said these principles will guide efforts to create a more competitive tourism industry while ensuring long-term preservation of Iraq’s cultural and natural resources.

The plan also emphasizes improving coordination among government institutions and the private sector to encourage investment and strengthen the country’s tourism ecosystem.

In addition to infrastructure projects, the Tourism Authority highlighted the importance of developing skilled professionals capable of supporting the industry’s growth.

The vision includes programs to strengthen the capabilities of workers in the tourism sector through training and capacity-building initiatives, recognizing that qualified personnel are essential to delivering high-quality visitor experiences.

The Tourism Authority said the long-term strategy reflects its commitment to restoring Iraq’s position as a prominent international tourism destination.

By combining investment in infrastructure, heritage preservation, sustainability, and workforce development, officials hope the plan will contribute to economic growth while showcasing Iraq’s unique cultural and historical assets to visitors from around the world.

World.title: Iraq liquidity crisis does not mean bankruptcy, says government financial adviser
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq liquidity crisis should not be interpreted as a sign that the country is running out of money or facing bankruptcy, according to government financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Salih. He emphasized that the Iraqi government retains sufficient financial and administrative tools to continue paying salaries and meeting its core obligations despite ongoing cash flow pressures.

Speaking to Shafaq News on Tuesday, Salih explained that the current challenge stems from timing mismatches between oil revenues entering the treasury and the government’s monthly expenditure commitments, particularly public sector salaries.

Salih stressed that Iraq’s financial pressures are primarily linked to liquidity management rather than a shortage of national wealth.

According to him, the government’s current challenges include:

Timing differences between oil revenue receipts and monthly spending obligations.

High levels of public expenditure.

Continued expansion of public sector employment.

Weak non-oil revenues.

Regional tensions affecting trade and oil exports.

He said these factors have created temporary liquidity pressures but do not indicate a severe financial crisis.

The financial adviser said the government can continue paying salaries and maintaining essential public services through several financial management tools.

These include:

Efficient liquidity management.

Prioritizing essential expenditures such as salaries.

Rescheduling non-urgent investment projects when necessary.

Improving tax and fee collection.

Reducing financial waste.

Increasing non-oil government revenues.

Salih also noted that domestic or external borrowing remains available if required, provided borrowing remains within safe public debt limits and supports financial stability.

Looking ahead, Salih said Iraq must accelerate long-term economic reforms to reduce dependence on oil revenues.

He highlighted several priorities:

Diversifying oil export routes.

Developing transportation and energy infrastructure.

Expanding non-oil revenue sources.

Building a more resilient economy capable of absorbing regional and global shocks.

He concluded that sustainable financial stability cannot rely solely on oil income and will require broader economic diversification and structural reforms.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports surpass 1.25 million bpd in July
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s seaborne crude oil shipments increased in July 2026 by more than 153 percent, or 757,000 barrels per day, compared to the previous month.

Iraqi oil shipments by sea rose to over 1.25 million barrels per day in July compared to 493,000 barrels per day in June, according to Attaqa News.

Despite this partial recovery, Iraqi shipments remain significantly lower than pre-war levels, reflecting a 63 percent decline from the July 2025 figure of 3.38 million barrels per day.

With the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Baghdad’s major marine trade route, strains on the state budget are increasing due to declining oil earnings.

The decrease in revenue from oil exports has driven the Iraqi government to accelerate its search for alternative land routes to export crude oil via neighboring countries.

In July, Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports reached one million barrels per day for the first time since March 2026, marking the end of a steep fall.

The country’s oil exports totaled 3.31 million barrels per day in January, 3.34 million barrels per day in February, 542,000 barrels per day in March, 132,000 barrels per day in April, 98,000 barrels per day in May, 493,000 barrels per day in June, and 1.25 million barrels per day in July.

The figures show that Iraq’s average offshore oil exports fell by 60 percent between January and July 2026, hitting 1.31 million barrels per day compared to 3.33 million barrels per day during the same period in 2025.

The partial restart of commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz prior to increased tensions and the development of the situation fueled this spike.

World.title: Iraq clarifies role in oil tanker transit through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry has clarified that it is not responsible for the movement of crude oil tankers after they leave Iraqi export terminals, emphasizing that buyers assume full responsibility for transporting shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The statement comes as Iraq continues to navigate regional security challenges affecting energy exports, while officials report gradual improvements in crude oil sales in recent months.

Oil Ministry spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi said Iraq continues to sell crude oil under the Free on Board (FOB) system, meaning ownership and responsibility for the cargo transfer to the buyer once the shipment is loaded at Iraqi ports.

According to Al-Rikabi, tankers carrying Iraqi crude continue to transit the Strait of Hormuz after departing export terminals. However, he stressed that the ministry is not responsible for the vessels’ navigation routes or for securing the necessary transit approvals.

“The ministry sells crude oil at the port, after which the buyer assumes responsibility for transporting and managing the shipment,” Al-Rikabi said.

He added that the ministry neither owns the tankers nor oversees their operations once they leave Iraqi waters.

Despite transferring responsibility to buyers, Al-Rikabi said the Oil Ministry continues monitoring tanker movements through international vessel-tracking systems.

He noted that Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) follows shipments until they reach their destination refineries, allowing authorities to track export deliveries without directly managing vessel operations.

Some tankers transporting Iraqi crude carry cargoes of up to 2 million barrels, according to the ministry.

Al-Rikabi also indicated that Iraq’s oil export performance has improved steadily in recent months despite disruptions linked to the regional security situation and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

He said sales last month exceeded those recorded in the previous month, continuing a gradual recovery following earlier export challenges caused by tensions affecting maritime traffic through the strategic waterway.

The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world’s most important oil shipping routes, carrying a significant share of global crude exports, making uninterrupted transit critical for Iraq’s energy sector and international oil markets.

World.title: Iraq launches 3,000-cubic-meter gas storage facility in Najaf
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated a gas storage project as part of the Oil Ministry’s efforts to raise storage capacity in line with current operations to boost gas output.

The Iraqi Oil Ministry revealed Monday the start of trial operations at a new gas storage facility in the central Iraqi province of Najaf.

Undersecretary for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber said in a statement that the new gas depot has a storage capacity of 3,000 cubic meters and is part of efforts to boost production and storage capabilities, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The step also reflects the ministry’s efforts to develop the transportation, storage, and distribution systems of liquefied gas, according to Saber.

The Iraqi official explained that the inauguration of the depot at the trial operation stage is certainly an important milestone in improving the capacity of strategic reserves and increasing the flexibility of the supply system.

The initiative will ensure that the requirements for liquefied gas in the central provinces and other cities are adequately met.

The delivery of liquefied gas to the new depot via pipelines, as opposed to tanker trucks, will adhere to safety standards and enhance the stability of supplies.

World.title: Iraq dollar exchange rate rises in local markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq dollar exchange rate increased in local currency markets on Tuesday, with the U.S. dollar gaining 1,000 Iraqi dinars compared with the previous trading session, according to market data published by local outlets.

Despite the increase in parallel market rates, the official exchange rate set by the Central Bank of Iraq remains at 131,000 Iraqi dinars per $100.

Exchange rates recorded in major Iraqi cities were as follows:

City Selling Price (IQD per $100) Buying Price (IQD per $100) Baghdad 152,750 152,250 Erbil 152,000 151,500 Basra 152,250 152,000

The latest figures indicate that the parallel market continues to trade well above the official exchange rate, reflecting the ongoing gap between official pricing and street market demand.

Currency exchange rates in Iraq are monitored closely by businesses, importers, and consumers because fluctuations in the parallel market can affect the prices of imported goods and broader market activity.

World.title: From launch to data, tech to Isro facility, pvt firms to get 30-100% subsidy
World.content:
BENGALURU: Indian private space companies and non-government entities will receive govt support ranging from 30% to 100% on everything from launch services and technology transfer to satellite data and access to Isro facilities under two new schemes of the Department of Space (DoS).

The incentives â Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and the Price Support Scheme â being implemented by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are aimed at lowering entry barriers, making Indian space businesses globally competitive and accelerating private participation across the sector.

The larger of the two initiatives is the Launch Services Price-support Scheme, with a budget of Rs 800 crore over five years until June 2031.

The scheme seeks to boost domestic commercial launch operations and strengthen India's position as a global launch hub.

IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka told TOI: âThe idea is to make the launches competitive. Therefore, we are trying to defray the cost of launch, thereby making the launch cost globally competitive. The ultimate beneficiary will be the satellite launch.â

Under Category A, eligible entities can receive up to 50% support for using Isro and DoS launch facilities.





The benefit extends to NGEs, government entities and launch vehicle providers.

Category B offers a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower, for Indian small launch vehicles carrying satellites, experiments or payloads weighing up to 500 kg. The support is available to satellite owners and operators.

The subsidy would apply to launches by Indian private entities from Indian soil too.

âIt will be applicable to [Skyrootâs] Vikram also. Any satellite launch by an Indian company... from Indian soil... we will directly pay the satellite guys $3,000 per kg,â Goenka said. He added that the policy is focused on promoting small launch vehicles where private sector participation is growing.

Category C provides the highest level of support, offering 100% funding for repurposed upper-stage platforms carrying payloads of up to 120 kg.

The funding is capped at $13,000 per kg and limited to four missions. The category is aimed at NGEs, govt entities and launch vehicle providers.

Category D extends launch incentives to satellites weighing up to 100 kg launched aboard PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 missions. Beneficiaries will receive a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower.

Complementing the launch incentives is a separate Price Support Scheme for Indian entities, which will run for three years until Feb 2029.

The programme is intended to reduce the cost of accessing Indiaâs space infrastructure, technologies and data.

The scheme has three components. The first provides up to 50% support for the utilisation of DoS and In-SPACe facilities, along with technical expertise.

The second offers a 30% subsidy on Technology Transfer Fees (TTF) for technologies licensed from Isro, lowering the cost for companies seeking to commercialise govt-developed technologies.

The third provides a 50% subsidy on standard Earth Observation data and data products, making satellite imagery and geospatial datasets more affordable for Indian companies developing applications in agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, climate services and other downstream sectors.

World.title: For every Rs 100 India spends on R&D, govt gives Rs 48, pvt Rs 45
World.content:
BENGALURU: For every Rs 100 spent on R&D, the govt contributes about Rs 48 while private industry accounts for Rs 45, latest data from R&D Statistics At a Glance 2025-26 by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), shows.

The remaining Rs 7 comes from scientific and industrial research organisations (SIROs) and private higher education institutions.

Indiaâs Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) breached Rs 2.4-lakh crore in 2023-24, more than three times the Rs 79,356 crore recorded a decade ago. However, overall R&D spend is still under 1% of the GDP, touching 0.8%, as per the latest figures.

Private industryâs share in GERD increased from 39.7% in 2020-21 to 45.2% in 2023-24 in just three years.

During the same period, govt share declined from 54.5% to 48.2%, although it continues to remain the countryâs single largest contributor to research spending.

The report notes that private R&D expenditure has been growing at an average annual rate of around 20% over the last three years.

While the DST reportâs detailed analysis is up to 2023-24, it has projected overall trends for two more years: âThe upward [spending] trend is expected to continue, with GERD projected to reach nearly Rs 2.8-lakh-crore by 2024-25 and more than Rs 3.1-lakh-crore crore by 2025â26,â it reads.





Govt spending continues to be concentrated in strategic and public-interest sectors. Among the Centreâs scientific agencies, DRDO accounted for 32.7%, followed by the Department of Space (15%), Department of Atomic Energy (14.4%), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (13.1%) and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (8.7%). Together, 12 major scientific agencies accounted for 76% of govt R&D spend.

Transportation emerged as the biggest destination for industrial R&D, accounting for 32.6% of private sector expenditure, followed by pharmaceuticals (21.4%), biotechnology (8.6%), IT (7.9%) and electrical and electronics (5.9%).

The report also highlights the growing role of MNCs in Indiaâs research landscape. Their share in business R&D expenditure has increased from 49.9% in 2020-21 to 71.3% in 2023-24.

According to the report, the growth rate of R&D expenditure has outpaced GDP growth after 2021-22, except in 2022-23, reflecting the increasing priority accorded to research and innovation.

Despite the encouraging trends, India continues to trail many major economies in research intensity. At 0.8% of GDP, the country's R&D expenditure remains below that of China (2.6%), Brazil (1.2%) and several advanced economies that invest more than 2% of their GDP in research.

World.title: Big clean energy milestone: NPCIL cumulatively generates over 1,000 bn units of N-power, avoids 860 million tons of CO2 emissions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a milestone for Indiaâs clean energy production, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of nuclear electricity.

NPCIL said Tuesday, âSince commencement of commercial operation, NPCILâs nuclear power plants have cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of clean electricity, thereby avoiding over 860 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions into the environment.â

âThis milestone reflects NPCILâs steadfast commitment to deliver safe, reliable and sustainable nuclear power, strengthening Indiaâs energy security while supporting the nationâs clean energy transition and climate goals,â it said on X

To give the scale of how much carbon emission is avoided, a typical passenger vehicle emits about 4.6 metric tonnes of CO2 per year.

Avoiding 860 million tonnes is equal to taking roughly 187 million gasoline-powered cars going off the road for an entire year. At least 860 million tonnes is roughly equivalent to the total annual greenhouse gas emissions of a major industrial country like Germany or Japan for a full year.

Govt has drawn up a roadmap for reaching the 100 GW nuclear power capacity in the next two decades by 2047, as announced in the Nuclear Energy Mission in the Budget 2025-26, thereby increasing the share of reliable, low-carbon base-load nuclear energy in the countryâs energy mix and reaching the goal of net zero carbon emissions by 2070.





The present nuclear power capacity of 8.78 GW is expected to reach about 22 GW by 2031-32 on progressive completion of projects presently at various stages of implementation. Another 32 GW of nuclear power capacity is envisaged to be set up beyond 2032 by NPCIL under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE).

This will comprise indigenous pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and light water reactors (LWRs) planned to be set up by 2047, taking NPCILâs nuclear power capacity to 54 GW.

The balance of 46 GW comprising reactors of different technologies, is expected to be set up by other public sector enterprises, private sector and joint ventures in different business models. With the govt enacting the SHANTI Act (Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act, 2025) last year, the new law provides the legal framework that makes this 46 GW expansion possible.

World.title: MPs feel left out of foundation stone laying, parliamentary panel steps in
World.content:
A parliamentary panel has called attention to the frequent exclusion of MPs from events related to rural road schemes.

NEW DELHI: A parliamentary panel in its report among various concerns pertaining to the centrally-sponsored rural road scheme PMGSY has brought into focus that despite advisories from the rural development ministry, MPs are often not invited for foundation laying and inauguration ceremonies.This, the committee observed, âundermines established parliamentary protocolâ.To deal with the situation, Standing Committee on Rural Development and Panchayati Raj chaired by Congress MP Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka in its report tabled in Parliament Friday recommended that department of rural development (DoRD) âissue strict mandatory instructionsâ to state govts and authorities to invite the MP concerned or their representative at least 15 days in advance through multiple modes of communication like email, letter, and SMS.âHigh-quality photographs of the events, clearly depicting the MPâs participation along with the plaque, must be mandatorily uploaded on the Online Monitoring, Management and Accounting System (OMMAS) within seven days of the ceremony,â the panel has recommended.It suggested instituting a quarterly monitoring mechanism to track compliance, linking persistent violations to administrative accountability, and conducting regular sensitisation programmes for officials for effective implementation of the 2022 advisory and enforcement of these protocols.These findings are part of the action taken on the recommendations made the panel in its 17th report on âPradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)â (2024-25), in which it was highlighted that the committee has been frequently informed about the violation of norms/provisions of PMGSY pertaining to the protocol with regards to MPs.In the action taken reply, the ministry shared its advisory, dated Feb 2, 2022, with regard to invitation to the public representatives for foundation laying and inauguration ceremonies of PMGSY works. The committee has acknowledged the reply but called for measures to ensure compliance.

World.title: Terror suspects spotted, search ops launched in J&K’s Poonch
World.content:
Following intelligence indicating potential terror suspects in Poonch, security forces have launched coordinated operations in two strategic locations. Reports have confirmed sightings near Gujjar Naar and Kherowali dhok, prompting a thorough search in the isolated Dhara Sangla village by army and police units. As of Tuesday evening, no contact with the suspects has been reported. Earlier, a significant search initiative was executed in the Thanamandi area of Rajouri district.

JAMMU: Security forces on Tuesday initiated joint cordon-and-search operations in two locations in J&Kâs Poonch district after being alerted about the alleged movement of terror suspects.According to intelligence inputs, three terror suspects were seen near Gujjar Naar area, and four more were spotted close to Kherowali dhok (high-altitude temporary huts constructed by nomads) in the remote Dhara Sangla village in Surankote sector.Troops of the Armyâs 16 Rashtriya Rifles and J&K Policeâs Special Operations Group subsequently launched intensive searches. No contact was established with the terror suspects till Tuesday evening, even as both operations remained underway, officials said.Earlier on July 14, a massive combing operation was carried out across multiple villages in Rajouri districtâs Thanamandi after CCTV footage purportedly captured the movement of two terror suspects in the area.

World.title: Vaishno Devi fake silver row: Court seeks detailed probe report, orders evidence preservation
World.content:
JAMMU: Jammu Chief Judicial Magistrate Munish Kumar Manhas, while hearing the case of alleged Rs 550 crore fake silver offerings at Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Ji shrine last week, directed Deputy SP Bhawan, Katra, to submit a detailed inquiry report and ordered the preservation of evidence on the next date of hearing.

The CJMâs orders came on July 29 following a petition filed by advocate Deepak Sharma seeking urgent preservation of all physical, documentary, and electronic evidence linked to the controversy alleging adulteration, substitution, pilferage and suspected misappropriation of approximately 20 tonnes of silver offerings devotees had made to the shrine.

The petitioner also sought safeguarding of the remaining silver or purported silver articles, samples, remnants, and residues, along with stock and vault records, weighing and dispatch registers, assay and laboratory reports, govt mint records, transportation documents and the complete chain-of-custody record.

He sought protection of CCTV footage, electronic inventory data, official emails, server logs, access records, audit trails, accounting records, reconciliation statements and other digital evidence linked to the alleged scam.

On May 9, Sharma submitted a complaint to IGP (crime branch) Jammu and SSP (crime branch, EOW) Jammu. The crime branch received the complaint on May 11 and forwarded it to its HQ on May 20 for further action. Crime branch HQ approved its reference to Zonal Police HQ on June 9, following which it was sent to IGP (Jammu) on June 13.

The SSP said the case was currently in the inquiry stage, and no FIR had been registered yet.

The CJM posted the next hearing on Aug 18.

World.title: NC, PDP announce protest plans; BJP to celebrate Article 370 abrogation
World.content:
Kashmir's political landscape will witness separate protests from the NC and PDP this Wednesday, marking seven years since Article 370 was abrogated. The NC is pushing for the restoration of its statehood, whereas the PDP demands the reinstatement of Article 370. Meanwhile, BJP's celebratory events, including a Tiranga rally from Lal Chowk, suggest a contrasting narrative on the changes in Jammu and Kashmir's sentiments following the abrogation.

SRINAGAR: NC and PDP announced plans for separate protests on Wednesday on the seventh anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370 and bifurcation of erstwhile J&K into two Union territories. BJP said it would mark the day with celebratory events at its party headquarters and in districts.J&Kâs governing NC said it would hold peaceful protests to demand the restoration of statehood while PDP said its demonstrations would seek the restoration of Article 370 and the release of political prisoners.âOn this day, I would just say they (Centre) should fulfil their promise. They promised the people of J&K and the entire country that statehood would be restored after elections and delimitation. Both have been done,â NC chief Farooq Abdullah said.BJP spokesperson Sajid Yousuf Shah said the party would take out a Tiranga rally from Lal Chowk, adding the abrogation of Article 370 had changed the mood in J&K.

World.title: After opening golf tournament, CM Omar says authorities must not allow repeat of migrant worker killings
World.content: Omar Abdullah, the chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir, strongly condemned the recent violence against migrant laborers, emphasizing that such acts are unacceptable and calling for heightened security measures. He also underscored the significance of golf tournaments as a means to boost tourism in the area, recalling a time when these events were a hallmark of Kashmir's serene landscape, well before militancy took root.

World.title: Sense of insecurity emerges as key concern of elderly people during panel’s sitting in Kochi
World.content:
A sense of insecurity and lack of support system faced by the elderly population emerged as a predominant concern during a sitting held by the Kerala State Elderly Commission (KSEC) at the district collectorate here on Tuesday.

The complaints lodged by senior citizens with the Commission pertained to a variety of issues including alleged neglect of elderly parents by adult children, financial cheating, and trouble from neighbours, officials said.

The Commission received seven complaints during the sitting, five from individuals and two from organisations involved in issues of the elder community.

“A common complaint we receive is about the alleged neglect of parents by children after getting their properties transferred to the latter’s name. Today also there were a couple of such complaints. There were also complaints about troubles from neighbours, including an allegation that improper maintenance of pets in neighbourhood was causing health issues to the complainant,” KSEC Chairperson K. Somaprasad said.

He added that the complainants approached the Commission alleging inaction by the authorities they had approached earlier. One of the complaints was from a retired government employee who had accused a non-banking financial company based in Aluva of cheating him of ₹85 lakh by promising higher returns on investment. The complainant knocked on the Commission’s door alleging that the local police were not keen to investigate the complaint.

A similar complaint alleged that a lender was not returning a 1.25-acre property mortgaged by an elderly person despite repaying the private loan.

Mr. Somaprasad said the Commission would seek report from the departments or agencies concerned on the complaints and summon the parties involved for hearing accordingly. Though two complaints received earlier were scheduled to be heard on Tuesday, neither of the opposing parties in one case turned up. Only the complainant appeared before the panel in the second case.

The Commission is scheduled to conduct similar hearing in other districts in the coming days. It has received around 300 complaints from across the State in the past nine months and nearly 50 of them have been disposed of.

World.title: Are pellet guns legal for crowd control in India? | Explained
World.content:
Story so far: At least one of the 80 protesters injured in police action during the Monday (July 20, 2026) march to Parliament called by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) sustained pellet gun injuries, according to a source at Lady Hardinge Medical College, where the victim is undergoing treatment. While the Delhi Police has denied using pellet guns and said such claims are “false and misleading”, the allegations have been strong against the Rapid Action Force, a specialised rapid reaction wing of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). This prompts questions over the legal framework governing the use of pellet guns and non-lethal weapons for crowd control in India.

The use of ‘non-lethal’ pellet guns was widely criticised during the 2024 farmers’ protests. Though the police denied using pellet guns, farmer leaders had alleged that several people were injured. They were also used in Manipur in 2023 and in Kashmir since 2010.

World.title: New seahorse species identified by Kerala researchers
World.content:
Marine researchers claimed to have solved a 150-year-old taxonomic confusion regarding the identity of the thorny seahorse, Hippocampus histrix.

Scientific studies have identified a new species, Hippocampus amandavincentae, which was previously misidentified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.

Earlier, researchers had described Hippocampus jayakari, a lesser-known one, which was also previously wrongly identified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.

The new species, which was named after noted marine biologist Amanda Vincent, was collected from the fish bycatch at the Tuticorin fisheries harbour by Shalu Kannan, the lead author of the paper.

The species was described in a recently released research paper, according to the team of researchers from Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos).

This is also the fifth known seahorse species from the Kerala coast, they said.

The study published in the taxonomy journal Zootaxa demonstrated that the thorny seahorse (Hippocampus histrix), historically believed to be widespread from the Red Sea and East Africa across the Indian Ocean to the western Pacific, was three distinct species, they claimed.

“Many museum specimens and online biodiversity records of spiny seahorses in the Indian Ocean have been assigned to Hippocampus histrix for decades,“ said Rajeev Raghavan, Assistant Professor at Kufos and a senior author of the study.

The new species was photographed alive during a survey held as part of the Ecomarine project at around 15-metre depth on the rocky reefs off Anchuthengu, said Kufos Vice-Chancellor A. Biju Kumar.

World.title: Security beefed up as Congress, PDP, NC to observe August 5 as 'Black Day'
World.content:
Security has been intensified across the Jammu region, particularly along the Jammu-Srinagar and Jammu-Pathankot national highways, as the National Conference (NC), the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the Congress have announced separate protests to observe August 5 as ‘Black Day’.

August 5 marks the seventh anniversary of the Centre's decision to abrogate the special status of the erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir State under Article 370 and reorganise it into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.

Police, the Army and the CRPF have stepped up security arrangements by increasing vehicle checking, frisking and surveillance at sensitive locations across the region, officials said.

Special checkpoints have been placed on high alert along the Jammu-Srinagar and Jammu-Pathankot highways, with security personnel conducting searches of vehicles and verifying the identity of commuters, they said.

Security has also been strengthened in border areas, where patrolling and area domination exercises have been intensified as a precautionary measure, the officials said, adding that additional deployments have been made at vulnerable locations.

The National Conference leadership will assemble outside the party headquarters in Jammu and stage a protest on Wednesday, party leaders said.

The Congress will hold a demonstration outside its Shaheedi Chowk headquarters, demanding restoration of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir, along with constitutional safeguards for land, jobs and natural resources, party leaders said.

The PDP will also hold a protest at its Gandhi Nagar headquarters to mark the occasion, its leaders said.

World.title: Political discourse still fails women leaders
World.content:
Maharashtra politics came to a boil after the ruling Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) protested against the Opposition, mainly the Congress, for calling its national president Sunetra Pawar “Goongi Gudiya” or a “dumb doll”. Ms. Sunetra Pawar is also the Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra.

The irony isn’t lost here. The Congress is the same party which had once raised its voice against similar criticism about its leader and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

And yet, the party refused to apologise or withdraw its comment from its official X account. Instead, the party threw an open challenge at Ms. Sunetra Pawar, asking her to prove that she was not a “dumb doll”. It doled out a list of demands, which, if fulfilled, will prove that she is an avatar of ‘Durga’, the party said. Both the constructs are equally problematic, and reek of misogyny and patronising behaviour.

The incident

What was noteworthy was the presence of patronising behaviour from both the sides. While the Congress faced immediate backlash for its comments, the incident due to which this comment was made, showed Ms. Sunetra Pawar’s own party leader treating her in a patronising manner.

The incident in question was a press conference conducted by Ms. Sunetra Pawar in Beed in Marathwada. While answering questions about several issues, she kept referring to her late husband and former Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar, expressing how she was only trying to fulfil his dream and vision. She was flanked by NCP leader Dhananjay Munde, who not only stopped a journalist from asking a difficult question, but also ushered Ms. Sunetra Pawar out of the press event. Mr. Munde kept intervening when questions were being addressed to Ms. Pawar.

It was this video that the Congress tagged, asking Ms. Sunetra Pawar when she will stop being a “Goongi Gudiya”. NCP leader Udaykumar Aher said the comment was an insult to the entire Pawar family; he appealed to Ms. Pawar’s uncle-in-law Sharad Pawar, who heads the NCP-SP and sits in alliance with the Congress, to extract an apology from the party, or leave the INDIA bloc in protest.

Senior Congress leaders said the comment was ‘silly’ and should have been avoided. “Congress has a history and should have taken the responsibility of setting the discourse at a higher pedestal. While there is hardly any awareness about gender issues in our political narrative, it is Congress party’s responsibility to maintain dignity in dialogue,” senior Congress leader Prithviraj Chavan said.

But a few leaders said that it also reflected the overall deterioration of political discourse in the State. They claimed that outrage over derogatory comments had become selective and that leaders from the ruling dispensation had used worse words while hitting out at the Opposition. Officially, the Congress has, as of yet, refused to issue an apology or withdraw its comment.

Abysmal track record

This isn’t the first time misogynistic comments have been made in Maharashtra’s politics. Neither does the issue restrict itself to any particular political party. A few years ago, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) minister Chandrakant Patil had asked NCP MP Supriya Sule to “go home and cook,” when she had questioned the government about OBC reservations. Ahead of the 2024 Assembly elections, Shiv Sena-UBT (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) leader Arvind Sawant had referred to Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC as “imported maal”.

A 2020 study by Amnesty International India, ‘Troll Patrol India,’ had shown how female politicians face more abusive language. The report had analysed over 1,14,000 tweets sent to 95 female politicians and found that one in seven posts (or 13%) were ‘problematic’ or ‘abusive’.

“This amounted to an average of 113 abusive tweets per day for each woman politician,” it had reported.

The study said that Indian female leaders faced substantially higher levels of online harassment than their counterparts in the U.K. or the U.S.

Now, the NCP has asked Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra if they endorsed this culture in their party, questioning if the Congress will condemn these sexist remarks. In a society where political discourse across party lines rarely shows gender sensitivity, the behaviour of a national party calls for condemnation.

World.title: NCP asks Sharad Pawar to seek Congress apology or quit INDIA Bloc over ‘gungi gudiya’ remark
World.content:
A Congress social media post calling Nationalist Congress Party president and Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar a “gungi gudiya (dumb doll)” sparked a political row in Maharashtra on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).

The NCP demanded an immediate apology from the Congress, asking leaders Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra if they endorsed the sexist comments and whether the party would condemn them. The term ‘gungi gudiya’ had once been used to mock Indira Gandhi, in her early days as Prime Minister.

Maharashtra Cabinet Ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Narhari Zhirwal, both senior NCP leaders, lashed out at the Congress, while NCP party workers hit the streets and forcibly entered the Congress office in Colaba in Mumbai, shouting slogans against the party. The police had to intervene to disperse the protestors.

Ms. Pawar herself said little, telling reporters that she would “speak at the right time”.

The controversy erupted after the Congress posted a video on Monday night, of Ms. Pawar’s recent press conference in Beed, where a journalist’s question on the deteriorating law and order situation in the district was allegedly stopped midway. Ms. Pawar, the guardian minister of Beed, can be seen getting up to walk away from the press conference as the journalist is stopped by NCP leader Dhananjay Munde.

After the video of the press conference went viral, the Congress posted it on its social media handle and asked, “For how many days will Sunetra Pawar continue to remain a ‘gungi gudiya’ or a ‘dumb doll’?”

‘Prove you are Durga’

The State Congress defended the post, calling the NCP workers’ behaviour ‘thuggery’, and asking NCP leaders to quit politics if they cannot take criticism.

“Sunetra Pawar should prove that she is a ‘Durga’ by seeking the Finance department [portfolio] from the BJP, by allocating ₹2,100 instead of ₹1,500 in the Ladki Bahin Yojana, as was promised by her late husband Ajit Pawar,” said Maharashtra Congress president Harshawardhan Sapkal. “She should take the decision of farm loan waiver for the State’s farmers, she should scrap the decision to install smart meters. If she does that, our allegations will prove false. The State will then call her ‘Durga’,” he said, adding that Indira Gandhi had proved through her actions that she was not a ‘gungi gudiya’.

A family affair

The NCP also dragged Congress ally and NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar into the controversy. NCP Maharashtra vice-president Udaykumar Aher said the Congress had insulted not just Ms. Pawar, but the entire Pawar family. “Sharad Pawar saaheb should force the Congress to publicly apologise to Sunetra vahini. Otherwise he should exit the INDIA bloc,” he said. Mr. Sharad Pawar is the uncle of Ms. Sunetra Pawar’s late husband Ajit Pawar.

Expressing anguish at the party’s comments, Mr. Aher said: “The Congress party has not only insulted vahini, but the entire people of Baramati who elected her with a record-breaking majority in the Assembly elections, and by extension, the entire Pawar family including Sharad Pawar saaheb. Sunetra vahini has, time and again, strengthened her and her party’s position in politics with measured words and by maintaining silence at the right moments. The nation has witnessed her steadfast courage. Therefore, Congress should not worry about her.”

Ms. Pawar’s nephew and NCP SP MLA Rohit Pawar said that Dhananjay Munde should have been reprimanded during the press event in Beed. Mr. Munde has been unsuccessfully seeking to regain his ministerial berth in the Maharashtra Cabinet after losing it following the arrest of his close aide in the case relating to the murder of village sarpanch Santosh Deshmukh.

‘Politics must not demean women’

NCP leader Umesh Patil said that while political criticism is healthy in a democracy, it should not mean demeaning women. “Congress has indirectly admitted that the criticism of late Indira Gandhi was justified,” he said. “Democracy allows differences of opinion and even sharp criticism of policies. However, language that demeans women does not befit any political party,” he added, saying that the issue went beyond party politics and concerned the standards of political discourse relating to women in public life.

Another NCP leader Suraj Chavan called the Congress leadership “cheap” over its comment. “The Congress has a tradition of civilised political ideology. The current Congress has drifted away from its ideology and the people. A woman’s respect must be shown not just through speeches, but through thoughts. From the following post, the Congress’ mental state becomes evident,” he said.

World.title: AAP chief warns of major movement if Centre continues forcing E20 petrol
World.content:
Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) warned the Centre that the country will be pushed to launch another major movement if it doesn’t stop forcing the E20-blended petrol on its citizens.

The AAP chief also alleged that the Union Government was imposing E20 petrol on the country under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump and urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to “stand up” to the former.

“PM Modi, what is the point of showing your strength against us? Show the same courage in front of Trump and stop imposing E20 on the country. Otherwise, the nation will once again be compelled to launch a major movement,” Mr. Kejriwal said.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Kejriwal led a march of around 100 people towards the PM’s residence, but was stopped by security forces.

“We had gone today to submit 2.3 lakh petitions to the Prime Minister. A month ago, we had sought time to discuss the forceful imposition of the E20-blended petrol issue with him, but we received no response. Today, when we went to hand over the petitions, we were informed that he would not meet us. This reflects the dictatorial attitude,” Mr. Kejriwal said.

He accused Mr. Modi of demonstrating the same “dictatorship” attitude he had shown against the NEET protests.

Tense standoff

The march, which began from the AAP headquarters on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane, covered barely 1 km before being stopped near 5, Ferozshah Road.

The police had put up barricades at two locations, including the main blockade near 5, Ferozshah Road and another close to the Mandi House roundabout, preventing protesters from advancing towards the Prime Minister’s residence.

As protesters approached the barricades, police repeatedly announced over loudspeakers that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force and declared the march unlawful.

In a tense standoff that followed, the protesters continued to raise slogans while senior police officers held negotiations with AAP leaders. The police also denied a request to allow a small delegation to proceed to the PM’s residence to submit a representation against the E20 policy.

However, the impasse ended without any major confrontation after Delhi Police arranged for a police vehicle to carry the protesters’ memorandum to the Prime Minister’s residence.

The petition demanded to provide a choice between pure petrol and E20 at fuel stations, so that people are not forced to use fuel that “damages” vehicles. It also urged the government to reduce the price of E20 petrol to reflect the lower calorific value and reduced mileage it delivers.

The AAP chief also alleged that the Indian farmers are not benefitting from the shift to E20 petrol.

“Ethanol there (U.S.) is produced from maize, and American farmers have put tremendous pressure on Trump. Trump, in turn, put pressure on PM Modi to buy ethanol to protect American farmers. Our farmers are not benefitting at all. So, fundamentally, this entire exercise is being carried out solely under Trump’s pressure because our Prime Minister is a weak Prime Minister,” he said.

Senior AAP leader Manish Sisodia, who was also present at the march, said, “The issue of E20 is about forcing ethanol into the vehicles of 30 crore people across the country. Crores of people are saying that it is damaging their vehicles, reducing mileage, harming engines and increasing servicing costs. When the public is suffering such huge losses, why is PM Modi still adamant about it?”

(With inputs from Lavpreet Kaur)

World.title: Cape Town airport runway closed after plane's tyres fail, passengers safe
World.content:
The main runway at Cape ‌Town International Airport was temporarily closed ‌after a Kenya Airways ‌plane's ⁠tyres failed on ⁠landing, but all passengers were safely taken off the ​plane, South ‌Africa's airports operator said on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).
